log:
# Change log — Pharmacology & Therapeutics

## 2026-06-29

Built the knowledge base from the 52 source papers in
`benchmark_corpus/05_pharmacology_therapeutics/papers/` (PubMed full texts). All 52 were converted
into immutable `raw/` sources with `bokf convert`, then curated into typed BioOKF v0.5 concept
documents. Final bundle: **353 nodes, 1,373 edges, 0 parse errors**; the `bokf verify` accountability
gate passes (`ok: true`, 0 errors).

Curation was organised into 14 drug/therapy clusters so each recurring entity (drug, molecular
target, gene→protein, disease) is a single shared node accumulating edges across all the papers that
discuss it. Every claim edge carries the provenance triplet (`knowledge_level`, `agent_type`,
`primary_source` = the ingested paper's own source node) plus a `reported_in` back-link, and reported
statistics (hazard/odds/risk ratios, CIs, p-values, MIC/MIC90, IC50/Kd, Cmax/AUC, % reductions,
response/remission rates, sample sizes, doses) are placed on the edges, not in prose.

### Clusters ingested (sources → pages)

- **Gepotidacin** (antibiotic, bacterial topoisomerase inhibitor) — 9 papers (PMID 28483959,
  29358297, 30249694, 36255258, 36271314, 36411033, 36883591, 38342126, 39004438) → 37 pages.
  EAGLE-2/EAGLE-3 minted as Study nodes; targets GyrA/DNA gyrase & ParC/topoisomerase IV; resistance
  variants; organisms (N. gonorrhoeae, S. aureus, E. coli); uUTI & urogenital gonorrhoea.
- **Nipocalimab** (anti-FcRn mAb) — 5 papers (33717213, 38362023, 39073504, 39115062, 39197469) →
  28 pages. FcRn/FCGRT, IgG, IVIg; HDFN (UNITY), myasthenia gravis, wAIHA, Sjögren's.
- **Imlunestrant** (oral SERD) — 5 papers (39241211, 39377773, 39442371, 39652577, 39660834) →
  23 pages. ESR1→ERα, ESR1 Y537S/D538G, abemaciclib/CDK4/6; EMBER, EMBER-2, EMBER-3.
- **Axatilimab** (anti-CSF1R mAb) — 4 papers (36459673, 39292927, 39704205, 39551906) → 21 pages.
  CSF1R, CSF1/IL-34, macrophages/monocytes; chronic GVHD; AGAVE-201; first approval.
- **Zenocutuzumab** (HER2×HER3 bispecific) — 2 papers (35135829, 38348690) → 15 pages. NRG1 fusion;
  HER2/HER3; eNRGy trial; NRG1-fusion NSCLC & pancreatic cancer.
- **Hereditary angioedema / kallikrein** — 4 papers (38294975, 39445704, 38142864, 38366937) →
  24 pages. NTLA-2002 (CRISPR-Cas9 KLKB1 editing), plasma kallikrein, C1-INH/SERPING1; the
  kallikrein–kinin pathway; lanadelumab/berotralstat/ecallantide/sebetralstat/donidalorsen.
- **Hemophilia B gene therapy** — 3 papers (38863155, 39321362, 38472707) → 15 pages. Fidanacogene
  elaparvovec (AAVRh74var), F9→Factor IX, FIX-R338L (Padua); BENEGENE-2; first approval.
- **TAS-102 / trifluridine–tipiracil** — 2 papers (28111727, 26557901) → 17 pages. Components +
  thymidine phosphorylase (TYMP) & thymidylate synthase (TYMS); metastatic colorectal cancer;
  RECOURSE.
- **Erdosteine** (mucoactive) — 2 papers (18035199, 38719503) → 16 pages. Bronchiectasis/COPD;
  chest physiotherapy; BETTER trial.
- **Vestibular migraine / anti-CGRP** — 2 papers (39344988, 36946234) → 21 pages.
  Galcanezumab/erenumab/fremanezumab, CGRP & CGRP receptor; INVESTMENT study.
- **Inebilizumab** (anti-CD19 mAb) — 2 papers (32729016, 39541094) → 14 pages. CD19, B cells/
  plasmablasts; NMOSD & IgG4-related disease; MITIGATE; first approval.
- **Infigratinib** (FGFR1–3 TKI) — 2 papers (35342457, 39555818) → 16 pages. FGFR3 & FGFR3 G380R;
  achondroplasia; PROPEL / PROPEL 2.
- **Oncology / CNS singletons** — 4 papers → 48 pages: zotiraciclib in glioblastoma (EORTC 1608
  STEAM, 38159337); glioma treatment review (38689623); luvadaxistat in Friedreich ataxia
  (34018342); CIDP therapy review (38435981).
- **Gene-editing / RNAi / IBD / platform / antibiotic singletons** — 6 papers → ~50 pages:
  nexiguran ziclumeran for ATTR cardiomyopathy (39555828); xalnesiran for chronic HBV (Piranga,
  39774313); tulisokibart (anti-TL1A) in ulcerative colitis (ARTEMIS-UC, 39321363); zodasiran
  (ANGPTL3 RNAi) for mixed hyperlipidemia (ARCHES-2, 38809174); StarGazer drug-target-prioritization
  platform (35711912); enmetazobactam first approval (38761353).

### Post-curation reconciliation

- Created 5 shared target nodes to resolve cross-cluster references: `Liver`, `Placenta` (Anatomy),
  `Blood coagulation`, `Iron-sulfur cluster assembly` (BiologicalPathway), `NMDA receptor`
  (Molecule). All dangling edge objects now resolve.
- Fixed 4 domain/range issues: the three NRG1-fusion cancers now use `associated_with` (not
  `has_phenotype`) to the `NRG1 gene fusion` variant; erdosteine→`Pulmonary exacerbation rate` is now
  `associated_with` (direction: decreased) rather than `prevents` a measure.
- Backfilled agent-coined `subtype` on measure/disease/class/phenotype/variant nodes that lacked one.
- Regenerated `index.md` (identifier registry + by-type catalog).

### Notes / deliberate choices

- Some drug→disease relationships carry multiple `treats` edges from the same trial source (e.g.
  inebilizumab→NMOSD: overall ITT HR 0.272 vs AQP4-IgG⁺ subgroup HR 0.227; several oncology drugs:
  one edge per OS/PFS/response endpoint). These are retained as distinct atomic, number-bearing
  claims (BioOKF "numbers are first-class") rather than collapsed; `bokf lint` reports them as
  soft `edge.duplicate` warnings.
- Several `used_to_study` edges target an Organism (N. gonorrhoeae), a Population (Japanese
  volunteers) or a Concept (drug-target-prioritization), which lint flags as soft range preferences;
  these are kept as the faithful reading of the source.

6-minute walk test distance.body:
# 6-minute walk test distance

The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance measures walking capacity and exercise tolerance. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) of [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md), 6MWT distance improved significantly from baseline in both arms (erdosteine group +67.3 m, p=0.001; physiotherapy-alone group +68.3 m, p=0.001), with no significant between-group difference, reflecting the systemic benefit of pulmonary rehabilitation.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
6-minute walk test distance.description: The distance walked in 6 minutes during a standardised six-minute walking test; a measure of exercise tolerance and walking capacity in chronic lung disease.

edges.note: used to assess exercise tolerance/walking capacity in elderly patients with bronchiectasis

AAVRh74var vector.body:
# AAVRh74var vector

The AAVRh74var vector is a single-stranded, non-replicating, recombinant adeno-associated virus (AAV) serotype Rh74var gene-delivery vehicle with a bioengineered AAVRh74var capsid. It forms the delivery component of [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md), carrying a liver-specific (ApoE/hAAT) expression cassette that encodes the high-activity [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) transgene. Pre-existing neutralizing antibodies to AAVRh74var are an exclusion criterion (they made 59.5% of screened men ineligible in [BENEGENE-2](../study/benegene-2-trial.md)), and all treated patients develop sustained neutralizing anti-AAVRh74var antibodies after infusion.

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
AAVRh74var vector.description: Single-stranded, non-replicating, recombinant adeno-associated virus (AAV) serotype Rh74var gene-delivery vector with a bioengineered AAVRh74var capsid, used in fidanacogene elaparvovec to carry a liver-specific (ApoE/hAAT) expression cassette encoding the high-activity factor IX variant R338L.

edges.note: fidanacogene elaparvovec is a single-stranded, non-replicating recombinant AAV serotype Rh74var vector comprising a bioengineered AAVRh74var capsid and an ApoE/hAAT-driven codon-optimized FIX-R338L expression cassette

pre-existing anti-AAV neutralizing antibodies made 188/316 (59.5%) of screened men ineligible; eligibility requires being negative for neutralizing antibodies to AAVRh74var; all treated participants developed sustained neutralizing anti-AAVRh74var antibodies after infusion

AGAVE-201 trial.body:
# AGAVE-201 trial

AGAVE-201 (NCT04710576; SNDX-6352-0504) was a phase 2, multinational, pivotal, randomized study funded by Syndax Pharmaceuticals and Incyte that evaluated [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) at three doses (0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 3 mg/kg every 4 weeks) in 241 patients with recurrent or refractory [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md) who had received at least two prior lines of systemic therapy. Enrolled across 121 sites in 16 countries, the study met its primary endpoint in all three dose groups, with overall response in the first six cycles of 74%, 67%, and 50% respectively. The 0.3-mg dose every 2 weeks showed the highest response rate and least toxicity.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
AGAVE-201 trial.description: Phase 2, multinational, pivotal, randomized study (NCT04710576) evaluating axatilimab at three doses in patients aged >=2 years with recurrent or refractory chronic graft-versus-host disease after at least two prior lines of systemic therapy.

edges.note: primary endpoint - overall response (complete or partial) within the first six cycles; met if lower bound of 95% CI exceeded 30%

ORR in first six cycles by dose arm - 0.3 mg/kg Q2W 74% (59/80, 95% CI 63-83); 1 mg/kg Q2W 67% (54/81, 95% CI 55-77); 3 mg/kg Q4W 50% (40/80, 95% CI 39-61); primary endpoint met in all groups (lower bound of 95% CI exceeded 30%); 241 patients randomized

ANGPTL3 (gene).body:
# ANGPTL3 (gene)

ANGPTL3 is the human gene encoding [angiopoietin-like 3](../molecule/angiopoietin-like-3-protein.md), a hepatically expressed regulator of lipid and lipoprotein metabolism. ANGPTL3 loss-of-function carriers have lower levels of triglycerides, LDL, HDL, and non-HDL cholesterol and an approximately 40% lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease than noncarriers, with no known adverse phenotypes. Because ANGPTL3 is [hepatically](../celltype/hepatocyte.md) expressed, its mRNA is a target for gene-silencing therapy: [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) is an siRNA that degrades ANGPTL3 mRNA to treat [mixed hyperlipidemia](../disease/mixed-hyperlipidemia.md).

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
ANGPTL3 (gene).description: The human gene encoding angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a hepatically expressed regulator of lipid and lipoprotein metabolism; loss-of-function variants lower triglycerides, LDL, HDL, and non-HDL cholesterol and reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk, making its mRNA a target for gene-silencing therapies.

edges.note: ANGPTL3 encodes the angiopoietin-like 3 protein, expressed hepatically
ANGPTL3 is hepatically expressed, making its mRNA an appropriate target for hepatically-directed gene-silencing therapy
ANGPTL3 loss-of-function carriers have lower triglycerides, LDL, HDL, and non-HDL cholesterol and ~40% lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease than noncarriers

ARCHES-2 trial.body:
# ARCHES-2 trial

ARCHES-2 (NCT04832971) was a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial evaluating [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md), an RNAi therapy targeting [ANGPTL3](../gene/angptl3-gene.md), in 204 adults with [mixed hyperlipidemia](../disease/mixed-hyperlipidemia.md) (fasting triglycerides 150-499 mg/dL with elevated LDL or non-HDL cholesterol). Patients were randomized 3:1 to subcutaneous zodasiran 50, 100, or 200 mg or placebo on day 1 and at week 12, and followed through week 36. The primary end point, percent change in fasting [triglycerides](../biomedicalmeasure/triglyceride-level.md) at week 24, showed dose-dependent reductions of -51, -57, and -63 percentage points versus placebo (P<0.001 for all), with commensurate reductions in ANGPTL3, remnant cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B.

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
ARCHES-2 trial.description: A phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial (NCT04832971) evaluating subcutaneous zodasiran (50, 100, or 200 mg) versus placebo on day 1 and week 12 in 204 adults with mixed hyperlipidemia; primary end point was percent change in fasting triglycerides from baseline to week 24.

edges.note: 204 adults randomized 3:1 to zodasiran 50/100/200 mg or placebo; mean age 61; 96% on statins; 42% with type 2 diabetes; mean baseline triglycerides 246 mg/dL
primary end point - percent change in fasting plasma triglycerides from baseline to week 24
difference in triglyceride change vs placebo at week 24: -51 (50 mg), -57 (100 mg), -63 (200 mg) percentage points (P<0.001 all)

ARTEMIS-UC trial.body:
# ARTEMIS-UC trial

ARTEMIS-UC (NCT04996797) was a phase 2, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 14 countries evaluating intravenous [tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md), an [anti-TL1A monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-tl1a-monoclonal-antibodies.md), for induction of [clinical remission](../biomedicalmeasure/clinical-remission.md) in adults with moderately to severely active [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md). Patients received tulisokibart 1000 mg on day 1 then 500 mg at weeks 2, 6, and 10, or placebo. Cohort 1 enrolled patients regardless of a genetic-based diagnostic test for likelihood of response; cohort 2 enrolled only test-positive patients. The primary end point, clinical remission at week 12 in cohort 1, was 26% with tulisokibart versus 1% with placebo (difference 25 percentage points, 95% CI 14 to 37, P<0.001), with significant benefit across all ranked secondary end points.

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)

AZALEA study.body:
# AZALEA study

AZALEA (NCT05912517) is a phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial — the first such prospective trial in severe [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md). Approximately 120 alloimmunized pregnant participants at risk for severe HDFN are randomized 2:1 to weekly IV [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) 45 mg/kg or placebo from 13-16 to 35 weeks gestation, with delivery planned at 37-38 weeks. The primary endpoint is the proportion of pregnancies that do not result in fetal loss, intrauterine transfusion, hydrops fetalis, or neonatal death. The 45 mg/kg weekly regimen was selected from PK/receptor-occupancy/PD modeling to maintain full [FcRn receptor occupancy](../biomedicalmeasure/fcrn-receptor-occupancy.md) in at least 96% of participants for at least 8 days. Nipocalimab holds FDA fast-track, breakthrough therapy and orphan drug designations and EMA orphan medicinal product designation for HDFN.

## Citations
- [Design of a Phase 3, Global, Multicenter, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Study of Nipocalimab in Pregnancies at Risk for Severe HDFN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39197469/) (PMID:39197469)
AZALEA study.description: Design paper for AZALEA, a phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized (2:1), placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of weekly IV nipocalimab 45 mg/kg from 13-16 to 35 weeks gestation in approximately 120 alloimmunized pregnant individuals at risk for severe hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

Abemaciclib.body:
# Abemaciclib

Abemaciclib is a potent oral [CDK4/6 inhibitor](../molecularclass/cdk4-6-inhibitors.md) administered on a continuous schedule, used in combination with [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) throughout the EMBER program. In the phase Ia/Ib [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md), imlunestrant + abemaciclib achieved a median PFS of 19.2 months in CDK4/6i-naive [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md), and in the phase 3 [EMBER-3 trial](../study/ember-3-trial.md) the combination significantly improved PFS over imlunestrant alone (HR 0.57). It was also active combined with imlunestrant in [ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer](../disease/er-positive-endometrioid-endometrial-cancer.md). Preclinically, imlunestrant + abemaciclib showed synergistic antiproliferative activity and enhanced tumor regression.

Achondroplasia.body:
# Achondroplasia

Achondroplasia (ACH) is the most common heritable short-limbed skeletal dysplasia, affecting an estimated 1 in 15,000 to 1 in 30,000 live births (global prevalence ~250,000). It is caused by gain-of-function pathogenic variants in [FGFR3](../gene/fgfr3-gene.md) — most commonly the [G380R](../variant/fgfr3-g380r.md) substitution — which impair [endochondral ossification](../biologicalpathway/endochondral-ossification.md) by inhibiting [chondrocyte](../celltype/chondrocyte.md) proliferation and differentiation.

Characteristic features include disproportionate short stature, smaller-than-average chest, macrocephaly with frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, abnormal spinal curvature, hypermobile joints, leg bowing, and shortened fingers and toes. Complications range from delayed motor development and recurrent otitis media to foramen magnum stenosis (with risk of sleep apnea and sudden death) and lumbosacral spinal stenosis. The only previously approved disease-modifying drug is vosoritide; [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md), evaluated in the [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md), is the first oral agent targeting the underlying FGFR3 driver.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Achondroplasia.description: The most common heritable short-limbed skeletal dysplasia, caused by gain-of-function pathogenic variants in FGFR3 that impair endochondral ossification; characterized by disproportionate short stature, macrocephaly with frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and limb shortening, affecting an estimated 1 in 15,000-30,000 live births.

edges.note: disproportionate short stature with limb shortening greater than truncal shortening; upper-to-lower body segment ratio ~2.0 from age 4 vs ~1.0 in average stature; reduced annualized growth velocity (4-5 cm/year in childhood vs 5-7 cm/year average)

Advanced solid tumors.body:
# Advanced solid tumors

Advanced solid tumors are histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced malignancies for which no standard therapy exists. This was the enrolled population of the phase 1 pharmacokinetic study of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) ([Belani 2017](../study/belani-2017-trifluridine-tipiracil-pk-study.md)), in which heavily pretreated patients (the majority with colon cancer) received the drug; disease control was observed in 52% of patients, with no objective responses.

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of trifluridine and tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)
Advanced solid tumors.description: Histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced malignant solid tumours for which no standard therapy exists; the enrolled population of the phase 1 pharmacokinetic study of trifluridine/tipiracil.

Alanine aminotransferase increased.body:
# Alanine aminotransferase increased

Increased serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is a marker of hepatocellular injury. In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md) of [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md), elevated ALT was the most common adverse event across the [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) groups (43-83%, most frequent with [peginterferon alfa-2a](../molecule/peginterferon-alfa-2a.md)) and the most frequent grade 3 or 4 event (13% in group 4). All elevations were asymptomatic, preserved liver synthetic and excretory function, and resolved without sequelae; one grade 4 ALT elevation (23x ULN) occurred during a clinical relapse after NA discontinuation and resolved after NA restart.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Alanine aminotransferase increased.description: An elevation in serum alanine aminotransferase, a marker of hepatocellular injury; in chronic hepatitis B antiviral therapy, ALT elevations (flares) can be asymptomatic and accompany HBsAg decline or nucleoside/nucleotide analogue discontinuation.

Albumin.body:
# Albumin

Serum albumin is the most abundant plasma protein and, like [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md), is salvaged from lysosomal degradation by the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md). FcRn blockade by [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) produces mild, transient, asymptomatic decreases in serum albumin (nadir ~Day 8-15, within ~10% for 30 mg/kg and ~15% for 60 mg/kg, recovering toward baseline by Day 29), an expected on-target pharmacodynamic effect.

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across infusion rates of intravenously administered nipocalimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38362023/) (PMID:38362023)
Albumin.description: The most abundant plasma protein, recycled by FcRn alongside IgG; mild, transient, asymptomatic reductions in serum albumin are an expected, on-target pharmacodynamic effect of FcRn blockade by nipocalimab.

edges.note: albumin is recycled by FcRn at a site distinct from the IgG-binding site; FcRn blockade modestly lowers serum albumin

Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell trans.body:
# Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation

Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) is a curative therapy for a range of hematologic disorders. [Chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md) is its most common late complication, affecting approximately half of recipients and serving as the clinical context for axatilimab development. All patients in the axatilimab cGVHD studies had undergone allo-HSCT.

## Citations

Angioedema attack.body:
# Angioedema attack

An angioedema attack is a recurrent, unpredictable episode of nonurticarial swelling affecting the skin, gastrointestinal tract, face, and/or upper airway, and is the hallmark clinical manifestation of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). Attacks result from excessive [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md)-driven vascular permeability, may occur as often as every few days, and can last from a few hours to several days; laryngeal attacks can be life-threatening through airway obstruction. The [angioedema attack rate](../biomedicalmeasure/angioedema-attack-rate.md) (attacks per month) is the principal efficacy endpoint for prophylactic therapies such as [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Angioedema attack.description: A recurrent, unpredictable episode of nonurticarial swelling of the skin, gastrointestinal tract, and/or upper airway in hereditary angioedema; laryngeal attacks can be life-threatening through airway obstruction.

edges.note: hallmark clinical manifestation of HAE; attacks may occur every few days and last hours to several days

Angioedema attack rate.body:
# Angioedema attack rate

The angioedema attack rate is the number of investigator-confirmed [angioedema attacks](../phenotype/angioedema-attack.md) per month (with a month defined as 28 days), recorded by patients in an electronic diary and adjudicated by investigators. It is the principal efficacy endpoint for prophylactic [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md) therapies and was the primary endpoint (week 1 through week 16) in the [NTLA-2002 phase 2 trial](../study/ntla-2002-phase-2-trial.md). Reductions in attack rate are the key clinical efficacy readout reported for [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md) and other kallikrein-directed agents.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
Angioedema attack rate.description: The number of investigator-confirmed angioedema attacks per month (a month defined as 28 days), the principal efficacy endpoint for prophylactic hereditary angioedema therapies.

Angiopoietin-like 3 (protein).body:
# Angiopoietin-like 3 (protein)

Angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), encoded by [ANGPTL3](../gene/angptl3-gene.md), is a hepatically secreted protein that regulates lipid and lipoprotein metabolism through reversible inhibition of lipoprotein lipase, endothelial lipase, and LDL-receptor-independent hepatic lipoprotein uptake. Loss-of-function lowers most plasma lipoproteins, including triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and LDL. [Zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) lowers circulating ANGPTL3 by degrading its mRNA, reducing [triglycerides](../biomedicalmeasure/triglyceride-level.md) and atherogenic lipoproteins in [mixed hyperlipidemia](../disease/mixed-hyperlipidemia.md) (ANGPTL3 reduction strongly correlated with triglyceride reduction, r=0.69).

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
Angiopoietin-like 3 (protein).description: A hepatically secreted protein that regulates lipid and lipoprotein metabolism by reversibly inhibiting lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase and LDL-receptor-independent hepatic lipoprotein uptake; inhibiting it lowers triglycerides and atherogenic lipoproteins.

edges.note: ANGPTL3 inhibits lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase, raising triglycerides and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins; its inhibition lowers them
ANGPTL3 regulates metabolism of triglycerides and non-HDL cholesterol; loss-of-function lowers plasma lipoproteins

Annualized bleeding rate.body:
# Annualized bleeding rate

The annualized bleeding rate (ABR) is the number of bleeding episodes per year and the primary efficacy endpoint for [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md) trials, reported for total (treated and untreated) and for treated bleeding episodes. In the [BENEGENE-2 trial](../study/benegene-2-trial.md), a single infusion of [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) reduced the total ABR from 4.42 to 1.28 (a 71% reduction; treatment difference -3.15, P=0.008) and the treated-bleed ABR from 3.34 to 0.73 (a 78% reduction; treatment difference -2.61, P=0.002) versus prophylaxis.

## Citations
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Annualized bleeding rate.description: Number of bleeding episodes per year, used as the primary efficacy endpoint in hemophilia trials; computed for total (treated and untreated) and treated bleeding episodes, with procedural bleeds typically excluded.

Annualized flare rate.body:
# Annualized flare rate

The annualized flare rate (or annualized attack rate) is the number of treated, adjudicated disease flares per patient-year. It served as a key secondary efficacy endpoint in the [MITIGATE trial](../study/mitigate-trial.md), where [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) reduced the annualized rate of [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md) flares by 86% (0.10 vs 0.71; rate ratio 0.14, 95% CI 0.06-0.31). The analogous annualized attack rate in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder was 0.113 after 1 year of open-label inebilizumab in N-MOmentum.

## Citations

- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)

Annualized height velocity.body:
# Annualized height velocity

Annualized height velocity (AHV) is the rate of linear (standing-height) growth in centimeters per year, derived from serial standing-height measurements. It is the primary efficacy endpoint in the [PROPEL study](../study/propel-study.md) (where baseline AHV is established from at least 6 months of observation) and the [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md) (where the change from that baseline measures the effect of [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) in [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md)).

In untreated achondroplasia, childhood AHV is reduced (about 4-5 cm/year versus 5-7 cm/year for average stature). In PROPEL 2, infigratinib at 0.25 mg/kg/day (cohort 5) produced a mean change from baseline of +2.50 cm/year at 18 months (95% CI 1.22-3.79; P=0.001).

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Annualized height velocity.description: The rate of linear (standing-height) growth expressed in centimeters per year, derived from serial standing-height measurements; the primary efficacy endpoint in the PROPEL/PROPEL 2 achondroplasia studies of infigratinib.

Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies.body:
# Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies

Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies are a class of B-cell-depleting therapies that bind the B-cell surface antigen [CD19](../molecule/b-lymphocyte-antigen-cd19-protein.md), depleting CD19-expressing [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md). Because CD19 is expressed earlier than CD20 and persists on [plasmablasts](../celltype/plasmablast.md) and some plasma cells, this class targets a broader range of B-lineage cells than anti-CD20 antibodies such as rituximab. [Inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) is the prototypical member.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies.description: A class of B-cell-depleting therapeutic monoclonal antibodies directed against the B-cell surface antigen CD19, depleting CD19-expressing B cells including pre-B, mature B, plasmablasts and some plasma cells.

Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies.body:
# Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies

Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies are a class of drugs that block CGRP signaling either by binding the [CGRP receptor](../molecule/cgrp-receptor-protein.md) — as [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md) does — or by neutralizing the [CGRP ligand](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md) — as [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md) do. They are established, safe preventives for episodic and chronic [migraine](../disease/migraine.md).

Because CGRP is expressed in the vestibular system, the class has been investigated for [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md). In the prospective [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md), 78% of patients achieved a concomitant >=50% reduction in vertigo days, headache days, and MIDAS, and the placebo-controlled [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md) provided the first randomized evidence of efficacy in vestibular migraine.

## Citations
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies.description: A class of monoclonal antibodies that block CGRP signaling, either by binding the CGRP receptor (erenumab) or by neutralizing the CGRP ligand (galcanezumab, fremanezumab); approved for migraine prevention and investigated for vestibular migraine.

edges.note: in the Russo 2023 cohort 39/50 (78%) achieved concomitant >=50% reduction in vertigo days, headache days, and MIDAS; individually 90% (45/50) for vertigo, 86% (43/50) for headache, 80% (40/50) for MIDAS at 12 months

Anti-CSF-1R monoclonal antibodies.body:
# Anti-CSF-1R monoclonal antibodies

Anti-CSF-1R monoclonal antibodies are a class of antibodies that bind [colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF-1R)](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md) and block ligand-mediated signaling, suppressing the monocyte- and macrophage-dependent pathways that drive inflammation and fibrosis. [Axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), a humanized IgG4 (kappa light chain) member of this class, was the first such antibody approved for [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md).

Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies.body:
# Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies

Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies (FcRn inhibitors/blockers) are engineered antibodies or Fc fragments that bind the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) with high affinity at neutral and acidic pH, blocking [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) recycling and thereby selectively and reversibly lowering serum IgG (including pathogenic autoantibodies) by up to ~85% without affecting IgG production, other immunoglobulins, or broad immune function. Members include [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md), efgartigimod (a humanized IgG1 Fc fragment) and rozanolixizumab (a humanized anti-FcRn IgG4 antibody), with leading development in [generalized myasthenia gravis](../disease/generalized-myasthenia-gravis.md) and other antibody-mediated diseases.

## Citations
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies.description: A class of engineered antibodies or Fc fragments that bind the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) with high affinity at neutral and acidic pH, blocking IgG recycling to selectively and reversibly lower serum IgG (including pathogenic autoantibodies) without broad immunosuppression.

edges.note: bind FcRn with high affinity at low and neutral pH, enhancing catabolism of all IgG subclasses
class-level selective serum IgG reduction up to 85% from baseline, dose-dependent and reversible (returns to near baseline 50-57 days after single dose); IgG3 most affected
emerging class for CIDP; efgartigimod (ADHERE) significantly reduced relapse risk (HR 0.39) while rozanolixizumab appeared negative; nipocalimab and batoclimab are under study

Anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies.body:
# Anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies

Anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies bind [tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A](../molecule/tumor-necrosis-factor-like-cytokine-1a-protein.md) (TL1A) and block its interaction with the receptor [DR3](../molecule/death-domain-receptor-3-protein.md), suppressing type 1 and type 17 helper T-cell responses and profibrotic pathways implicated in [inflammatory bowel disease](../disease/inflammatory-bowel-disease.md). [Tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md), a humanized IgG1 kappa antibody, is the member evaluated in the [ARTEMIS-UC trial](../study/artemis-uc-trial.md), where TL1A blockade was established as a new mechanism of action for [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md).

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)
Anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies.description: A class of monoclonal antibodies that bind tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A (TL1A) and block its interaction with the receptor DR3, suppressing pro-inflammatory and profibrotic pathways for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.

edges.note: TL1A blockade is a new mechanism of action for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, demonstrated by tulisokibart in ARTEMIS-UC

Antimetabolites.body:
# Antimetabolites

Antimetabolites are cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents that structurally mimic natural metabolites — particularly nucleosides and nucleotides — and thereby interfere with DNA/RNA synthesis. The class includes the fluoropyrimidines (e.g. 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine) and nucleoside analogues such as [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md), the active component of the combination antimetabolite [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102). Antimetabolites characteristically have short plasma half-lives.

Arthropathy.body:
# Arthropathy

Arthropathy here refers to drug-induced injury to weight-bearing articular cartilage (most commonly the distal femur and proximal tibia) characteristic of fluoroquinolone toxicity in juvenile animals, which has restricted fluoroquinolone use in children. A juvenile-rat study found that [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) — which lacks the fluorine atom and magnesium-chelating beta-keto acid structure of fluoroquinolones — did not induce macroscopic or microscopic arthropathy of the femoral head or stifle joint at the highest tolerated dose (300/1250 mg/kg/day), supporting potential pediatric use.

## Citations
- [Novel Bacterial Topoisomerase Inhibitor Gepotidacin Demonstrates Absence of Fluoroquinolone-Like Arthropathy in Juvenile Rats](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36255258/) (PMID:36255258)
Arthropathy.description: Drug-induced injury to weight-bearing articular cartilage (e.g. distal femur, proximal tibia) characteristic of fluoroquinolone toxicity in juvenile animals; gepotidacin did not induce arthropathy in juvenile rats.

Aspartate aminotransferase increased.body:
# Aspartate aminotransferase increased

Increased serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) is among the most common adverse events with [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), reflecting reduced clearance of circulating enzymes following depletion of Kupffer cells ([liver macrophages](../celltype/macrophage.md)) — an on-target effect of CSF-1R inhibition. It is transient, dose-dependent (14%, 38%, 54% across the 0.3-, 1-, and 3-mg AGAVE-201 dose groups), and not accompanied by end-organ damage. AST was modeled as a safety PD biomarker dependent on nonclassical monocyte count in the population PK/PD analysis.

Autologous hematopoietic stem cell trans.body:
# Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT) is an intensive immunosuppressive procedure that uses the patient's own stem cells to reset the immune system. In refractory [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md), a 66-patient prospective study reported 80% treatment-free remission at 6 months (stable to 5 years) with no treatment-related deaths, and a meta-analysis of 89 cases found an 86% response rate and 85% remission rate, albeit with early neutropenic sepsis in >30%. Benefit appears greatest in younger patients.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)

Axatilimab.body:
# Axatilimab

Axatilimab (SNDX-6352; NIKTIMVO; axatilimab-csfr) is a high-affinity (KD 4-8 pM) humanized IgG4 (kappa light chain) [monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-csf-1r-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that recognizes the ligand-binding domain on [colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF-1R)](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md). It blocks binding of both [CSF-1](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-protein.md) and [interleukin-34](../molecule/interleukin-34-protein.md) ligands, potently inhibiting ligand-induced monocyte activation (IC50 0.1-0.455 nM) without antibody-mediated receptor internalization or activation, thereby restraining the development of profibrotic [monocytes](../celltype/nonclassical-monocyte.md) and [macrophages](../celltype/macrophage.md).

Developed by Incyte and Syndax, axatilimab received its first US approval on 14 August 2024 for [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy. In the pivotal phase 2 [AGAVE-201 trial](../study/agave-201-trial.md), overall response in the first six cycles reached 74%, 67%, and 50% at the 0.3-, 1-, and 3-mg dose levels respectively, with the 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks regimen the approved dose. Its characteristic adverse effects (periorbital edema, transient AST/CPK/LDH/lipase elevations) are dose-dependent on-target consequences of CSF-1R blockade and Kupffer cell depletion.

Axatilimab First Approval (Keam 2024).body:
# Axatilimab First Approval (Keam 2024)

This AdisInsight First Approval report (Drugs 2024;84:1475-1480) summarizes the development of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) (NIKTIMVO; axatilimab-csfr), an anti-CSF-1R humanized IgG4 (kappa light chain) monoclonal antibody developed by Incyte Corporation and Syndax Pharmaceuticals. Axatilimab received its first approval on 14 August 2024 in the USA for the treatment of [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and paediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg, and was added to the NCCN guidelines for cGVHD in August 2024. The report covers pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic trials (AGAVE-201), and adverse events.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39551906/) (PMID:39551906)

B cell.body:
# B cell

B cells are lymphocytes of the adaptive immune system that express the surface antigen [CD19](../molecule/b-lymphocyte-antigen-cd19-protein.md) from early (pre-B) development through to [plasmablasts](../celltype/plasmablast.md) and some plasma cells. Pathogenic B cells drive the immunopathology of both neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md). [Inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) targets and depletes CD19-expressing B cells through antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity; in N-MOmentum CD20+ B cells fell below the lower limit of normal in all treated patients by 4 weeks.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
B cell.description: A lymphocyte of the adaptive immune system expressing the surface antigen CD19 throughout its development; the cell population depleted by the anti-CD19 antibody inebilizumab.

B-lymphocyte antigen CD19 (protein).body:
# B-lymphocyte antigen CD19 (protein)

CD19 is a B-cell surface transmembrane glycoprotein expressed across B-cell development, from pre-B and mature B lymphocytes through to [plasmablasts](../celltype/plasmablast.md) and some plasma cells. Encoded by the [CD19 gene](../gene/cd19-gene.md), it is the molecular target of [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md). Because CD19 expression appears earlier than CD20 in B-cell development and persists later, CD19-targeted depletion captures a broader range of pathogenic [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md) than anti-CD20 strategies.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)

BENEGENE-2 trial.body:
# BENEGENE-2 trial

BENEGENE-2 (NCT03861273) was a phase 3, open-label, single-arm study conducted at 27 centres in 13 countries that evaluated a single intravenous infusion of [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) at 5x10^11 vg/kg in 45 adult men with moderately severe to severe [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md) (factor IX level <=2%) who had received at least 6 months of prophylactic factor IX concentrate in the BENEGENE-1 lead-in study. The primary endpoint, the [annualized bleeding rate](../biomedicalmeasure/annualized-bleeding-rate.md) for total bleeding episodes from week 12 to month 15, met noninferiority and superiority versus prophylaxis (4.42 to 1.28; treatment difference -3.15; P=0.008). Mean [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) at month 15 was 26.9% by one-stage SynthASil assay.

## Citations

BETTER trial.body:
# BETTER trial

The BETTER trial (ACTRN12621000315819) is an international multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel, superiority randomised controlled trial whose protocol plans to enrol 194 children and adults aged 2-49 years with [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) across eight sites in Australia, Malaysia and the Philippines. It is the first RCT to combine children and adults with bronchiectasis into a single trial and the first trial of [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) in bronchiectasis.

Participants receive weight-based [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) (oral suspension 175 mg/5 mL or 300 mg capsules, twice daily) or matching placebo for 12 months. The primary endpoint is the [acute respiratory exacerbation rate](../biomedicalmeasure/pulmonary-exacerbation-rate.md) over 12 months; secondary outcomes include [quality of life](../biomedicalmeasure/quality-of-life.md), exacerbation duration, time-to-next exacerbation, hospitalisations and [lung function](../biomedicalmeasure/forced-expiratory-volume-in-1-second.md). This is a protocol paper describing planned design; no efficacy results are yet reported.

## Citations

Bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors.body:
# Bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors

Bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors are antibacterial agents that target bacterial type II topoisomerase enzymes — [DNA gyrase](../biologicalfunction/dna-gyrase.md) and [topoisomerase IV](../biologicalfunction/topoisomerase-iv.md). The novel (non-fluoroquinolone) bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs), such as [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md), bind at a distinct site and stabilise the precleavage enzyme-DNA complex, generating single-strand breaks rather than the double-strand breaks induced by fluoroquinolones.

Belani 2017 — trifluridine/tipiracil PK.body:
# Belani 2017 — trifluridine/tipiracil PK study

This phase 1, open-label, randomised, parallel, two-group pharmacokinetic study (NCT01867866) was conducted at four centres in the United States from May 2013 to January 2014. A total of 44 patients with [advanced solid tumors](../disease/advanced-solid-tumors.md) were enrolled and randomized to receive a single 35 mg/m2 dose of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (group 1) or [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) alone (group 2) on the morning of day 1; all patients then received multiple-dose trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m2 twice daily on days 2-5 and 8-12 of a 28-day cycle.

The study demonstrated that coadministration of [tipiracil](../molecule/tipiracil.md) (a thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor) markedly increased trifluridine exposure: trifluridine AUC0-last was ~37-fold higher and Cmax ~22-fold higher with trifluridine/tipiracil than with trifluridine alone, providing proof of concept that thymidine phosphorylase inhibition raises trifluridine bioavailability.

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of nucleoside analog trifluridine and thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)

Berotralstat.body:
# Berotralstat

Berotralstat (Orladeyo, formerly BCX7353) is a once-daily oral small-molecule selective inhibitor of [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md). Approved in 2020 for long-term prophylaxis of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md), it offers a convenient oral route of administration but is associated with gastrointestinal adverse events in some patients. As a [plasma kallikrein inhibitor](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md), it requires regular daily administration; some patients used berotralstat as concomitant or prior prophylaxis in the NTLA-2002 trials.

Beta-lactamase inhibitors.body:
# Beta-lactamase inhibitors

Beta-lactamase inhibitors are agents that inhibit bacterial beta-lactamase enzymes, thereby protecting and restoring the activity of partner beta-lactam antibacterials against beta-lactamase-producing bacteria. The class includes tazobactam, avibactam, and [enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md). The development of more potent inhibitors of [extended-spectrum beta-lactamases](../molecularclass/extended-spectrum-beta-lactamases.md) for combination with available beta-lactams offers carbapenem-sparing therapy against ESBL-producing Gram-negative pathogens such as in [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md).

Bhagwat 2024 — imlunestrant preclinical.body:
# Bhagwat 2024 — imlunestrant preclinical profile

This preclinical study describes the profile of [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) (LY3484356), a next-generation, brain-penetrant oral [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md) and pure [ERα](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) antagonist. Imlunestrant bound ERα with high affinity (Ki 0.64 nM for wild-type, 2.80 nM for ERα-Y537S, 0.11 nM for ERβ), degraded ERα and inhibited ER-regulated gene transcription and cell proliferation regardless of [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) mutation status.

In xenograft and PDX models (including [ESR1 Y537S](../variant/esr1-y537s.md) and [ESR1 D538G](../variant/esr1-d538g.md) mutants and fulvestrant-resistant models), imlunestrant inhibited tumor growth more effectively than [fulvestrant](../molecule/fulvestrant.md), showed synergy with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md), and improved survival in an ER-positive intracranial breast cancer model with the highest brain drug exposure among SERDs tested.

## Citations

Bhagwat 2024 — imlunestrant preclinical.description: Preclinical characterization of imlunestrant (LY3484356), a next-generation, brain-penetrant oral ERα degrader and pure antagonist, demonstrating potent activity in ESR1 wild-type and mutant breast cancer cell lines, xenografts and PDX models, enhanced combination activity, and inhibition of intracranial ER-positive tumor growth.

Bispecific antibodies.body:
# Bispecific antibodies

Bispecific antibodies are engineered immunoglobulins capable of binding two distinct antigens or epitopes simultaneously. [Zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) is a bispecific, humanized, glycoengineered IgG1 antibody whose two Fab arms target the extracellular domains of [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md) and [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md), enabling its Dock & Block mechanism against NRG1-driven signaling.

Blood coagulation.body:
# Blood coagulation

Blood coagulation is the cascade of plasma clotting factors, including [factor IX](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md), that culminates in fibrin clot formation and hemostasis. The high-activity variant [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) enhances this pathway and underlies the activity measured in the FIX-R338L field study.

## Citations
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)

Blood creatine kinase increased.body:
# Blood creatine kinase increased

Increased blood creatine kinase (creatine phosphokinase, CPK) is a frequent on-target laboratory abnormality of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), reflecting reduced macrophage-mediated enzyme clearance after CSF-1R inhibition. It was dose-dependent in AGAVE-201 (11%, 32%, 62% across the 0.3-, 1-, and 3-mg dose groups). In the phase I/II study, a grade 4 CPK increase with inflammatory myopathy was one of two dose-limiting toxicities at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks. CPK was modeled as a safety PD biomarker driven by nonclassical monocyte count.

Increased blood lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is a transient on-target laboratory abnormality of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), reflecting reduced Kupffer cell-mediated enzyme clearance after CSF-1R inhibition. Bradykinin (protein).body:
# Bradykinin (protein)

Bradykinin is a vasoactive nonapeptide cleaved from high-molecular-weight kininogen by [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) within the [kallikrein-kinin pathway](../biologicalpathway/kallikrein-kinin-pathway.md). Acting on the bradykinin B2 receptor, it increases vascular permeability and is the principal mediator of the swelling that characterizes [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). Therapies for HAE reduce bradykinin either by lowering or inhibiting plasma kallikrein (e.g., [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), [lanadelumab](../molecule/lanadelumab.md), [berotralstat](../molecule/berotralstat.md)) or by antagonizing the bradykinin B2 receptor (e.g., icatibant, deucrictibant).

- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Bradykinin (protein).description: A vasoactive nonapeptide cleaved from high-molecular-weight kininogen by plasma kallikrein; acting on the bradykinin B2 receptor, it increases vascular permeability and is the principal mediator of swelling in hereditary angioedema.

Bronchiectasis.body:
# Bronchiectasis

Bronchiectasis (here, non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis) is a chronic lung disorder affecting all age groups, characterised clinically by recurrent or persistent wet/productive [cough](../phenotype/cough.md), lower airway infection and inflammation, [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md) and disrupted mucociliary clearance, and radiographically by abnormal bronchial dilatation on chest CT. Acute respiratory exacerbations are common and a major contributor to disease burden. It ranks behind only asthma and [COPD](../disease/chronic-obstructive-pulmonary-disease.md) as the most common chronic pulmonary disorder, yet has no licensed therapies.

Both the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) and the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md) evaluate the mucoactive agent [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) in this disease. Bronchiectasis frequently coexists with COPD (prevalence ~54% of COPD patients), where it worsens exacerbation risk and mortality.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Bronchiectasis.description: A chronic lung disorder characterised by abnormal, irreversible bronchial dilatation on chest CT, with recurrent or persistent wet/productive cough, chronic lower airway infection and inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and frequent acute respiratory exacerbations.

edges.note: chronic mucus hypersecretion is a typical respiratory condition in bronchiectasis, with or without chronic airway obstruction
characterised clinically by recurrent or persistent wet/productive cough

meta-analysis of 18 studies found prevalence of bronchiectasis in COPD of 54% (range 25-69%); comorbid bronchiectasis in COPD raised exacerbation risk (RR 1.97, 95% CI 1.29-3.00) and mortality (RR 1.96, 95% CI 1.04-3.70)

C1 esterase inhibitor (protein).body:
# C1 esterase inhibitor (protein)

C1 esterase inhibitor (C1INH) is a serine protease inhibitor (serpin) encoded by [SERPING1](../gene/serping1-gene.md) and produced primarily by the liver. It is the key negative regulator of the contact ([kallikrein-kinin](../biologicalpathway/kallikrein-kinin-pathway.md)) activation pathway, attenuating [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md) production by inhibiting factor XIIa and [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md). Quantitative deficiency (type 1) or dysfunction (type 2) of C1INH causes [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). Plasma-derived and recombinant C1INH replacement therapies are approved for long-term prophylaxis and on-demand treatment, and gene therapies (e.g., BMN 331) aim to restore endogenous functional C1INH.

# CALCA (gene)

CALCA is the human gene that, through alternative splicing, encodes both calcitonin and the alpha isoform of [calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md). CGRP is the neuropeptide target of the anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md) studied for [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md).

CD19 (gene).body:
# CD19 (gene)

CD19 is the human gene encoding [B-lymphocyte antigen CD19](../molecule/b-lymphocyte-antigen-cd19-protein.md), a B-cell surface glycoprotein. Its product is expressed throughout B-cell development and is the target of the B-cell-depleting antibody [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md). CD19+ [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md) drive the immunopathology of both neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md).

CDK4/6 inhibitors.body:
# CDK4/6 inhibitors

CDK4/6 inhibitors (cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors) — including [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md), palbociclib, and ribociclib — are targeted agents that, combined with endocrine therapy, have had a dramatic impact on outcomes in [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md). In the EMBER program, [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) was combined with abemaciclib, the only CDK4/6i administered on a continuous schedule, in both advanced breast cancer and [ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer](../disease/er-positive-endometrioid-endometrial-cancer.md).

CDK9 (gene).body:
# CDK9 (gene)

CDK9 encodes [cyclin-dependent kinase 9](../molecule/cyclin-dependent-kinase-9-protein.md), a transcriptional CDK that phosphorylates RNA polymerase II to drive productive transcription elongation. It is the principal molecular target of [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) (TG02); inhibiting CDK-9 depletes short-lived survival proteins such as c-MYC and MCL-1 in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md).

CGRP receptor (protein).body:
# CGRP receptor (protein)

The CGRP receptor is the cell-surface receptor for [calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md), a heterodimeric complex of the calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CALCRL) and receptor activity-modifying protein 1 (RAMP1). It is expressed in the vestibular system of the inner ear, supporting a possible causative role for CGRP signaling in [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md).

The receptor is the direct molecular target of [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md), which blocks the receptor; this distinguishes it mechanistically from the ligand-neutralizing antibodies [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md).

CIDP therapy review 2024.body:
# CIDP therapy review 2024

A comprehensive review of current and emerging treatments for [chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md) (CIDP). It covers RCT-supported first-line therapies ([intravenous immunoglobulin](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md), [subcutaneous immunoglobulin](../molecule/subcutaneous-immunoglobulin.md), [corticosteroids](../molecularclass/corticosteroids.md), [plasma exchange](../methodorprocedure/plasma-exchange.md)), refractory-disease options ([cyclophosphamide](../molecule/cyclophosphamide.md), [rituximab](../molecule/rituximab.md), [autologous HSCT](../methodorprocedure/autologous-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplantation.md)), and novel agents including the FcRn blocker [efgartigimod](../molecule/efgartigimod.md), complement inhibitors and BTK inhibitors.

## Citations

edges.note: review of first-line, refractory and emerging treatments for CIDP and the need for better biomarkers and outcome measures

CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.body:
# CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing

CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing (more accurately, guide RNA-Cas9 editing) uses the bacterial Cas9 endonuclease directed by a single guide RNA to make a sequence-specific double-strand break at a chosen genomic locus. Endogenous repair by nonhomologous end-joining introduces small insertions and deletions that disrupt the targeted gene. In an in vivo approach, the editing components (Cas9 mRNA and sgRNA) are delivered directly to the patient, often via [lipid nanoparticle hepatic delivery](../methodorprocedure/lipid-nanoparticle-hepatic-delivery.md). [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md) applies this method to knock out [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md) in [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md) as a single-dose treatment for [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md), and [nexiguran ziclumeran](../molecule/nexiguran-ziclumeran.md) applies it to knock out [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md) in hepatocytes as a one-time treatment for [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)

CSF1R (gene).body:
# CSF1R (gene)

CSF1R is the human gene encoding [colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF-1R)](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md), a cell-surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase. Signaling through the receptor, triggered by its ligands [CSF-1](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-protein.md) and [interleukin-34](../molecule/interleukin-34-protein.md), is the primary regulatory pathway for the development and differentiation of the mononuclear phagocytic cell lineage. CSF-1R-driven signaling underpins the profibrotic macrophage biology targeted by [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) in [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md).

Calcitonin gene-related peptide (protein.body:
# Calcitonin gene-related peptide (protein)

Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is a potent vasodilating neuropeptide of the trigeminovascular system, encoded by [CALCA](../gene/calca-gene.md). Beyond its established role as a validated target for [migraine](../disease/migraine.md), CGRP is expressed in cochlear and vestibular organs and is implicated in [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) pathophysiology, potentially via neurogenic inflammation.

The therapeutic benefit of CGRP-blocking antibodies such as [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md), [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md), and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md) indirectly supports a causative role for CGRP in vestibular symptoms. CGRP knockout mice show altered vestibulo-ocular reflexes, and CGRP infusion in mice causes impaired balance and nausea, consistent with a role in generating [dizziness](../phenotype/dizziness.md).

## Citations

- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
Calcitonin gene-related peptide (protein.description: A potent vasodilating neuropeptide of the trigeminovascular system, encoded by CALCA, that is also expressed in cochlear and vestibular organs; an excellent target for migraine treatment and implicated in vestibular migraine pathophysiology.

edges.note: CGRP is expressed in the vestibular system and may be involved in VM pathophysiology by promoting neurogenic inflammation; efficacy of anti-CGRP antibodies indirectly supports a causative role of CGRP in vestibular symptoms

Cardiac failure.body:
# Cardiac failure

Cardiac failure (heart failure) is the clinical syndrome in which the heart cannot pump blood sufficiently to meet the body's needs. In [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md) it reflects progressive amyloid infiltration of the myocardium. In the [nexiguran ziclumeran phase 1 trial](../study/nexiguran-ziclumeran-phase-1-attr-cm-trial.md) it was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event (13/36, 36%) and the most common serious adverse event (5/36, 14%); the observed rate of serious cardiac events (heart failure, arrhythmia, or stroke) was 0.16/patient/year (95% CI 0.08-0.36).

## Citations

Cefepime.body:
# Cefepime

Cefepime is a broad-spectrum 4th-generation [cephalosporin](../molecularclass/cephalosporins.md) antibacterial, first approved in the 1990s, with activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens, including good antipseudomonal activity and intrinsic resistance to hydrolysis by AmpC and OXA-48-like enzymes. Its bactericidal action is due to inhibition of peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis by binding [penicillin-binding protein](../molecule/penicillin-binding-protein.md) targets; a positively charged substitution makes it a zwitterion that enhances cell-wall penetration. Because resistance has increased with the spread of ESBLs, cefepime is combined with the beta-lactamase inhibitor [enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) (EXBLIFEP) to restore activity against ESBL-producing bacteria in [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md).

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Cefepime.description: A broad-spectrum 4th-generation cephalosporin antibacterial with activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens (including antipseudomonal activity); a zwitterion with enhanced cell-wall penetration, combined with enmetazobactam to overcome ESBL-mediated resistance.

edges.note: cefepime (first approved in the 1990s) was previously approved for cUTI/pyelonephritis, pneumonia, and associated bacteraemia; the cefepime/enmetazobactam EU indication is based partly on these prior cefepime indications
4th-generation cephalosporin; intrinsic resistance to hydrolysis by AmpC and OXA-48-like enzymes
bactericidal action via inhibition of peptidoglycan cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding protein targets

Cephalosporins.body:
# Cephalosporins

Cephalosporins are a class of beta-lactam antibacterials that inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding [penicillin-binding proteins](../molecule/penicillin-binding-protein.md). [Cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) is a 4th-generation cephalosporin with broad Gram-negative and Gram-positive activity, including antipseudomonal activity and intrinsic resistance to hydrolysis by AmpC and OXA-48-like enzymes; it is combined with the beta-lactamase inhibitor [enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) to overcome ESBL-mediated resistance.

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Cephalosporins.description: A class of beta-lactam antibacterials that inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins; cefepime is a 4th-generation cephalosporin with broad Gram-negative and Gram-positive activity.

Chest physiotherapy.body:
# Chest physiotherapy

Chest physiotherapy is a non-pharmacologic airway clearance therapy used to facilitate mucus drainage in hypersecretory lung disorders. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) it comprised self-assisted (autogenic drainage, Flutter oscillatory PEP device) and physiotherapy-assisted (percussion/vibration, active cycle of breathing) techniques delivered in ~45-minute sessions over 15-20 days as part of pulmonary rehabilitation. It was the common background therapy in both arms; the trial tested whether adding [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) to chest physiotherapy improved outcomes over physiotherapy alone in [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) with [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md).

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
Chest physiotherapy.description: Non-pharmacologic airway clearance therapy (eg, postural/autogenic drainage, percussion/vibration, active cycle of breathing, oscillatory positive expiratory pressure devices) used to facilitate mucus clearance in hypersecretory lung disorders.

edges.note: administered to all patients as the airway-clearance active treatment to drain mucus; one active treatment given equally to both study arms
routine technique of the pulmonary rehabilitation strategy; comparator/adjunct background therapy in both study arms

Chondrocyte.body:
# Chondrocyte

Chondrocytes are the cartilage-forming cells of the growth plate whose proliferation and differentiation drive longitudinal bone growth through [endochondral ossification](../biologicalpathway/endochondral-ossification.md). [FGFR3](../molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-receptor-3-protein.md) is particularly prevalent on the chondrocyte surface; in [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md), activating [FGFR3](../gene/fgfr3-gene.md) variants inhibit chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation (via STAT1 and MAPK signaling), impairing growth. [Infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) reduces this FGFR3 overactivity to restore chondrocyte-driven growth.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Chondrocyte.description: The cartilage-forming cell of the growth plate whose proliferation and differentiation drive longitudinal bone growth via endochondral ossification; chondrocytes express FGFR3 on their surface, and FGFR3 overactivity inhibits their proliferation and differentiation.

edges.note: longitudinal bone growth is driven by the proliferation and differentiation of chondrocytes in the growth plate

Chronic graft-versus-host disease.body:
# Chronic graft-versus-host disease

Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) is an immune-mediated, multiorgan complication that arises in 30-70% of recipients after [allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation](../methodorprocedure/allogeneic-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplantation.md) and is the major cause of late nonrelapse morbidity and mortality. It is characterized by inflammatory and fibrotic manifestations (skin sclerosis, joint/fascial involvement, bronchiolitis obliterans) sharing features with autoimmune disorders. [CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md)-dependent nonclassical monocytes and profibrotic [macrophages](../celltype/macrophage.md) are key disease mediators, providing the rationale for treatment with [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md).

## Citations
- [Axatilimab for Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease After Failure of at Least Two Prior Systemic Therapies: Results of a Phase I/II Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36459673/) (PMID:36459673)
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
- [Axatilimab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39551906/) (PMID:39551906)
Chronic graft-versus-host disease.description: An immune-mediated, serious, multiorgan complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, affecting 30-70% of recipients, characterized by inflammatory and fibrotic manifestations and driven in part by CSF-1R-dependent monocytes and macrophages; the major cause of late nonrelapse morbidity and mortality.

edges.note: cGVHD is the most common late complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, affecting approximately half of transplant recipients
