Chronic hepatitis B.body:
# Chronic hepatitis B

Chronic hepatitis B is a persistent infection of the liver by [hepatitis B virus](../organism/hepatitis-b-virus.md), defined by HBV infection beyond six months. It increases the risk of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, liver decompensation, and death. A functional cure — sustained loss of hepatitis B surface antigen with undetectable HBV DNA at 24 weeks after finite-duration therapy — is the desired outcome but is rarely achieved with standard care (peginterferon and lifelong nucleoside/nucleotide analogues). The [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md) evaluated [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) with or without an immunomodulator to improve functional-cure rates.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Chronic hepatitis B.description: A chronic infection of the liver by hepatitis B virus, persisting beyond six months, that increases the risk of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, liver decompensation, and death; a functional cure (sustained HBsAg loss with undetectable HBV DNA) is the desired treatment outcome.

edges.note: 54% of participants had an elevated ALT level during treatment or follow-up (6% grade 3 or 4); ALT flares can accompany HBsAg decline and NA discontinuation

Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyr.body:
# Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy

Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) is the most common chronic autoimmune peripheral nervous system disorder (estimated worldwide prevalence ~3 per 100,000), classically presenting with symmetrical proximal and distal motor and sensory dysfunction of the four limbs progressing over more than 8 weeks. It is antibody-mediated, with pathogenic [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) implicated, which underlies the efficacy of IgG-lowering [FcRn blockers](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md). First-line evidence-based therapies are [immunoglobulins](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md), [corticosteroids](../molecularclass/corticosteroids.md) and [plasma exchange](../methodorprocedure/plasma-exchange.md), with up to 25-50% of treated patients eventually entering remission.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyr.description: The most common chronic autoimmune peripheral nervous system disorder, typically presenting with symmetrical proximal and distal motor and sensory dysfunction of the four limbs progressing over more than 8 weeks; treatable with immunoglobulins, corticosteroids and plasma exchange.

edges.note: an antibody-mediated disorder; pathogenic IgG autoantibodies contribute to demyelination, and FcRn blockade lowering IgG is therapeutic

Chronic mucus hypersecretion.body:
# Chronic mucus hypersecretion

Chronic mucus hypersecretion is the coughing and bringing up of sputum lasting at least 3 months in a given year for 2 or more consecutive years. It is a typical respiratory condition in [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) (with or without chronic airway obstruction) and in [COPD](../disease/chronic-obstructive-pulmonary-disease.md)/chronic bronchitis. Mucus plugging and hypersecretion are negative prognostic determinants, associated with an increased risk of death, and are of particular relevance in the elderly. Reducing it is a therapeutic target for the mucoactive agent [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md).

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Chronic mucus hypersecretion.description: Chronic coughing and expectoration of sputum lasting at least 3 months in a year for 2 or more consecutive years; a typical feature of bronchiectasis, chronic bronchitis and COPD and a negative prognostic determinant.

edges.note: typical respiratory condition in patients with bronchiectasis, with or without chronic airway obstruction
mucus plugging and hypersecretion are negative prognostic determinants associated with increased risk of death from pulmonary infection or all causes, of prognostic relevance in the elderly

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.body:
# Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common chronic lung disease with airflow limitation and, frequently, [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md). In both papers COPD appears as clinical context for [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md): the two conditions overlap (bronchiectasis present in ~54% of COPD patients) and share a pathobiology of chronic airway infection, inflammation and disrupted mucociliary clearance. Evidence for [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) in COPD/chronic bronchitis (reduced exacerbations and hospitalisation) underpins the rationale for testing it in bronchiectasis.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.description: A common chronic progressive lung disease characterised by airflow limitation, often with chronic mucus hypersecretion; it frequently coexists with bronchiectasis and shares the pathobiology of chronic airway infection, inflammation and impaired mucociliary clearance.

edges.note: chronic mucus hypersecretion and mucus plugging are negative prognostic determinants associated with increased risk of death from pulmonary infection or all causes in COPD
bronchiectasis-COPD overlap recognised; prevalence of bronchiectasis in COPD 54% (range 25-69%) in a meta-analysis of 18 studies

Clinical remission.body:
# Clinical remission

Clinical remission in [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md) is a composite outcome defined by a modified Mayo endoscopic subscore of 0 or 1, a rectal-bleeding subscore of 0, and a stool-frequency subscore of 0 or 1 (not greater than baseline). It was the primary efficacy end point of the [ARTEMIS-UC trial](../study/artemis-uc-trial.md), where [tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md) achieved clinical remission at week 12 in 26% of cohort 1 patients versus 1% with placebo (difference 25 percentage points, P<0.001), and in 32% versus 11% among test-positive patients (P=0.02).

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)
Clinical remission.description: A composite remission outcome in ulcerative colitis defined by a modified Mayo endoscopic subscore of 0 or 1, a rectal-bleeding subscore of 0, and a stool-frequency subscore of 0 or 1 (not greater than baseline); the primary efficacy end point in the ARTEMIS-UC trial.

edges.note: composite of modified Mayo endoscopic subscore 0-1, rectal-bleeding subscore 0, and stool-frequency subscore 0-1 not greater than baseline; primary end point at week 12

Coagulation factor IX (protein).body:
# Coagulation factor IX (protein)

Coagulation factor IX (FIX) is a vitamin K-dependent serine protease encoded by [F9](../gene/f9-gene.md) and synthesized in [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md). It circulates as a single-chain zymogen and, on activation, the activation peptide is removed to form FIXa, which functions in the intrinsic coagulation tenase complex with activated factor VIII and factor X on phospholipid surfaces. Deficiency or dysfunction of FIX causes [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md). The high-activity [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) variant exhibits roughly 8- to 12-fold greater coagulant activity than wild-type FIX.

## Citations
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Coagulation factor IX (protein).description: Vitamin K-dependent serine protease coagulation factor IX synthesized in hepatocytes; circulates as a single-chain zymogen that is activated (FIXa) and participates in the intrinsic coagulation tenase complex with activated factor VIII and factor X on phospholipid surfaces. Deficiency or dysfunction causes hemophilia B.

edges.note: FIX circulates as a single-chain zymogen; on activation the activation peptide is removed to form FIXa; the high-activity R338L variant requires interaction with FVIIIa and FX on phospholipid surfaces in the tenase complex

Coagulation factor IX concentrates.body:
# Coagulation factor IX concentrates

Coagulation factor IX concentrates are plasma-derived or recombinant factor IX replacement products, including standard half-life (e.g. nonacog alfa) and extended half-life (e.g. eftrenonacog alfa) products, infused intravenously to raise [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) and prevent or treat bleeding in [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md). They are the prophylactic standard of care and the comparator against which [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) demonstrated superiority in [BENEGENE-2](../study/benegene-2-trial.md). The FIX-R338L field study showed that spiked-in exogenous concentrate is additive to endogenous FIX-R338L without assay interference.

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)
Coagulation factor IX concentrates.description: Class of plasma-derived or recombinant coagulation factor IX replacement products (including standard half-life and extended half-life products) infused intravenously to raise factor IX activity for the prophylaxis and treatment of bleeding in hemophilia B; the standard-of-care comparator for fidanacogene elaparvovec gene therapy.

edges.note: standard of care for severe hemophilia B is regular replacement therapy with clotting factor concentrates; even extended half-life FIX products require IV infusion every 7-14 days

Colony-stimulating factor 1 (protein).body:
# Colony-stimulating factor 1 (protein)

Colony-stimulating factor 1 (CSF-1, M-CSF) is an endogenous cytokine ligand of [CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md). Together with [interleukin-34](../molecule/interleukin-34-protein.md), CSF-1-mediated CSF-1R signaling is the primary pathway regulating development and differentiation of the mononuclear phagocytic lineage. Because [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) competitively blocks CSF-1 binding to the receptor, circulating CSF-1 rises dose-dependently during treatment, serving as a pharmacodynamic biomarker of CSF-1R blockade.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
- [Semimechanistic Population PK/PD Modeling of Axatilimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39704205/) (PMID:39704205)
Colony-stimulating factor 1 (protein).description: An endogenous cytokine ligand of CSF-1R; binding of CSF-1 to CSF-1R induces signaling that regulates development and differentiation of monocytes and macrophages. CSF-1 is a PD biomarker of axatilimab activity, rising on CSF-1R blockade.

edges.note: CSF-1 binds CSF-1R competitively with axatilimab; KdCSF1 fixed at 0.048 nM (48 pM) in the PK/PD model

edges.note: CSF-1 binding to CSF-1R on monocyte precursors leads to their differentiation to nonclassical monocytic cells (NCMCs)

Colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (pr.body:
# Colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (protein)

Colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF-1R) is a cell-surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase encoded by [CSF1R](../gene/csf1r-gene.md) and expressed on monocyte precursors, monocytes, and [macrophages](../celltype/macrophage.md). Binding of its ligands [CSF-1](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-protein.md) or [interleukin-34](../molecule/interleukin-34-protein.md) induces the primary regulatory signaling for development and differentiation of the mononuclear phagocytic cell lineage. In [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md), CSF-1R-dependent nonclassical monocytes and profibrotic macrophages drive multiorgan inflammation and fibrosis, making CSF-1R the molecular target of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md).

## Citations
- [Axatilimab for Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease After Failure of at Least Two Prior Systemic Therapies: Results of a Phase I/II Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36459673/) (PMID:36459673)
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
- [Semimechanistic Population PK/PD Modeling of Axatilimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39704205/) (PMID:39704205)
- [Axatilimab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39551906/) (PMID:39551906)

It is the molecular target of axatilimab.

Complicated urinary tract infection.body:
# Complicated urinary tract infection

Complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI), including acute pyelonephritis, is a urinary tract infection associated with conditions that raise the risk of treatment failure or complications; it is distinct from [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md) (acute cystitis). It is frequently caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria such as [Escherichia coli](../organism/escherichia-coli.md), [Klebsiella pneumoniae](../organism/klebsiella-pneumoniae.md), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae complex. Cefepime/[enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) received its first approval (USA, February 2024) for adults with cUTI including pyelonephritis, demonstrating superiority over piperacillin/tazobactam in the phase 3 ALLIUM trial.

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Complicated urinary tract infection.description: A urinary tract infection associated with conditions that increase the risk of treatment failure or complications (including acute pyelonephritis), often caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria; distinct from uncomplicated UTI/acute cystitis.
synonyms: complicated urinary tract infection including pyelonephritis

Corticosteroids.body:
# Corticosteroids

Corticosteroids (e.g. prednisolone, dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) are anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive steroids and a first-line therapy for [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md), effective since first described in 1958. RCT evidence is limited (one 35-subject unblinded trial showed non-significant superiority over no treatment), but the PREDICT study (41 subjects) found pulse oral dexamethasone equivalent to daily prednisolone for 12-month remission while acting faster (median 17 vs 39 weeks) with fewer side-effects. Corticosteroids may allow longer therapy-free remission than [IVIg](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md).

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Corticosteroids.description: A class of anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive steroid hormones (e.g. prednisolone, dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) used as first-line therapy for CIDP, acting through genomic and rapid non-genomic mechanisms.

edges.note: first-line therapy effective since 1958; a single unblinded RCT of 35 subjects (oral prednisolone vs no treatment) showed non-significant superiority on NIS group scores with borderline significant superiority by number improved (not in ITT); may yield longer therapy-free remission than IVIg

PREDICT RCT (41 subjects) comparing daily oral prednisolone vs monthly pulse oral dexamethasone showed no difference in remission-without-treatment at 12 months, but dexamethasone acted faster (median 17 vs 39 weeks) with fewer side-effects

Cough.body:
# Cough

Cough (typically wet/productive in bronchiectasis) is a key respiratory symptom and patient-reported outcome in both papers. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) cough was scored on a 0-200 mm visual analog scale and improved significantly in both arms (erdosteine group -11.0%, p=0.001; physiotherapy-alone group -0.4%, p=0.04). In the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), a sustained change in cough is part of the paediatric exacerbation definition, and cough QoL (PC-QoL) is a secondary outcome. It is a defining feature of [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md).

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Cough.description: A respiratory symptom; in bronchiectasis it is typically a recurrent or persistent wet/productive cough and a key patient-reported outcome.

edges.note: recurrent or persistent wet/productive cough is a defining clinical feature of bronchiectasis

Crisafulli 2007 — erdosteine in bronchie.body:
# Crisafulli 2007 — erdosteine in bronchiectasis

This 15-day, prospective, parallel, open-label pilot study enrolled 30 elderly patients (mean age 71 years) with [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) and [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md) referred to a pulmonary rehabilitation program at Ospedale Villa Pineta (Pavullo-Modena, Italy). Patients were randomised into group 1 (oral [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) 225 mg twice daily plus routine [chest physiotherapy](../methodorprocedure/chest-physiotherapy.md), n=15) or group 2 (chest physiotherapy alone, n=15).

The primary endpoint was the subjective semiquantitative score of sputum characteristics (mucus density, purulence and volume). Both groups improved in [6-minute walk test distance](../biomedicalmeasure/6-minute-walk-test-distance.md), [cough](../phenotype/cough.md) and [dyspnoea](../phenotype/dyspnoea.md) (VAS), while significant improvements in [FEV1](../biomedicalmeasure/forced-expiratory-volume-in-1-second.md) and [FVC](../biomedicalmeasure/forced-vital-capacity.md) occurred only in the erdosteine group.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion: a 15-day, prospective, parallel, open-label, pilot study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
Crisafulli 2007 — erdosteine in bronchie.description: A 15-day, prospective, parallel, open-label pilot study (n=30) in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and chronic mucus hypersecretion comparing oral erdosteine 225 mg twice daily plus chest physiotherapy (group 1) with chest physiotherapy alone (group 2).

edges.note: primary endpoint - subjective semiquantitative sputum characteristics (mucus density, purulence, volume) on a 3-point scale
secondary physiologic endpoint
group 1 (erdosteine 225 mg BID + chest physiotherapy, n=15) vs group 2 (chest physiotherapy alone, n=15); significant FEV1/FVC, MIP and PaO2 improvement only in erdosteine group

Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (protein).body:
# Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (protein)

Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK-9), encoded by [CDK9](../gene/cdk9-gene.md), is a transcriptional CDK that phosphorylates the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II to promote transcription elongation. Because [c-MYC](myc-proto-oncogene-protein.md) and [MCL-1](induced-myeloid-leukemia-cell-differentiation-protein-mcl-1-protein.md) are short-lived proteins, CDK-9 inhibition rapidly depletes them and induces apoptosis. It is the principal direct target of [zotiraciclib](zotiraciclib.md), and the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md) confirmed near-universal CDK-9 expression in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md).

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (protein).description: A transcriptional cyclin-dependent kinase that phosphorylates the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II; its inhibition depletes short-lived survival proteins (c-MYC, MCL-1), and it is the main direct target of zotiraciclib in glioblastoma.

edges.note: as a transcriptional CDK, CDK-9 supports expression of short-lived c-MYC; CDK-9 IHC correlated with c-MYC (r=0.29, p=0.007), supporting a regulatory role
CDK-9 supports expression of short-lived MCL-1; CDK-9 IHC correlated with MCL-1 (r=0.38, p=0.0004)
edges.object: Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1 (protein)

edges.note: nuclear CDK-9 expression detected in 102/105 glioblastomas, with 86% immunoreactive in >50% of tumor cells; proposed as both prognostic factor and therapeutic target

Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors.body:
# Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors

Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitors are small molecules that block CDK activity. Inhibitors of transcriptional CDKs, especially [CDK-9](../molecule/cyclin-dependent-kinase-9-protein.md), suppress RNA polymerase II-driven transcription and rapidly deplete short-lived survival proteins (c-MYC, MCL-1). [Zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) is a multi-CDK/CDK-9 inhibitor in this class evaluated in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md).

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors.description: A class of small-molecule kinase inhibitors that block cyclin-dependent kinases; transcriptional CDK (notably CDK-9) inhibitors deplete short-lived survival proteins and are being explored in glioblastoma.

edges.note: transcriptional CDK inhibitors such as zotiraciclib target CDK-9 to block RNA polymerase II phosphorylation

Cyclophosphamide.body:
# Cyclophosphamide

Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating immunosuppressant used as a first immunosuppressant in severe, refractory [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md), typically given intravenously at 1 g/m2 monthly for up to 6 months, often with high-dose corticosteroids. Case-series evidence (Good et al) reported complete remission in 11/15 (73.3%) of patients refractory to all three first-line therapies; a later meta-analysis indicated that concomitant corticosteroids did not add benefit.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Cyclophosphamide.description: An alkylating immunosuppressant used in severe refractory CIDP, typically intravenously and often with high-dose corticosteroids, supported by case-series evidence.

edges.note: Good et al case series of 15 subjects refractory to all three first-line therapies achieved amelioration within a mean of 4 months and complete remission in 11/15 (73.3%); an unpublished Chinese abstract reported 88% responder rate in 32 subjects; a meta-analysis found associated corticosteroid therapy did not add benefit

stats.dose: 1 g/m2 IV monthly for up to 6 months

D-amino acid oxidase (protein).body:
# D-amino acid oxidase (protein)

D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) is a flavoenzyme that oxidatively deaminates d-amino acids and is the enzyme responsible for breakdown of [d-serine](d-serine.md). It is the molecular target of [luvadaxistat](luvadaxistat.md): inhibiting DAAO (IC50 ~3.6 ng/mL for the human enzyme, with >90% peak target occupancy at the higher dose) prevents d-serine catabolism and raises d-serine in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
D-amino acid oxidase (protein).description: A flavoenzyme that catalyzes the oxidative deamination of d-amino acids and mediates breakdown of d-serine; the molecular target of luvadaxistat.

edges.note: DAAO mediates d-serine breakdown (oxidative deamination); its inhibition by luvadaxistat raises plasma and CSF d-serine

D-amino acid oxidase inhibitors.body:
# D-amino acid oxidase inhibitors

D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) inhibitors are small molecules that block [DAAO](../molecule/d-amino-acid-oxidase-protein.md), the enzyme that catabolizes [d-serine](../molecule/d-serine.md). By raising endogenous d-serine they enhance NMDA-receptor co-agonism, a rationale for their exploration in CNS disorders. [Luvadaxistat](../molecule/luvadaxistat.md) is a member of this class evaluated (without efficacy) in [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md).

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
D-amino acid oxidase inhibitors.description: A class of small molecules that inhibit d-amino acid oxidase, thereby raising endogenous d-serine and enhancing NMDA-receptor co-agonism; explored for CNS disorders including Friedreich ataxia.

edges.note: DAAO inhibitors block d-serine breakdown, raising d-serine in plasma and CSF

D-serine.body:
# D-serine

D-serine is an endogenous amino acid that serves as a co-agonist of NMDA-type glutamate receptors and an agonist of glutamate receptor delta 2, and is highly expressed in the cerebellum where it mediates glutamate-receptor-dependent functions. It is degraded by [DAAO](d-amino-acid-oxidase-protein.md); inhibiting DAAO with [luvadaxistat](luvadaxistat.md) raised plasma d-serine by ~62-66 ng/mL at week 12 in the [FRDA trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md), confirming target engagement, although this did not translate to clinical benefit in Friedreich ataxia.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
D-serine.description: An endogenous amino acid that acts as a co-agonist of NMDA-type glutamate receptors and an agonist of glutamate receptor delta 2, highly expressed in the cerebellum; its level is raised by DAAO inhibition.

edges.note: d-serine is an N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA)-type glutamate receptor co-agonist and an agonist of glutamate receptor delta 2; a critical mediator of glutamate-receptor-dependent cerebellar functions

DNA gyrase.body:
# DNA gyrase

DNA gyrase is a bacterial type IIA topoisomerase, a heterotetramer of two [GyrA](../molecule/gyra-protein.md) and two GyrB subunits, that regulates DNA topology during replication. It is one of the two enzymatic targets of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md); gepotidacin induces high levels of gyrase-mediated single-stranded DNA breaks, a bactericidal mechanism that differs from that of fluoroquinolones.

## Citations
- [Gepotidacin (GSK2140944) in vitro activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28483959/) (PMID:28483959)
DNA gyrase.description: A bacterial type IIA topoisomerase (heterotetramer of two GyrA and two GyrB subunits) that introduces negative supercoils into DNA during replication; one of the two enzymatic targets of gepotidacin.

Dalakas 2021 — FcRn in neuro-immunothera.body:
# Dalakas 2021 — FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies

This mini-review (Therapeutic Advances in Neurological Disorders) discusses how the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) protects IgG from lysosomal degradation, how [FCGRT](../gene/fcgrt-gene.md) VNTR polymorphisms may affect [IVIg](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md) and therapeutic monoclonal antibody pharmacokinetics, and the promise of [anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md) — efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab and [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) — in antibody-mediated neurological diseases such as myasthenia gravis.

## Citations
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies: From IgG catabolism, FCGRT gene polymorphisms, IVIg dosing and efficiency to specific FcRn inhibitors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
Dalakas 2021 — FcRn in neuro-immunothera.description: Mini-review on the role of the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) in IgG catabolism, FCGRT VNTR polymorphisms and IVIg efficacy, and the emerging anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies (efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab, nipocalimab) in antibody-mediated neurological diseases.

Death domain receptor 3 (protein).body:
# Death domain receptor 3 (protein)

Death domain receptor 3 (DR3), encoded by TNFRSF25, is the receptor for [TL1A](../molecule/tumor-necrosis-factor-like-cytokine-1a-protein.md). The TL1A-DR3 axis is a costimulatory cytokine system that is substantially up-regulated in inflamed intestinal tissue and contributes to [inflammatory bowel disease](../disease/inflammatory-bowel-disease.md) pathogenesis. [Tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md) prevents the interaction of TL1A with DR3, thereby suppressing pro-inflammatory T-cell responses in [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md).

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)
Death domain receptor 3 (protein).description: The receptor for TL1A, encoded by TNFRSF25; together with TL1A it forms a costimulatory cytokine system that is up-regulated in inflamed intestinal tissue and contributes to inflammatory bowel disease pathogenesis.

edges.note: DR3 (TNFRSF25), the TL1A receptor, is up-regulated in inflamed intestinal tissue; TNFRSF25 is an IBD-susceptibility gene; tulisokibart blocks TL1A-DR3 interaction

Definite dizzy days.body:
# Definite dizzy days

Definite dizzy days (DDDs) are a count of days per month on which a participant reported moderate or severe [dizziness](../phenotype/dizziness.md), captured daily by text-message survey. In the [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md), monthly DDDs fell from 17.9 to 6.6 on [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) versus 18.0 to 12.5 on placebo (difference -5.7 days; p=0.026; Cohen's d=1.02).

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
Definite dizzy days.description: A count of days per month on which a participant reported moderate or severe dizziness; an objective diary-based vestibular symptom endpoint in the INVESTMENT trial.

edges.note: any day with moderate or severe dizziness (rated daily via text message) counts as a definite dizzy day; secondary endpoint

Depatuxizumab mafodotin.body:
# Depatuxizumab mafodotin

Depatuxizumab mafodotin (depatux-m, ABT-414) is an antibody-drug conjugate joining the anti-[EGFR](../gene/egfr-gene.md)/EGFRvIII humanized antibody depatuxizumab (ABT-806) to the cytotoxic payload monomethyl auristatin F. Although effective in EGFR-amplified/EGFRvIII glioblastoma models, a phase 3 trial of 691 patients showed no overall-survival benefit in EGFR-amplified newly diagnosed [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md), attributed to emergence of resistant clones and limited tumor penetration. Reversible adverse events included photosensitivity and thrombocytopenia.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Depatuxizumab mafodotin.description: An antibody-drug conjugate linking the anti-EGFR/EGFRvIII humanized antibody depatuxizumab (ABT-806) to the cytotoxic payload monomethyl auristatin F (mafodotin), evaluated in EGFR-amplified glioblastoma where it failed to improve overall survival.

edges.note: phase 3 NCT02573324 (Lassman et al, 2023) showed no OS benefit for depatux-m in EGFR-amplified newly diagnosed glioblastoma; possibly due to resistant clones and limited tumor penetration
binds EGFRvIII and wild-type EGFR at elevated levels; upon binding activated EGFR the ADC is internalized and releases monomethyl auristatin F (mafodotin) causing cell death
most frequent reversible adverse events were photosensitivity (light sensitivity) and thrombocytopenia

Dhillon 2024 — Fidanacogene elaparvovec.body:
# Dhillon 2024 — Fidanacogene elaparvovec first approval

This AdisInsight "First Approval" report (Drugs 2024;84:479-486, S. Dhillon) summarizes the development of [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md), an AAV serotype Rh74var vector-based gene therapy developed by Spark Therapeutics (Roche) and Pfizer for [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md). It documents the drug's first approval in Canada on 27 December 2023 for adults with moderately severe to severe hemophilia B negative for neutralizing antibodies to AAVRh74var, and summarizes the BENEGENE-2 phase 3, phase 1/2a, and long-term follow-up trials.

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Dhillon 2024 — Fidanacogene elaparvovec.description: AdisInsight "First Approval" report (Drugs 2024;84:479-486) summarizing the development milestones, pharmacology, clinical trials, and first regulatory approval of the AAV vector-based gene therapy fidanacogene elaparvovec for hemophilia B.

Diarrhoea.body:
# Diarrhoea

Diarrhoea is a gastrointestinal adverse effect and the most common treatment-emergent adverse event associated with [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md), observed in 14% of patients in [EAGLE-2](../study/eagle-2-trial.md) and 18% in [EAGLE-3](../study/eagle-3-trial.md), versus 3-4% with [nitrofurantoin](../molecule/nitrofurantoin.md). Events were mostly mild to moderate, with gastrointestinal tolerability improved when gepotidacin is taken with food.

## Citations
- [Oral gepotidacin versus nitrofurantoin in patients with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38342126/) (PMID:38342126)
Diarrhoea.description: A gastrointestinal adverse effect characterized by frequent loose or watery stools; the most common treatment-emergent adverse event with gepotidacin.

Disproportionate short stature.body:
# Disproportionate short stature

Disproportionate short stature is the cardinal clinical manifestation of [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md), in which limb shortening exceeds truncal shortening, producing an elevated [upper-to-lower body segment ratio](../biomedicalmeasure/upper-to-lower-body-segment-ratio.md) (~2.0 from age 4 in achondroplasia versus ~1.0 in average stature). In the [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md), treatment with [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) at 0.25 mg/kg/day reduced this ratio from 2.02 to 1.88 over 18 months, indicating an improvement in body proportionality.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Disproportionate short stature.description: Short stature in which limb shortening exceeds truncal shortening, producing an elevated upper-to-lower body segment ratio; the cardinal clinical manifestation of achondroplasia.

edges.note: cardinal feature of achondroplasia; disproportionate limb shortening relative to truncal height, yielding a mean upper-to-lower body segment ratio of ~2.0 from age 4 versus ~1.0 in average stature

Dizziness.body:
# Dizziness

Dizziness is a non-specific sensation of imbalance or disequilibrium that, with [vertigo](../phenotype/vertigo.md), constitutes the core vestibular symptom burden of [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md). Reduction in dizziness was the central efficacy target in both the [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md) (count of definite dizzy days) and the [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md) (monthly dizziness days), where anti-CGRP therapy substantially reduced symptom days.

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
Dizziness.description: A non-specific sensation of imbalance or disequilibrium; with vertigo it constitutes the core vestibular symptom burden of vestibular migraine and the primary efficacy outcome target of anti-CGRP therapy in this setting.

edges.note: vestibular migraine is one of the most common causes of dizziness

Dizziness Handicap Inventory.body:
# Dizziness Handicap Inventory

The Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) is the most widely used patient-reported metric of vestibular outcomes, scored from 0 to 100, with a minimal clinically important difference of about 11 points. As a secondary endpoint in the [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md), DHI dropped 22.0 points on [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) versus 8.3 points on placebo (difference -13.7; 95% CI -20.4 to -8.5; p=0.018; Cohen's d=0.98).

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
Dizziness Handicap Inventory.description: The most widely used patient-reported metric of vestibular outcomes, scored 0-100; a secondary endpoint in the INVESTMENT trial with a minimal clinically important difference of about 11 points.

edges.note: secondary outcome - symptom-specific patient-reported outcome of vestibular handicap; MCID ~11 points, minimal detectable change ~18 points

Donidalorsen.body:
# Donidalorsen

Donidalorsen (IONIS-PKK-LRx, formerly IONIS-PKKRx; Ionis Pharmaceuticals) is an investigational GalNAc3-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide that targets the liver via the asialoglycoprotein receptor and binds prekallikrein mRNA, recruiting RNase H1 to degrade it and thereby lowering [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) and downstream [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md) production. As a [plasma kallikrein inhibitor](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md)-class agent for [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md), 80 mg SC every 4 weeks reduced the monthly attack rate to 0.23 versus 2.21 with placebo (P<0.001) in phase 2, an approximately 90% decrease, with 92% of patients attack-free from week 5 to 17. Phase 3 trials (OASIS-HAE) are underway.

## Citations
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Donidalorsen.description: An investigational GalNAc3-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (Ionis Pharmaceuticals) that binds prekallikrein mRNA in the liver and recruits RNase H1 to degrade it, lowering plasma prekallikrein and downstream bradykinin production for prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema.

edges.note: prekallikrein-lowering antisense oligonucleotide; reduces total plasma kallikrein
phase 2 mean HAE attacks/month wk1-17 0.23 (95% CI 0.08-0.39) with donidalorsen (n=14) vs 2.21 (95% CI 0.58-3.85) placebo (n=6), P<0.001, ~90% decrease; 12/13 (92%) attack-free wk5-17
phase 1 - mean 93.6% reduction in plasma prekallikrein protein 2 weeks after final dose in 80 mg group, persisting 3 months; Riedl review reports 94% reduction

Drug repositioning.body:
# Drug repositioning

Drug repositioning (repurposing) is the identification of new therapeutic uses for an existing drug beyond its original indication, regardless of whether it was approved or failed in clinical trials. It can reduce development time by about half and cut costs roughly 5-fold relative to developing a new drug from scratch. Computational repositioning leverages multi-omics evidence; a three-step PheWAS strategy identifies genes associated with a phenotype, drugs associated with those genes (e.g. via DrugBank), and returns those drugs as repositioning candidates. [StarGazer](../methodorprocedure/stargazer.md) operationalizes this with a single integrative score and [drug target prioritization](../concept/drug-target-prioritization.md) across 1844 phenotypic traits.

## Citations
- [StarGazer: A Hybrid Intelligence Platform for Drug Target Prioritization and Digital Drug Repositioning Using Streamlit](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35711912/) (PMID:35711912)
Drug repositioning.description: The identification of new therapeutic uses for an existing drug beyond its original indication (whether approved or failed in trials), reducing development time and cost; computational repositioning leverages multi-omics data such as genetic, expression, and network evidence.

Drug target prioritization.body:
# Drug target prioritization

Drug target prioritization is the computational process of ranking candidate drug targets for a disease of interest by integrating multi-omics evidence (genetic association from GWAS/PheWAS, target druggability, and protein-protein interaction network connectivity). It is an essential step for [drug repositioning](../concept/drug-repositioning.md). [StarGazer](../methodorprocedure/stargazer.md) implements it by computing a normalized score from five features and ranking genes associated with each of 1844 phenotypic traits.

## Citations
- [StarGazer: A Hybrid Intelligence Platform for Drug Target Prioritization and Digital Drug Repositioning Using Streamlit](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35711912/) (PMID:35711912)
Drug target prioritization.description: The computational process of ranking candidate drug targets (typically genes/proteins) for a disease of interest by integrating multi-omics evidence such as genetic association, druggability, and network connectivity, to focus drug discovery and repositioning efforts.

edges.note: target prioritization is an essential step for repositioning, highlighting potential drug targets for a disease

Duration of response.body:
# Duration of response

Duration of response (DOR) is the time from first documented objective response (complete or partial response, RECIST v1.1) to disease progression or death. In the [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md) it is the key secondary endpoint, assessing the durability of antitumor activity of [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) in patients with [NRG1 fusion-positive cancer](../disease/nrg1-fusion-positive-cancer.md), evaluated by both local investigator and central review. A confirmed response requires two consecutive assessments of complete or partial response at least 4 weeks apart.

## Citations
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
Duration of response.description: The time from first documented objective response (complete or partial) to disease progression or death; the key secondary endpoint capturing the durability of antitumor activity in the eNRGy trial.

edges.note: key secondary endpoint - durability of antitumor activity of zenocutuzumab per RECIST v1.1 (local and central review)

Dyspnoea.body:
# Dyspnoea

Dyspnoea (breathlessness) is a respiratory symptom assessed in both papers. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) it was measured on a 0-200 mm visual analog scale and improved significantly in both arms (erdosteine group -14.2%, p=0.001; physiotherapy-alone group -0.6%, p=0.01). In the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), breathlessness is one of the deteriorating symptoms in the adult [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) exacerbation definition.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Dyspnoea.description: A subjective sensation of breathing difficulty (breathlessness); a respiratory symptom and patient-reported outcome in bronchiectasis and COPD.

edges.note: breathlessness is one of the deteriorating symptoms in the adult bronchiectasis exacerbation definition

EAGLE-2 trial.body:
# EAGLE-2 trial

EAGLE-2 (NCT04020341, Efficacy of Antibacterial Gepotidacin Evaluated) was a phase 3, randomised, multicentre, double-blind, double-dummy, non-inferiority trial comparing oral [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) (1500 mg twice daily for 5 days) with [nitrofurantoin](../molecule/nitrofurantoin.md) (100 mg twice daily for 5 days) in adolescent and adult female patients with [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md). It uniquely collected pharmacokinetic data. After a prospectively agreed interim analysis, the study was stopped for efficacy; gepotidacin was non-inferior to nitrofurantoin (therapeutic success 50.6% vs 47.0%; adjusted difference 4.3%, 95% CI -3.6 to 12.1).

## Citations
- [Oral gepotidacin versus nitrofurantoin in patients with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38342126/) (PMID:38342126)
EAGLE-2 trial.description: Phase 3, randomised, multicentre, double-blind, double-dummy, non-inferiority trial comparing oral gepotidacin (1500 mg twice daily for 5 days) with nitrofurantoin (100 mg twice daily for 5 days) for uncomplicated urinary tract infection in adolescent and adult female patients.

edges.note: primary endpoint - combined clinical and microbiological success at test-of-cure
gepotidacin therapeutic success 162/320 (50.6%) vs nitrofurantoin 135/287 (47.0%); microbiological success 72.5% vs 67.6%; clinical success 65.6% vs 65.2%

EAGLE-3 trial.body:
# EAGLE-3 trial

EAGLE-3 (NCT04187144) was a phase 3, randomised, multicentre, double-blind, double-dummy, non-inferiority trial comparing oral [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) (1500 mg twice daily for 5 days) with [nitrofurantoin](../molecule/nitrofurantoin.md) (100 mg twice daily for 5 days) in adolescent and adult female patients with [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md). It was near-identical to EAGLE-2 but uniquely collected post-dose electrocardiograms. After a prospectively agreed interim analysis, the study was stopped for efficacy; gepotidacin was non-inferior and superior to nitrofurantoin (therapeutic success 58.5% vs 43.6%; adjusted difference 14.6%, 95% CI 6.4 to 22.8; one-sided p=0.0003 for superiority).

## Citations

EGFR (gene).body:
# EGFR (gene)

EGFR encodes the epidermal growth factor receptor. EGFR amplification and the constitutively active EGFRvIII variant are common oncogenic drivers in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md) and serve as therapeutic targets: the rindopepimut EGFRvIII vaccine (which showed no OS benefit in phase 3) and the antibody-drug conjugate [depatuxizumab mafodotin](../molecule/depatuxizumab-mafodotin.md) (also negative for OS in phase 3).

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
EGFR (gene).description: Gene encoding the epidermal growth factor receptor; EGFR amplification and the EGFRvIII variant are common oncogenic drivers in glioblastoma and targets for the vaccine rindopepimut and the antibody-drug conjugate depatuxizumab mafodotin.

edges.note: EGFR amplification and the constitutively active EGFRvIII variant are common in glioblastoma; targeted by rindopepimut vaccine and depatuxizumab mafodotin
depatux-m binds EGFRvIII and overexpressed wild-type EGFR; activity is seen in EGFR-amplified/EGFRvIII models, though phase 3 showed no OS benefit

EMBER trial.body:
# EMBER trial

EMBER (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04188548) is a global, open-label, first-in-human phase Ia/Ib study of [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md), an oral [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md), as monotherapy and in combination with targeted therapy (including [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) with or without an aromatase inhibitor, everolimus, or alpelisib). It used an i3+3 dose-escalation design (200-1,200 mg once daily, five dose levels) followed by dose-expansion cohorts. The ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer experience (PMID 39241211) reported 262 treated patients; the recommended phase II dose was determined to be 400 mg once daily.

At the RP2D, imlunestrant monotherapy achieved a median [progression-free survival](../biomedicalmeasure/progression-free-survival.md) of 7.2 months in heavily pretreated patients with [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md), with antitumor activity observed regardless of ESR1 mutation status.

## Citations
- [Imlunestrant, an Oral Selective Estrogen Receptor Degrader, as Monotherapy and in Combination With Targeted Therapy in ER-Positive, HER2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer: Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)

EMBER trial — endometrial cancer cohort.body:
# EMBER trial — endometrial cancer cohort

This is the recurrent/advanced [ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer](../disease/er-positive-endometrioid-endometrial-cancer.md) cohort of the phase 1a/1b [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md) (NCT04188548), reported in PMID 39442371. It evaluated [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) monotherapy and imlunestrant plus [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) (150 mg twice daily) in 72 patients with disease progression or recurrence after platinum-containing chemotherapy; all patients were CDK4/6 inhibitor-naive and prior fulvestrant or aromatase inhibitor was not allowed.

Among 39 patients who received imlunestrant monotherapy, ORR was 10.3%, CBR 33.3%, and median [progression-free survival](../biomedicalmeasure/progression-free-survival.md) 3.8 months; among 33 who received imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, ORR was 18.2%, CBR 42.4%, and median PFS 6.8 months. ESR1 mutations were rare in this cohort (2 of 72 patients).

## Citations
- [Imlunestrant, an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader, as monotherapy and combined with abemaciclib, in recurrent/advanced ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer: Results from the phase 1a/1b EMBER study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39442371/) (PMID:39442371)

EMBER-2 study.body:
# EMBER-2 study

EMBER-2 (NCT04647487) is a global, phase I, open-label, randomized preoperative window-of-opportunity study of oral [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) in postmenopausal women with untreated, operable [ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md). Patients were randomized to 400 versus 800 mg daily (with a later single-arm 200 mg cohort) for approximately 2 weeks before surgery, and pharmacodynamic biomarker changes were evaluated in paired pre-/post-treatment tumor samples.

Single-agent imlunestrant induced substantial [ER](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) degradation and PR downregulation (81% geometric mean decrease for both) and reduced [Ki-67](../biomedicalmeasure/ki-67.md) by ~71%, with similar biological effect at 400 and 800 mg. Combined with the EMBER trial data, EMBER-2 identified 400 mg as the optimal imlunestrant dose.

## Citations
- [A Preoperative Window-of-Opportunity Study of Oral SERD, Imlunestrant, in Newly Diagnosed ER-Positive, HER2-Negative Early Breast Cancer: Results from the EMBER-2 Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39377773/) (PMID:39377773)
EMBER-2 study.description: Global, multicountry, phase I, open-label, randomized preoperative window-of-opportunity study of oral imlunestrant (200, 400, or 800 mg daily for ~2 weeks before surgery) in postmenopausal women with untreated, operable ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, evaluating pharmacodynamic biomarker changes (ER, PR, Ki-67) in paired tumor samples.

edges.note: postmenopausal women with untreated, operable, stage I-III early breast cancer
secondary endpoint; change in Ki-67 index by IHC, surrogate of cell proliferation and complete cell-cycle arrest
primary endpoint - change in ER expression (IHC H-score) between pre- and post-treatment tumor samples
ER degradation across all dose levels (-82% at 400 mg, -70% at 800 mg, -89% at 200 mg); combined with EMBER established 400 mg as optimal dose

EMBER-3 trial.body:
# EMBER-3 trial

EMBER-3 (NCT04975308) is a phase 3, open-label trial that randomized 874 patients with [ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md) — whose disease recurred or progressed during/after aromatase inhibitor therapy (alone or with a CDK4/6 inhibitor) — in a 1:1:1 ratio to [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) (400 mg once daily), investigator's choice standard endocrine monotherapy (exemestane or [fulvestrant](../molecule/fulvestrant.md)), or imlunestrant plus [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) (150 mg twice daily).

Imlunestrant significantly improved [progression-free survival](../biomedicalmeasure/progression-free-survival.md) over standard therapy among patients with [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) mutations (restricted mean survival time difference 2.6 months; P<0.001) but not in the overall population (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.72-1.04; P=0.12). Imlunestrant-abemaciclib significantly improved PFS over imlunestrant alone (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.44-0.73; P<0.001), regardless of ESR1-mutation status.

## Citations
- [Imlunestrant with or without Abemaciclib in Advanced Breast Cancer (EMBER-3)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)
EMBER-3 trial.description: Phase 3, open-label trial (1:1:1 randomization) of imlunestrant, investigator's choice standard endocrine monotherapy (exemestane or fulvestrant), or imlunestrant plus abemaciclib in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that recurred or progressed during/after aromatase inhibitor therapy with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor (874 patients).

edges.note: investigator-assessed PFS was the primary endpoint for all three between-group comparisons
overall response was a secondary endpoint
imlunestrant vs standard therapy in overall population; median PFS 5.6 vs 5.5 months; not significant

EORTC 1608 STEAM trial.body:
# EORTC 1608 STEAM trial

EORTC 1608 (NCT03224104), known as STEAM, was a phase Ib, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter trial with a three-parallel-group design (A, B, C) evaluating the oral multi-CDK inhibitor [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) (TG02) in IDH-wildtype [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md). Groups A and B used a 3 + 3 design to determine the maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase II dose of TG02 in elderly patients combined with hypofractionated radiotherapy alone (group A, MGMT promoter unmethylated) or [temozolomide](../molecule/temozolomide.md) alone (group B, MGMT promoter methylated). Group C was a single-arm phase II evaluation of single-agent TG02 in recurrent disease with a primary endpoint of 6-month progression-free survival (PFS-6). The trial enrolled at 9 sites in 4 countries from June 2018 to July 2021; arms A and B were prematurely closed by the company, and arm C was fully enrolled (50 patients after amendment 3).

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
EORTC 1608 STEAM trial.description: A phase Ib, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter, three-parallel-group (A, B, C) trial of zotiraciclib (TG02) in IDH-wildtype newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly (groups A/B) or recurrent glioblastoma (group C), conducted at 9 sites in 4 countries with enrolment from June 2018 to July 2021.

edges.note: three-parallel-group phase Ib trial in IDH-wildtype newly diagnosed glioblastoma/anaplastic astrocytoma (groups A,B) and recurrent glioblastoma (group C)

ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer.body:
# ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer

ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer is the most common breast cancer subtype, accounting for roughly 70% of cases, and is driven by [estrogen receptor alpha](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) signaling. Endocrine therapy is the treatment foundation, often combined with [CDK4/6 inhibitors](../molecularclass/cdk4-6-inhibitors.md) or PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitors. Acquired activating [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) mutations are a predominant mechanism of endocrine resistance. [Imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) was evaluated across the disease spectrum — early (EMBER-2), advanced phase 1 (EMBER), and advanced phase 3 (EMBER-3) — as monotherapy and combined with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md).

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
- [EMBER-3 phase 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)
ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer.description: The most common subtype of breast cancer, driven by estrogen receptor signaling and lacking HER2 amplification; treated with endocrine therapy, often combined with CDK4/6, PI3K, AKT, or mTOR inhibitors, with ESR1 mutations a predominant mechanism of endocrine resistance.

edges.note: activating ESR1 mutations drive acquired endocrine-therapy resistance

ER-positive endometrioid endometrial can.body:
# ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer

ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer (EEC) is an estrogen receptor-driven subtype of endometrial cancer, most often low-to-intermediate grade. Standard treatment for metastatic disease includes platinum-based chemotherapy, immunotherapy (with or without lenvatinib), or endocrine therapy (progestins, aromatase inhibitors, tamoxifen, or [SERDs](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md)). In the EMBER endometrial cohort, [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) as monotherapy (median PFS 3.8 months) and combined with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) (median PFS 6.8 months) showed preliminary antitumor activity; [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) mutations were rare (2 of 72 patients).

## Citations
- [Phase 1a/1b EMBER study in ER+ endometrioid endometrial cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39442371/) (PMID:39442371)
ER-positive endometrioid endometrial can.description: An estrogen receptor-driven subtype of endometrial cancer, most often low-to-intermediate grade, treated with chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or endocrine therapy; ESR1 mutations are rare in this disease.

ESR1 (gene).body:
# ESR1 (gene)

ESR1 is the human gene encoding [estrogen receptor alpha](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) (ERα), a canonical driver of breast cancer progression. Acquired activating mutations of ESR1 — most frequently [Y537S](../variant/esr1-y537s.md) and [D538G](../variant/esr1-d538g.md) — confer ligand-independent constitutive ER activation and reduced sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors and other endocrine therapies, and are a predominant mechanism of endocrine-therapy resistance in [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md).

In the EMBER program, baseline ESR1 mutations (assessed by ctDNA) were enriched in heavily pretreated patients, and [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) showed antitumor activity regardless of ESR1 mutation status, with a more pronounced benefit over standard endocrine therapy in patients with ESR1 mutations in EMBER-3.

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
- [EMBER-3 phase 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)
ESR1 (gene).description: The human gene encoding estrogen receptor alpha (ERα); activating mutations (notably Y537S and D538G) are a predominant mechanism of acquired resistance to endocrine therapy in ER-positive breast cancer.

edges.note: activating ESR1 mutations linked to acquired endocrine-therapy resistance; detected in up to ~50% of ET-treated ER+/HER2- ABC and in 56% of imlunestrant RP2D patients at baseline

ESR1 D538G.body:
# ESR1 D538G

ESR1 D538G is an activating missense mutation in the [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) ligand-binding domain and, with [Y537S](../variant/esr1-y537s.md), one of the two most frequently occurring ESR1 mutations in metastatic ER-positive breast cancer. It confers ligand-independent constitutive [ERα](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) activation and reduced sensitivity to endocrine therapy including [fulvestrant](../molecule/fulvestrant.md). In an ESR1-D538G PDX model, [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) decreased tumor volume to a greater extent than fulvestrant, alone and combined with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md).

## Citations
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
ESR1 D538G.description: An activating missense mutation in ESR1 (ligand-binding domain) that confers ligand-independent constitutive ERα activation and reduced sensitivity to endocrine therapy; one of the two most frequently occurring ESR1 mutations in metastatic ER-positive breast cancer.

edges.note: missense substitution in the ESR1 ligand-binding domain
linked to acquired endocrine-therapy resistance, particularly to aromatase inhibitors; confers ligand-independent constitutive ERα activation
reduces sensitivity to fulvestrant; imlunestrant inhibited tumor growth to a greater extent than fulvestrant in an ESR1-D538G PDX model

ESR1 Y537S.body:
# ESR1 Y537S

ESR1 Y537S is an activating missense mutation in the [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) ligand-binding domain and, with [D538G](../variant/esr1-d538g.md), one of the two most frequently occurring ESR1 mutations in metastatic ER-positive breast cancer. It confers ligand-independent constitutive activation of [ERα](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) and reduced sensitivity to endocrine therapy including [fulvestrant](../molecule/fulvestrant.md). [Imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) retained high binding affinity (Ki 2.80 nM) and potent ERα degradation, transcriptional suppression, and antitumor activity in ESR1-Y537S cell lines and PDX models.

Ecallantide.body:
# Ecallantide

Ecallantide (Kalbitor, DX-88) is a recombinant protein that selectively and reversibly inhibits [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md). Administered subcutaneously, it is approved for on-demand treatment of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md) attacks and is effective in decreasing their severity and duration. As a [plasma kallikrein inhibitor](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md), it suppresses the pathogenetic mechanism of bradykinin overproduction during an attack.

## Citations
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Ecallantide.description: A recombinant protein that selectively and reversibly inhibits plasma kallikrein; approved for subcutaneous on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks.

edges.note: selectively and reversibly inhibits the activity of plasma kallikrein
approved for SC on-demand treatment of HAE attacks; effective in decreasing severity and duration of attacks

Efgartigimod.body:
# Efgartigimod

Efgartigimod is a humanized [IgG1](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) Fc fragment that blocks the [neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md), accelerating catabolism of circulating IgG including pathogenic autoantibodies. It is the first [FcRn blocker](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md) with RCT evidence in [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md): in the ADHERE study (subcutaneous efgartigimod alfa with hyaluronidase), it reduced the risk of relapse in stage B by 61% (HR 0.39; 95% CI 0.25-0.61), with stage A open-label improvements of ~7.7 points on I-RODS and 12.3 kPa on [grip strength](../biomedicalmeasure/grip-strength.md), though the placebo response was high.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Efgartigimod.description: A humanized IgG1 Fc fragment that blocks the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), accelerating catabolism of circulating IgG (including pathogenic autoantibodies); the first FcRn blocker shown in an RCT to reduce relapse in CIDP.

edges.note: a humanized IgG1 Fc fragment FcRn blocker (engineered Fc, in the FcRn-inhibitor class)
blocks the FcRn, reducing binding of endogenous (including pathogenic) IgG and negating FcRn protection from lysosomal degradation, shortening autoantibody serum lifespan
ADHERE study stage B; efgartigimod alfa significantly reduced risk of CIDP relapse by 61% vs placebo in previous responders; high placebo response (46% at wk24, 40% at wk48)

ADHERE stage A open-label improvements approached/reached published MCIDs: mean 7.7 points on I-RODS and 12.3 kPa on grip strength; 78% improvement rate in subjects receiving >=4 injections to reach full IgG-lowering effect
lowers serum IgG including pathogenic autoantibodies via FcRn blockade; full IgG-lowering effect reached after about 4 injections

Elacestrant.body:
# Elacestrant

Elacestrant is a next-generation oral [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md) approved for [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md) with [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) mutations, where it showed superiority over investigator's choice of endocrine therapy (HR 0.55). It is used as a comparator SERD against [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md); in preclinical studies imlunestrant produced greater ERα degradation and higher brain exposure and overall survival than elacestrant in an intracranial ER-positive breast cancer model.

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
Elacestrant.description: A next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader approved for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutant advanced breast cancer; a comparator SERD benchmarked against imlunestrant.

edges.note: approved for ER+/HER2-, ESR1-mutant ABC; demonstrated superiority vs investigator's choice ET in ESR1-mutant patients (HR 0.55; 95% CI 0.39 to 0.77; P=0.0005)

Endochondral ossification.body:
# Endochondral ossification

Endochondral ossification (endochondral bone formation) is the process by which cartilage is progressively replaced by bone to drive longitudinal skeletal growth. It depends on the proliferation and differentiation of [chondrocytes](../celltype/chondrocyte.md) in the growth plate. [FGFR3](../molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-receptor-3-protein.md) is a negative regulator of this process; gain-of-function FGFR3 variants in [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md) impair endochondral ossification by inhibiting chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation and extracellular matrix synthesis through the STAT1 and MAPK pathways. [Infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) is designed to relieve this inhibition.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Endochondral ossification.description: The process by which cartilage is progressively replaced by bone to drive longitudinal skeletal growth, dependent on the proliferation and differentiation of growth-plate chondrocytes; negatively regulated by FGFR3 and defective in achondroplasia.

Enmetazobactam.body:
# Enmetazobactam

Enmetazobactam (AAI-101) is a novel zwitterionic penicillanic acid sulfone [beta-lactamase inhibitor](../molecularclass/beta-lactamase-inhibitors.md) that inhibits class A [extended-spectrum beta-lactamases](../molecularclass/extended-spectrum-beta-lactamases.md). It has no intrinsic antibacterial activity but protects [cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) from degradation by serine beta-lactamases; the fixed-dose combination (EXBLIFEP) restores cefepime activity against ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria. Adding enmetazobactam 8 ug/mL lowered the cefepime MIC90 for the Enterobacteriaceae panel from 32 to 0.25 ug/mL (seven doubling dilutions). In the phase 3 ALLIUM trial for [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md), cefepime/enmetazobactam achieved a composite response of 79.1% versus 58.9% for piperacillin/tazobactam (difference 21.2%, 95% CI 14.3-27.9), meeting superiority.

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Enmetazobactam.description: A novel zwitterionic penicillanic acid sulfone beta-lactamase inhibitor that inhibits class A extended-spectrum beta-lactamases; combined in a fixed dose with the 4th-generation cephalosporin cefepime (EXBLIFEP) to restore activity against ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria.

edges.note: phase 3 ALLIUM (mMITT) - cefepime/enmetazobactam composite response (clinical cure + microbiological response) 79.1% vs 58.9% piperacillin/tazobactam (difference 21.2%, 95% CI 14.3-27.9); superiority met; clinical cure 92.5% vs 88.9%

stats.dose: cefepime 2 g / enmetazobactam 0.5 g IV every 8 h over 2 h for 7 days

edges.note: inhibits class A ESBLs (IC50 <1 uM for class A including KPC-2/KPC-3 in vitro); limited activity vs OXA-1 (IC50 1-10 uM); no activity vs class C, most class D, or class B (metallo) beta-lactamases
zwitterionic penicillanic acid sulfone beta-lactamase inhibitor; structurally similar to tazobactam but zwitterion enhances potency

adding enmetazobactam 8 ug/mL lowered cefepime MIC90 for the full Enterobacteriaceae panel by seven doubling dilutions (32 to 0.25 ug/mL); for ESBL-producing E. coli >64 to 0.12 ug/mL and K. pneumoniae >64 to 1.0 ug/mL; no enhancement vs P. aeruginosa (MIC90 16 ug/mL)

most frequent adverse reactions in ALLIUM (cefepime/enmetazobactam vs piperacillin/tazobactam): increased transaminases 20% vs 20%, increased bilirubin 7% vs 4%, headache 5% vs 2%, phlebitis/infusion-site reactions 5% vs <1%, diarrhoea 4% vs 5%

Entrectinib.body:
# Entrectinib

Entrectinib (RXDX-101) is an oral, blood-brain-barrier-penetrant selective inhibitor of TRK (NTRK) and ROS1 kinases, approved by the FDA and EMA for tumors with NTRK or ROS1 fusions. In [glioma](../disease/glioma.md), it achieved a 79% objective response rate across solid tumors including CNS tumors, and the STARTRK-NG trial reported positive radiographic responses in four pediatric high-grade glioma patients harboring NTRK/ROS1 fusions; further work on CNS penetrance and resistance is needed.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Entrectinib.description: An oral, blood-brain-barrier-penetrant selective inhibitor of TRK (NTRK) and ROS1 tyrosine kinases, approved for tumors harboring NTRK or ROS1 fusions and explored in NTRK/ROS1-fusion pediatric high-grade glioma.

edges.note: 79% objective response rate across various solid tumors including CNS tumors; STARTRK-NG trial reported positive radiographic responses in four pediatric high-grade glioma patients with NTRK/ROS1 fusions

Erdosteine.body:
# Erdosteine

Erdosteine (trademark Erdotin) is a novel oral thiol-derivative [mucoactive (mucolytic) agent](../molecularclass/mucoactive-agents.md). It was synthesised to overcome the non-efficacy and toxicity problems associated with increased circulating free thiols seen with other thiols such as N-acetylcysteine; its free sulfhydryl group resides in the active metabolite. Erdosteine has four main properties: it is a mucoactive agent (modulating mucus production and viscosity and increasing mucociliary transport), an antioxidant, an airway anti-inflammatory, and it confers bacterial anti-adherence. It is licensed in around 40 countries (orphan drug status in the USA).

In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md), erdosteine 225 mg twice daily added to [chest physiotherapy](../methodorprocedure/chest-physiotherapy.md) gave physiologic and mucus-clearance benefits in elderly patients with [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) and [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md). The [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md) protocol plans to test whether 12 months of erdosteine reduces the [pulmonary exacerbation rate](../biomedicalmeasure/pulmonary-exacerbation-rate.md) versus placebo. Cited evidence in adults with [COPD](../disease/chronic-obstructive-pulmonary-disease.md) or chronic bronchitis shows erdosteine reduced exacerbations by 35% and hospitalisation by 44%.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Erdosteine.description: A novel oral thiol-derivative mucoactive (mucolytic) agent whose free sulfhydryl (SH) group in its active metabolite confers mucoactive, antioxidant, airway anti-inflammatory and bacterial anti-adherence properties.

edges.note: a thiol-derivative mucoactive (mucolytic) agent
described as a novel oral mucoactive agent with additional antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-microbial properties

BETTER trial protocol - planned/hypothesised 40% reduction in acute respiratory exacerbation rate vs placebo; efficacy not yet reported

stats.dose: 300 mg (or weight-based suspension) twice daily for 12 months

edges.note: cited meta-analysis of 10 RCTs - erdosteine vs placebo reduced exacerbations by 35% and hospitalisation by 44% in adults with COPD or chronic bronchitis
improves sputum rheology, increases mucociliary clearance and transport (reduces mucus density and purulence, increases expectorated volume)
primary hypothesis - regular erdosteine over 12 months will yield fewer acute respiratory exacerbations than placebo in children and adults with bronchiectasis

Erenumab.body:
# Erenumab

Erenumab (Aimovig; AMG 334) is a human IgG2 [monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-cgrp-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that binds and blocks the [CGRP receptor](../molecule/cgrp-receptor-protein.md). Unlike [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md), which neutralize the [CGRP ligand](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md), erenumab acts at the receptor.

In the prospective [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md), erenumab (140 mg monthly) was given to 7 of 50 [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) patients, contributing to an overall 90% rate of >=50% reduction in vertigo frequency, with no statistically significant efficacy difference between the three antibodies tested.

Escherichia coli.body:
# Escherichia coli

Escherichia coli (including uropathogenic E. coli) is the Gram-negative bacillus that is the primary uropathogen in [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md), causing more than 75% of uncomplicated UTIs and 90% of qualifying uropathogens in the EAGLE trials. [Gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) retains activity against it including ESBL-producing, fluoroquinolone-resistant, and multidrug-resistant strains (MIC90 2-4 mg/L).

Estrogen receptor alpha (protein).body:
# Estrogen receptor alpha (protein)

Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) is a nuclear hormone receptor encoded by [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md) and a canonical driver of [ER-positive breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md). On ligand binding it drives ER-dependent gene transcription and tumor cell proliferation. [Imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md), a pure ERα antagonist and [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md), binds the ERα ligand-binding domain with high affinity (Ki 0.64 nM wild-type, 2.80 nM Y537S) and induces proteasome-mediated ERα degradation, suppressing ERα signaling in both ESR1 wild-type and mutant disease.

## Citations
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
