Estrogen receptor alpha (protein).description: A nuclear hormone receptor responsive to estrogen, encoded by ESR1, and a canonical driver of ER-positive breast cancer; the molecular target degraded and antagonized by imlunestrant and other selective estrogen receptor degraders.

edges.note: canonical driver of ER+ breast cancer initiation and progression; ER positivity is a biomarker of imlunestrant sensitivity

Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.body:
# Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases

Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) are a family of predominantly class A bacterial serine beta-lactamase enzymes (CTX-M, SHV, TEM, and VEB groups) that hydrolyze extended-spectrum cephalosporins and confer resistance in Gram-negative bacteria. ESBL-mediated resistance is a growing global threat, and treatment options are limited and usually require carbapenems. [Enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that targets class A ESBLs, restoring [cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) activity against ESBL-producing organisms such as [Escherichia coli](../organism/escherichia-coli.md) and [Klebsiella pneumoniae](../organism/klebsiella-pneumoniae.md) in [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md).

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.description: A family of (predominantly class A) bacterial serine beta-lactamase enzymes that hydrolyze extended-spectrum cephalosporins and confer resistance in Gram-negative bacteria; the molecular target of the inhibitor enmetazobactam.

edges.note: ESBLs (CTX-M, SHV, TEM, VEB groups) mediate antimicrobial resistance in Gram-negative uropathogens; treatment options are limited and usually require carbapenems

F9 (gene).body:
# F9 (gene)

F9 is an X-chromosomal human gene that [encodes](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md) blood [coagulation factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md). Dysfunction or deficiency of F9 causes [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md), with point mutations and deletions making up most pathogenic variants. The naturally occurring gain-of-function R338L (Padua) substitution in F9 yields the high-activity [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) variant delivered by [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md).

## Citations

F9 (gene).description: X-chromosomal human gene encoding blood coagulation factor IX; dysfunction or deficiency of F9 causes hemophilia B, and the gain-of-function R338L (Padua) substitution yields a high-activity factor IX variant.

edges.note: F9 codes for the blood coagulation factor IX (FIX)
hemophilia B is caused by a dysfunction or deficiency in the F9 gene; point mutations account for 76% and deletions for 17% of pathogenic variants

FCGRT (gene).body:
# FCGRT (gene)

FCGRT is a ~14 kb gene on the long arm of chromosome 19 that [encodes](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) the alpha subunit of the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md). Variable-number-tandem-repeat (VNTR) promoter polymorphisms (VNTR1-5) modulate FcRn expression: the common VNTR3 allele raises promoter activity and FcRn levels, whereas the minor [VNTR2](../variant/fcgrt-vntr2.md) allele is associated with reduced expression and has been linked to variable [IVIg](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md) response in neuroimmune disease. A phase 1 study in Japanese volunteers found FCGRT highly conserved across diverse populations, with no Japanese-specific variants altering the FcRn IgG-binding site targeted by [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md).

## Citations
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
- [Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Nipocalimab in Healthy Japanese Volunteers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39073504/) (PMID:39073504)
FCGRT (gene).description: Human gene on the long arm of chromosome 19 (~14 kb) encoding the alpha subunit of the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn); variable-number-tandem-repeat (VNTR) promoter polymorphisms (VNTR1-5) and rare coding variants modulate FcRn expression.

edges.note: FCGRT encodes the FcRn alpha subunit, which contains the majority of the IgG binding site
VNTR promoter polymorphisms alter FcRn mRNA/protein expression; VNTR3 (most common) increases promoter activity and FcRn level in VNTR3/3 homozygotes vs VNTR2 carriers
in myasthenia gravis (Su et al., n=334) VNTR2/3 patients had lower endogenous IgG and poorer IVIg response than VNTR3/3; VNTR genotype may affect duration of infused IgG and IVIg effectiveness

FCGRT VNTR2.body:
# FCGRT VNTR2

FCGRT VNTR2 is a minor variable-number-tandem-repeat polymorphism in the [FCGRT](../gene/fcgrt-gene.md) promoter (~3.2% of Japanese, ~7.5% of Caucasian individuals) that reduces [FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) expression relative to the common VNTR3 allele. It has been associated with variable reports of decreased [IVIg](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md) response and altered therapeutic-antibody pharmacokinetics, notably poorer IVIg response in VNTR2/3 myasthenia gravis patients. Because VNTR2 does not alter the FcRn protein sequence or its IgG-binding site, [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) is expected to retain activity in VNTR2 carriers.

FGFR inhibitors.body:
# FGFR inhibitors

FGFR inhibitors are a class of agents that inhibit fibroblast growth factor receptors. Selective FGFR inhibitors with demonstrated efficacy in FGFR-altered cancers (e.g. cholangiocarcinoma and bladder/urothelial carcinoma) have been repurposed, at substantially lower doses, to target [FGFR3](../molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-receptor-3-protein.md) overactivity in [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md). [Infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md), an FGFR1-3 selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is a member of this class and the first orally administered FGFR inhibitor to be studied in children with achondroplasia.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
FGFR inhibitors.description: A class of agents that inhibit fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFR1-4); selective FGFR inhibitors are used in FGFR-altered cancers and, at low doses, are being investigated to counteract FGFR3 overactivity in achondroplasia.

FGFR3 (gene).body:
# FGFR3 (gene)

FGFR3 is the human gene encoding [fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3)](../molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-receptor-3-protein.md), a receptor tyrosine kinase that acts as a negative regulator of [endochondral bone formation](../biologicalpathway/endochondral-ossification.md) and is particularly prevalent on the surface of [chondrocytes](../celltype/chondrocyte.md). Gain-of-function (activating) pathogenic variants in FGFR3 cause [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md) by inhibiting chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation.

Most cases of achondroplasia result from a G-to-A or G-to-C substitution at nucleotide position 1138, both of which yield the same [Gly380Arg (G380R)](../variant/fgfr3-g380r.md) amino-acid substitution in the transmembrane domain; about 80% of affected individuals carry a de novo event. [Infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) is being developed to counteract the resulting FGFR3 overactivity.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
FGFR3 (gene).description: Human gene encoding fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3), a receptor tyrosine kinase that is a negative regulator of endochondral bone formation; gain-of-function pathogenic variants in FGFR3 cause achondroplasia.

edges.note: FGFR3 is a receptor tyrosine kinase and a negative regulator of endochondral bone formation, particularly prevalent on the surface of chondrocytes

FGFR3 G380R.body:
# FGFR3 G380R

FGFR3 G380R (p.Gly380Arg) is the recurrent activating (gain-of-function) missense substitution in the transmembrane domain of [FGFR3](../gene/fgfr3-gene.md) that causes the great majority of [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md) cases. It arises from either a G-to-A or a G-to-C substitution at nucleotide position 1138, both of which produce the same glycine-to-arginine change at codon 380. About 80% of affected individuals carry a de novo event. The resulting constitutively active FGFR3 inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation, the mechanism that [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) is designed to counteract.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)

FIX-R338L field study 2024.body:
# FIX-R338L field study 2024

This international, multisite field study used one central analytical laboratory and 18 local laboratories in 13 countries to characterize the activity of the high-activity factor IX variant [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) in plasma from [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md)-treated participants of a phase 1/2a [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md) trial (NCT02484092). [Factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) was higher with the one-stage silica-based SynthASil assay than with the one-stage ellagic acid Actin FSL or chromogenic Rox FIX assays, with variation greatest at the lowest activity levels. Activated FIX (FIXa) was not detected in participant plasma, and spiked-in exogenous replacement FIX was additive to endogenous FIX-R338L.

## Citations
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)

FXN (gene).body:
# FXN (gene)

FXN encodes [frataxin](../molecule/frataxin-protein.md), a mitochondrial protein essential for iron-sulfur cluster assembly. Loss-of-function mutations cause [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md); the resulting frataxin deficiency produces mitochondrial dysfunction underlying the disease's neurodegeneration, cardiomyopathy, diabetes mellitus and skeletal deformities. Many disease-modifying strategies aim to raise frataxin levels or counter mitochondrial dysfunction.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
FXN (gene).description: Gene encoding frataxin, a mitochondrial protein involved in iron-sulfur cluster assembly; loss-of-function mutations (typically GAA repeat expansions) cause Friedreich ataxia.

edges.note: FXN encodes frataxin, involved in mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly
FXN mutations cause FRDA; frataxin deficiency leads to mitochondrial dysfunction, neurodegeneration, cardiomyopathy, diabetes and skeletal deformities

Factor IX R338L (Padua).body:
# Factor IX R338L (Padua)

Factor IX R338L (FIX-Padua) is a naturally occurring gain-of-function missense substitution (leucine for arginine at position 338) in the [F9](../gene/f9-gene.md)-encoded [coagulation factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md) protein. It circulates at normal antigenic levels but exhibits roughly 8- to 12-fold higher coagulant activity than non-mutant FIX, an enhancement dependent on its interaction with activated factor VIII and factor X in the tenase complex. It is the high-activity transgene delivered by [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md). Its [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) reads higher on one-stage silica (SynthASil) assays than on ellagic acid (Actin FSL) or chromogenic assays, especially at low activity levels.

## Citations
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Factor IX R338L (Padua).description: Naturally occurring gain-of-function missense substitution (leucine for arginine at position 338) in the F9-encoded factor IX protein; circulates at normal antigenic levels but exhibits approximately 8- to 12-fold higher coagulant activity than non-mutant factor IX, and is the transgene delivered by fidanacogene elaparvovec.

edges.note: high-activity variant of human FIX protein, differing from wild-type by replacement of arginine with leucine at position 338

confers approximately eightfold increased activity versus wild-type FIX (Dhillon report: 8- to 12-fold); enhanced activity depends on interaction with FVIIIa and FX on phospholipid surfaces in the tenase complex. Measured FIX-R338L activity is higher with OS silica SynthASil than OS ellagic acid Actin FSL; SynthASil/Actin FSL ratio 4.34 at lowest activity (low 1, 0.025 IU/mL) and 1.84 at normal activity; variability greatest at lowest activity levels and larger than for wild-type FIX (ratios 1.79 low, 1.16 normal)

Factor IX activity.body:
# Factor IX activity

Factor IX activity is the functional clotting activity of [coagulation factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md) in plasma, expressed as a percentage of normal or in IU/mL, and is the key measure for diagnosing and grading [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md) severity and monitoring response to [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md). It is measured by one-stage clotting (aPTT-based, e.g. SynthASil, Actin FSL) and chromogenic substrate assays. For the high-activity [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) variant, measured activity varies by assay and reagent, with the one-stage silica SynthASil assay consistently reading higher than ellagic acid Actin FSL and chromogenic assays, especially at low activity levels.

## Citations
- [Field Study and Correlative Studies of Factor IX Variant FIX-R338L in Participants Treated with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38863155/) (PMID:38863155)
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
Factor IX activity.description: Functional clotting activity of coagulation factor IX in plasma, expressed as a percentage of normal or in IU/mL (IU/dL), measured by one-stage clotting (aPTT-based) assays or chromogenic substrate assays; used to diagnose and grade hemophilia B severity and to monitor response to factor IX replacement or gene therapy.

edges.note: severity grading (severe <1%, moderate 1-5%, mild >5-40% of normal); accurate FIX activity assays are key for diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring; no international standard exists for FIX-R338L activity measurement

one-stage (aPTT) assays calibrate against an international wild-type FIX plasma standard; CS assays use purified factor components; values for FIX-R338L vary by assay/reagent, with OS silica (SynthASil) reading higher than OS ellagic acid (Actin FSL) and chromogenic assays, most pronounced at low activity

Farkas 2024 — kallikrein inhibitors for.body:
# Farkas 2024 — kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema

This review (Expert Opin Investig Drugs 2024;33:191-200) summarizes preclinical and early-phase clinical results of newer drugs targeting the dysregulated kinin-kallikrein system in [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md), a bradykinin-mediated disorder driven by unregulated activation of [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md). Agents covered include the oral plasma kallikrein inhibitors ATN-249, KVD-824, and [sebetralstat](../molecule/sebetralstat.md); the long-acting monoclonal antibody STAR-0215; the antisense oligonucleotide [donidalorsen](../molecule/donidalorsen.md) (IONIS-PKKRx); and the in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), which inactivates the [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md) gene. Approved kallikrein-directed agents [lanadelumab](../molecule/lanadelumab.md), [berotralstat](../molecule/berotralstat.md), and [ecallantide](../molecule/ecallantide.md) are also discussed.

## Citations
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Farkas 2024 — kallikrein inhibitors for.description: Review of preclinical and early-phase clinical studies of newer drugs targeting the dysregulated kinin-kallikrein system in hereditary angioedema, covering plasma kallikrein inhibitors (ATN-249, KVD-824, sebetralstat, STAR-0215), the antisense oligonucleotide donidalorsen, and the gene-editing therapy NTLA-2002.

Fatigue.body:
# Fatigue

Fatigue is a common, predominantly grade 1-2 treatment-emergent adverse event of [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md), reported in 39.2% of patients at the recommended phase II dose in the [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md) and 22.6% in the imlunestrant arm of [EMBER-3](../study/ember-3-trial.md). It was the most common treatment-related adverse event with the 400 mg dose in the [EMBER-2 study](../study/ember-2-study.md).

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
Fatigue.description: A common, mostly low-grade treatment-emergent adverse event of imlunestrant characterized by persistent tiredness or lack of energy.

FcRn receptor occupancy.body:
# FcRn receptor occupancy

FcRn receptor occupancy is the fraction of the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) occupied by an anti-FcRn antibody, a target-engagement biomarker. [Nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) achieves greater than 90% FcRn occupancy within 2 h at 3 mg/kg, and PK/receptor-occupancy/PD modeling for the phase 3 [AZALEA](../study/azalea-study.md) study predicted that 45 mg/kg IV weekly maintains full FcRn occupancy in at least 96% of participants for at least 8 days. Receptor occupancy (with maternal serum IgG and alloantibody titers) is a prespecified PD endpoint.

## Citations
- [Design of a Phase 3 Study of Nipocalimab in Pregnancies at Risk for Severe HDFN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39197469/) (PMID:39197469)
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
FcRn receptor occupancy.description: The fraction of neonatal Fc receptor bound (occupied) by an anti-FcRn antibody; a target-engagement biomarker used to select and confirm the nipocalimab dose regimen and link drug exposure to IgG lowering.

edges.note: maternal monocyte FcRn receptor occupancy used as a PD/target-engagement biomarker

Fetal anemia.body:
# Fetal anemia

Fetal anemia is the central manifestation of [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md), caused by maternal anti-erythrocyte IgG alloantibodies crossing the placenta and hemolyzing fetal red cells. It is monitored noninvasively by middle cerebral artery Doppler peak systolic velocity (>=1.5 multiples of the median) and confirmed by cordocentesis, then treated by intrauterine transfusion. By lowering maternal IgG and blocking transplacental alloantibody transfer, [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) delayed or prevented fetal anemia in the [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) study.

## Citations

Fetal anemia.description: Reduced fetal hemoglobin/red-cell mass, the central manifestation of HDFN; monitored noninvasively by middle cerebral artery Doppler peak systolic velocity and treated with intrauterine transfusion.

Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (pro.body:
# Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (protein)

Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) is a receptor tyrosine kinase, encoded by the [FGFR3 gene](../gene/fgfr3-gene.md), that acts as a negative regulator of [endochondral bone formation](../biologicalpathway/endochondral-ossification.md). It is particularly prevalent on the surface of [chondrocytes](../celltype/chondrocyte.md), where its activation inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation and extracellular matrix synthesis through the STAT1 and MAPK signaling pathways.

Gain-of-function variants (notably [G380R](../variant/fgfr3-g380r.md)) produce a hyperactive FGFR3 that causes [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md). [Infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) is an FGFR1-3 selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor that binds and inhibits FGFR3 phosphorylation, reducing this overactivity.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (pro.description: A receptor tyrosine kinase that is a negative regulator of endochondral bone formation; its activation inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation via the STAT1 and MAPK pathways. The molecular target of infigratinib in achondroplasia.

edges.note: negative regulator of endochondral bone formation; signaling inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation and extracellular matrix synthesis
activated FGFR3 inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation through STAT1 and MAPK signaling pathways in chondrocytes
particularly prevalent on the surface of chondrocytes that give rise to cartilaginous bone
hyperactivity / overactivity of FGFR3 (from gain-of-function variants) is the pathophysiological cause of achondroplasia; infigratinib counteracts this overactivity

Fidanacogene elaparvovec.body:
# Fidanacogene elaparvovec

Fidanacogene elaparvovec (BEQVEZ, Durveqtix; PF-06838435, SPK-9001) is a single-stranded, non-replicating, recombinant [AAVRh74var vector](../molecule/aavrh74var-vector.md)-based [gene therapy](../molecularclass/gene-therapies.md) for [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md). It comprises a bioengineered AAVRh74var capsid and a liver-specific (ApoE/hAAT) expression cassette delivering a codon-optimized high-activity human coagulation factor IX variant, [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md), to [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md). In the phase 3 [BENEGENE-2 trial](../study/benegene-2-trial.md) a single 5x10^11 vg/kg infusion reduced the total [annualized bleeding rate](../biomedicalmeasure/annualized-bleeding-rate.md) by 71% and was superior to factor IX prophylaxis, with mean [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) of 26.9% at month 15. Increased aminotransferase levels were the most common adverse effect. It received its first approval in Canada on 27 December 2023.

## Citations

Fluoroquinolones.body:
# Fluoroquinolones

Fluoroquinolones (e.g. ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin) are synthetic antibacterials that inhibit bacterial type II topoisomerases by stabilizing double-strand DNA breaks. Unlike [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md), they contain a fluorine atom and a magnesium-chelating beta-keto acid structure and are associated with juvenile [arthropathy](../phenotype/arthropathy.md) and tendinopathy, restricting pediatric use. Gepotidacin's distinct binding mode confers activity against fluoroquinolone-resistant strains and avoids fluoroquinolone-like arthropathy.

## Citations
- [Novel Bacterial Topoisomerase Inhibitor Gepotidacin Demonstrates Absence of Fluoroquinolone-Like Arthropathy in Juvenile Rats](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36255258/) (PMID:36255258)
Fluoroquinolones.description: A class of synthetic antibacterial agents (e.g. ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin) that inhibit bacterial type II topoisomerases by stabilizing double-strand DNA breaks; contain a fluorine atom and a magnesium-chelating beta-keto acid structure, and are associated with arthropathy and tendinopathy.

edges.note: fluoroquinolones cause age-related arthropathy in weight-bearing joints of juvenile animals, restricting pediatric use

Forced expiratory volume in 1 second.body:
# Forced expiratory volume in 1 second

Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is a spirometric measure of airflow and lung function. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) of [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md), FEV1 improved significantly only in the [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) group (+0.2 L, p=0.02) and not with physiotherapy alone (0 L, NS); the between-group difference reached p=0.05. In the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), FEV1 (z-score / %predicted) and the FEV1/FVC ratio are secondary lung-function outcomes.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Forced expiratory volume in 1 second.description: The volume of air forcibly exhaled in the first second of a maximal expiration; a spirometric measure of airflow and lung function.

edges.note: spirometric lung-function outcome (forced lung volume)

Forced vital capacity.body:
# Forced vital capacity

Forced vital capacity (FVC) is a spirometric measure of lung volume. In the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) of [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md), FVC improved significantly only in the [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) group (+0.3 L, p=0.02) and not with physiotherapy alone (0 L, NS); the between-group difference reached p=0.05. In the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), FVC (z-score / %predicted) and the FEV1/FVC ratio are secondary lung-function outcomes.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Forced vital capacity.description: The total volume of air forcibly exhaled after a maximal inspiration; a spirometric measure of lung volume and function.

Frataxin (protein).body:
# Frataxin (protein)

Frataxin, encoded by [FXN](../gene/fxn-gene.md), is a mitochondrial matrix protein required for the assembly of iron-sulfur clusters. Deficiency of frataxin produces the mitochondrial dysfunction at the cellular level that drives the neurodegeneration, cardiomyopathy, diabetes and skeletal deformities of [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md). Because FRDA pathophysiology stems from this deficiency affecting multiple pathways, agents acting on a single downstream system (such as the d-serine pathway targeted by luvadaxistat) may have limited clinical benefit.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Frataxin (protein).description: A mitochondrial matrix protein required for the assembly of iron-sulfur clusters; its deficiency causes the mitochondrial dysfunction underlying Friedreich ataxia.

edges.note: frataxin is involved in assembly of iron-sulfur clusters in the mitochondrial matrix
frataxin (FXN) deficiency causes mitochondrial dysfunction leading to FRDA

Fremanezumab.body:
# Fremanezumab

Fremanezumab (Ajovy; TEV-48125) is a humanized IgG2 [monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-cgrp-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that binds the [calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md) ligand, neutralizing its activity (the same ligand-targeting mechanism as [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md), in contrast to the receptor-targeting [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md)).

In the prospective [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md), fremanezumab (225 mg monthly) was the most frequently used antibody, given to 25 of 50 [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) patients, contributing to an overall 90% rate of >=50% reduction in vertigo frequency, with no statistically significant efficacy difference between the three antibodies tested.

## Citations
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)

Friedreich ataxia.body:
# Friedreich ataxia

Friedreich ataxia (FRDA) is a rare hereditary disorder (affecting ~5000 individuals in the US) caused by mutations in the [FXN](../gene/fxn-gene.md) gene encoding [frataxin](../molecule/frataxin-protein.md). Frataxin deficiency impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly, producing mitochondrial dysfunction with progressive neurodegeneration ([limb ataxia](../phenotype/limb-ataxia.md), dysarthria, sensory neuropathy), cardiomyopathy, diabetes mellitus and skeletal deformities. No therapy is currently approved; the [luvadaxistat phase 2 trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md) was a proof-of-concept attempt to address the neurological component that did not demonstrate efficacy.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Friedreich ataxia.description: A rare hereditary disorder caused by FXN (frataxin) gene mutations, characterized by progressive neurodegeneration (limb ataxia, dysarthria, sensory neuropathy), cardiomyopathy, diabetes mellitus and skeletal deformities; no approved therapy exists.

edges.note: caused by mutations in the frataxin (FXN) gene; FXN deficiency impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly, causing mitochondrial dysfunction
prominent, highly penetrant neurological symptom along with dysarthria; includes sensory ataxia with loss of proprioception

Fulvestrant.body:
# Fulvestrant

Fulvestrant is the only [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md) broadly approved both as monotherapy and in combination for [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md). Its poor oral bioavailability necessitates intramuscular injection, which limits dose and dose-dependent efficacy, and its activity is limited in [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md)-mutant disease. It served as the principal comparator (standard endocrine therapy) in the phase 3 [EMBER-3 trial](../study/ember-3-trial.md) and as the benchmark for [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md)'s pharmacokinetics, ER degradation, and antitumor activity, which were superior in ESR1-mutant preclinical models.

## Citations
- [EMBER-3 phase 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
Fulvestrant.description: A first-generation selective estrogen receptor degrader requiring intramuscular administration; the broadly approved SERD for ER-positive advanced breast cancer used as the principal comparator and combination backbone against which imlunestrant is benchmarked.

edges.note: standard endocrine therapy comparator (most patients in the standard-therapy group, 292 of 330, received fulvestrant 500 mg); poorly soluble, not orally absorbed, requires intramuscular injection; efficacy limited in ESR1-mutant disease
prior reported ER reduction with fulvestrant in window-of-opportunity data, numerically less than the -81% with imlunestrant (cross-trial comparison)

GYRA (gene).body:
# GYRA (gene)

GYRA (gyrA) is the bacterial gene encoding the [GyrA protein](../gene/gyra-protein.md), the A subunit of [DNA gyrase](../biologicalfunction/dna-gyrase.md). Mutations in its quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR), such as GyrA S91F, D95A/G, and A92T, alter the [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) and fluoroquinolone binding site in [Neisseria gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md). The GyrA A92T substitution is associated with high-level gepotidacin resistance.

## Citations
- [Microbiological Analysis from a Phase 2 Randomized Study in Adults Evaluating Single Oral Doses of Gepotidacin in the Treatment of Uncomplicated Urogenital Gonorrhea](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30249694/) (PMID:30249694)
GYRA (gene).description: Bacterial gene encoding the A subunit (GyrA) of DNA gyrase; quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) mutations alter the gepotidacin and fluoroquinolone binding site.

Galcanezumab.body:
# Galcanezumab

Galcanezumab (Emgality; LY2951742) is a humanized IgG4 [monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-cgrp-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that binds the [calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md) ligand, neutralizing its activity. Approved for migraine prophylaxis, it has been investigated for [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md).

In the placebo-controlled [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md), galcanezumab reduced monthly [definite dizzy days](../biomedicalmeasure/definite-dizzy-days.md) by 11.3 versus 5.6 for placebo (difference -5.7 days; p=0.026; Cohen's d=1.02) and improved [DHI](../biomedicalmeasure/dizziness-handicap-inventory.md) and [VM-PATHI](../biomedicalmeasure/vm-pathi-score.md) scores more than placebo. In the [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md) it was one of three anti-CGRP antibodies given, with no significant efficacy differences between them. Only mild injection-site reactions were reported.

Gene therapies.body:
# Gene therapies

Gene therapies deliver genetic material, most often via adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors, to drive sustained endogenous production of a deficient protein. For [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md), a single-dose AAV gene therapy such as [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) delivers a [factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md) transgene to [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md), aiming to achieve long-term [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md) and reduce treatment burden compared with chronic factor IX concentrate prophylaxis.

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Gene therapies.description: Class of therapeutics that deliver genetic material (commonly via adeno-associated virus vectors) to provide sustained endogenous production of a deficient protein; for hemophilia B, single-dose AAV gene therapies deliver a factor IX transgene to hepatocytes to achieve long-term factor IX expression.

edges.note: gene therapy provides a prophylactic option in which sustained long-term FIX levels may be achieved after a single-dose infusion of a gene-delivery product

Generalized myasthenia gravis.body:
# Generalized myasthenia gravis

Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a chronic [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) autoantibody-mediated neuromuscular disease, most often driven by pathogenic anti-acetylcholine-receptor (AChR) antibodies (with IgG4 anti-MuSK antibodies in a minority). It is the indication in which [anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md) are most advanced: efgartigimod and rozanolixizumab are FDA-approved, and [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) was studied in the phase 2 Vivacity-MG trial, where it rapidly and dose-dependently reduced total IgG and anti-AChR autoantibodies with significant MG-ADL improvement.

## Citations
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
- [Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across infusion rates of intravenously administered nipocalimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38362023/) (PMID:38362023)
Generalized myasthenia gravis.description: A chronic IgG autoantibody-mediated neuromuscular disease, most commonly driven by pathogenic anti-acetylcholine-receptor (AChR) antibodies (and IgG4 anti-MuSK antibodies in a subset), in which FcRn blockade lowers pathogenic IgG and improves disease activity.

edges.note: driven by pathogenic anti-AChR IgG autoantibodies; ~7% of MG patients have IgG4 anti-MuSK antibodies

Gepotidacin.body:
# Gepotidacin

Gepotidacin (formerly GSK2140944) is a novel, bactericidal, first-in-class [triazaacenaphthylene antibiotic](../molecularclass/triazaacenaphthylene-antibiotics.md) and bacterial topoisomerase inhibitor. It inhibits bacterial DNA replication by a distinct mechanism, providing well-balanced dual inhibition of two type II topoisomerase enzymes — DNA gyrase (via the [GyrA](../gene/gyra-gene.md) subunit) and topoisomerase IV (via the ParC subunit) — at a binding site distinct from that of fluoroquinolones, conferring activity against fluoroquinolone-resistant pathogens.

It is in clinical development for [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md) (1500 mg twice daily for 5 days) and [uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea](../disease/uncomplicated-urogenital-gonorrhoea.md) (two 3000 mg oral doses 10-12 h apart). In the phase 3 [EAGLE-2](../study/eagle-2-trial.md) and [EAGLE-3](../study/eagle-3-trial.md) trials it was non-inferior (and superior in EAGLE-3) to [nitrofurantoin](../molecule/nitrofurantoin.md) for uUTI.

## Citations

Glioblastoma.body:
# Glioblastoma

Glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype, WHO grade IV) is the most aggressive [glioma](glioma.md), defined by necrosis, microvascular endothelial proliferation and pronounced molecular heterogeneity. The standard of care for newly diagnosed disease is maximal safe surgery followed by radiotherapy with concomitant and adjuvant [temozolomide](../molecule/temozolomide.md); no agent has improved survival when added to temozolomide in that setting, and [MGMT](../gene/mgmt-gene.md) promoter methylation status strongly predicts temozolomide benefit.

The [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md) confirmed near-universal tumor expression of the [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) target [CDK-9](../molecule/cyclin-dependent-kinase-9-protein.md) and its downstream effectors [c-MYC](../molecule/myc-proto-oncogene-protein.md) and [MCL-1](../molecule/induced-myeloid-leukemia-cell-differentiation-protein-mcl-1-protein.md), with high MCL-1 associated with inferior survival.

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Glioblastoma.description: A highly aggressive WHO grade IV diffuse glioma characterized by necrosis, endothelial proliferation and molecular heterogeneity; standard of care for IDH-wildtype newly diagnosed disease is surgery followed by radiotherapy with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide.

edges.note: WHO grade IV glioma; highly aggressive with necrosis, endothelial proliferation and molecular heterogeneity
nuclear CDK-9 expression in 102/105 tumors; 90/105 (86%) immunoreactive in >50% of tumor cells
nuclear c-MYC expression in 81/102 tumors, more heterogeneous than CDK-9; CDK-9 correlated with c-MYC (r=0.29, p=0.007)
cytoplasmic MCL-1 expression in 100/101 tumors; high MCL-1 (>8 by median split) associated with inferior OS from surgery (27.4 vs 15.2 months, p=0.06); CDK-9 correlated with MCL-1 (r=0.38, p=0.0004)
edges.object: Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1 (protein)

edges.note: MGMT promoter methylation is strongly predictive of benefit from temozolomide; unmethylated tumors respond poorly to temozolomide; central methylation-specific PCR guided group A (unmethylated) vs B (methylated) allocation
IDH-wildtype status confers increased risk; the STEAM trial enrolled IDH-wildtype glioblastoma

Glioma.body:
# Glioma

Gliomas are the most prevalent primary tumors of the central nervous system, with a general incidence of about 5.81 per 100,000. They arise from glial cells and are graded WHO I-IV: low-grade gliomas (LGG; e.g. pilocytic astrocytoma, diffuse astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma) generally carry a better prognosis than high-grade gliomas (HGG; anaplastic astrocytoma and [glioblastoma](glioblastoma.md)). Prognosis is shaped by molecular markers ([IDH1](../gene/idh1-gene.md), [EGFR](../gene/egfr-gene.md), MGMT) and the extent of surgical resection. The [glioma treatment review](../publication/glioma-treatment-review-2024.md) emphasizes a shift toward personalized and targeted therapies.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Glioma.description: The most prevalent primary tumors of the central nervous system, arising from glial cells and graded WHO I-IV; encompasses low-grade gliomas (e.g. pilocytic and diffuse astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma) and high-grade gliomas (anaplastic astrocytoma, glioblastoma).

edges.note: IDH-wildtype status is an adverse risk factor; IDH-mutant low-grade gliomas are targeted by IDH inhibitors such as vorasidenib
EGFR amplification and the EGFRvIII variant occur in glioblastoma and are targets for rindopepimut and depatuxizumab mafodotin

Glioma treatment review 2024.body:
# Glioma treatment review 2024

A comprehensive review of current and emerging treatment options for [glioma](../disease/glioma.md), with particular focus on low-grade glioma. It surveys immunotherapies (including the CDK9 inhibitor [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md), the viral immunotherapy [lerapolturev](../molecule/lerapolturev.md), and PD-1 inhibitors), targeted agents (the IDH inhibitor [vorasidenib](../molecule/vorasidenib.md), the TRK/ROS1 inhibitor [entrectinib](../molecule/entrectinib.md), the EGFR antibody-drug conjugate [depatuxizumab mafodotin](../molecule/depatuxizumab-mafodotin.md), and the imipridone [ONC201](../molecule/onc201.md)), radiation therapy (including proton therapy), surgical resection strategies, and cancer vaccines.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Glioma treatment review 2024.description: A comprehensive narrative review of current and emerging treatment options for glioma (with emphasis on low-grade glioma), covering immunotherapies, targeted agents, radiation therapy, surgical resection and cancer vaccines.

edges.note: review of immunotherapies, targeted therapies, radiotherapy, surgery and vaccines for low- and high-grade glioma

Grip strength.body:
# Grip strength

Grip strength is a quantitative measure of hand grip force used as a functional outcome in [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md) trials. In the ADHERE study of [efgartigimod](../molecule/efgartigimod.md), grip strength improved by a mean of 12.3 kPa in the open-label stage A, approaching the published minimal clinically important difference; it also improved with subcutaneous immunoglobulin and after autologous HSCT.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Grip strength.description: A quantitative measure of hand grip force used as a functional outcome in CIDP trials; improvements with efgartigimod and SCIg approached published minimal clinically important differences.

edges.note: outcome measure in CIDP; efgartigimod (ADHERE stage A) improved grip strength by a mean of 12.3 kPa, approaching/reaching the published minimal clinically important difference; also improved with SCIg and autologous HSCT

GyrA (protein).body:
# GyrA (protein)

GyrA is the A subunit of bacterial [DNA gyrase](../biologicalfunction/dna-gyrase.md), a type II topoisomerase. It is encoded by the [GYRA gene](../gene/gyra-gene.md) and is one of the two molecular targets of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md). Residue A92 (in the quinolone resistance-determining region) is critical for gepotidacin interaction; the GyrA A92T substitution causes high-level gepotidacin resistance, whereas A92P/S do not.

## Citations
- [In silico gepotidacin target mining among 33 213 global Neisseria gonorrhoeae genomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39004438/) (PMID:39004438)
GyrA (protein).description: The A subunit of bacterial DNA gyrase, a type II topoisomerase; the molecular target subunit to which gepotidacin binds, with quinolone resistance-determining region residues (e.g. A92) critical for gepotidacin interaction.

GyrA A92T.body:
# GyrA A92T

GyrA A92T is an amino acid substitution at residue A92 of the [GyrA](../molecule/gyra-protein.md) subunit of [Neisseria gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md) DNA gyrase. Combined with a pre-existing [ParC D86N](parc-d86n.md) substitution, it confers high-level [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) resistance (MIC >=32 ug/mL). It emerged at test-of-cure in two of three phase 2 microbiological-failure isolates. In silico mining of 33,213 global gonococcal genomes (1928-2023) found no A92T, indicating A92 is highly conserved; modelling suggests A92T forms a new polar contact with bound DNA that weakens gepotidacin binding.

## Citations
- [Microbiological Analysis from a Phase 2 Randomized Study in Adults Evaluating Single Oral Doses of Gepotidacin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30249694/) (PMID:30249694)
- [In silico gepotidacin target mining among 33 213 global Neisseria gonorrhoeae genomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39004438/) (PMID:39004438)
GyrA A92T.description: An amino acid substitution at residue A92 of the GyrA subunit of N. gonorrhoeae DNA gyrase that, combined with a pre-existing ParC D86N substitution, confers high-level gepotidacin resistance.

edges.note: emerged at test-of-cure in 2 microbiological-failure isolates (with pre-existing ParC D86N), gepotidacin MIC increased >=32-fold to >=32 ug/mL

GyrA S91F.body:
# GyrA S91F

GyrA S91F is an amino acid substitution at residue S91 of the [GyrA](../molecule/gyra-protein.md) subunit of [Neisseria gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md) DNA gyrase. It is the principal fluoroquinolone-resistance target mutation, most commonly co-occurring with D95A/G substitutions, and was present (with ParC D86N) in the fluoroquinolone-resistant isolates from gepotidacin phase 2 microbiological failures. It does not itself confer [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) resistance. In silico mining found GyrA S91 alterations in a large fraction of the 33,213 global gonococcal genomes.

## Citations
- [Microbiological Analysis from a Phase 2 Randomized Study in Adults Evaluating Single Oral Doses of Gepotidacin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30249694/) (PMID:30249694)
- [In silico gepotidacin target mining among 33 213 global Neisseria gonorrhoeae genomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39004438/) (PMID:39004438)
GyrA S91F.description: An amino acid substitution at residue S91 of the GyrA subunit of N. gonorrhoeae DNA gyrase; the principal fluoroquinolone-resistance target mutation, commonly co-occurring with D95 substitutions, and present in fluoroquinolone-resistant gepotidacin treatment-failure isolates.

edges.note: most prevalent GyrA alteration in 33,213 global genomes, usually combined with D95A (24.7%) or D95G (20.5%); main fluoroquinolone target

HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling.body:
# HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling

HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling is the oncogenic cascade driven by NRG1 in NRG1 fusion-positive cancers. [Neuregulin 1](../molecule/neuregulin-1-protein.md) (or an NRG1 fusion ligand) binds the pseudokinase [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md), promoting heterodimerization with [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md) (and EGFR/HER4). The partner receptor phosphorylates HER3, creating SH2-domain docking sites that activate the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway (and STAT signaling), culminating in cell proliferation and survival. [Zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) potently suppresses this pathway in NRG1 fusion-positive cells while sparing isogenic nonfusion controls, inducing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling.description: The oncogenic signaling cascade in which NRG1-bound HER3 heterodimerizes with HER2 (or EGFR/HER4), is phosphorylated, and activates the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway to drive tumor cell proliferation and survival.

edges.note: NRG1 fusions co-opt HER2-HER3 downstream growth and survival pathways (AKT, mTOR, STAT) to drive tumorigenesis

Headache.body:
# Headache

Headache was the most frequently reported treatment-emergent adverse event in the phase 1 infusion-rate study of IV [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md), occurring in 6 of 30 nipocalimab recipients (20%) versus 1 of 10 placebo recipients (10%). All headaches were grade 1 or 2, began 5-11 h after the start of infusion (none during infusion), and resolved; most were considered treatment-related.

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across infusion rates of intravenously administered nipocalimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38362023/) (PMID:38362023)
Headache.description: Pain in the head; the most frequently reported treatment-emergent adverse event in the phase 1 infusion-rate study of intravenous nipocalimab.

Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newbo.body:
# Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn

Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) is a rare, potentially life-threatening alloimmune disease in which transplacental transfer of maternal anti-erythrocyte [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) alloantibodies (e.g. anti-D, anti-K) causes progressive [fetal anemia](../phenotype/fetal-anemia.md), [hydrops fetalis](../phenotype/hydrops-fetalis.md), and fetal/neonatal death. Early-onset severe HDFN (at or before 24 weeks gestation) carries high morbidity and mortality and a high recurrence risk. Standard care is middle-cerebral-artery Doppler monitoring with high-risk intrauterine transfusions; [IVIg](../molecule/intravenous-immunoglobulin.md) has been used to delay transfusions with poor outcomes. [Nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) is the first noninvasive therapy in clinical development for HDFN, evaluated in the phase 2 [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) and phase 3 [AZALEA](../study/azalea-study.md) trials.

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
- [Design of a Phase 3 Study of Nipocalimab in Pregnancies at Risk for Severe HDFN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39197469/) (PMID:39197469)
Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newbo.description: A rare, potentially life-threatening alloimmune disease in which transplacental transfer of maternal anti-erythrocyte IgG alloantibodies (e.g. anti-D, anti-K) causes progressive fetal/neonatal hemolytic anemia, hydrops fetalis, and fetal or neonatal death; standard care is fetal-anemia monitoring with high-risk intrauterine transfusions.

edges.note: progressive fetal hemolytic anemia is the hallmark; severe early-onset HDFN occurs at <=24 weeks gestation
untreated severe fetal anemia progresses to hydrops fetalis and fetal loss

Hemophilia B.body:
# Hemophilia B

Hemophilia B is an X-linked recessive genetic bleeding disorder caused by dysfunction or deficiency of [coagulation factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md), encoded by the [F9 gene](../gene/f9-gene.md). Point mutations account for ~76% and deletions ~17% of pathogenic variants. Patients bleed mostly into muscles and joints, with severity graded by residual factor IX activity (severe <1%, moderate 1-5%, mild >5-40% of normal). Standard of care is prophylactic [factor IX concentrate](../molecularclass/coagulation-factor-ix-concentrates.md) replacement, while [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) offers a single-dose gene-therapy alternative.

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
Hemophilia B.description: X-linked recessive genetic bleeding disorder caused by dysfunction or deficiency of coagulation factor IX (encoded by F9), characterized by excessive bleeding mostly into muscles and joints; severity is graded by residual factor IX activity (severe <1%, moderate 1-5%, mild >5-40% of normal).

edges.note: caused by dysfunction or deficiency of the F9 gene encoding coagulation factor IX; point mutations account for 76% and deletions for 17% of pathogenic variants
deficiency or dysfunction of coagulation factor IX is the underlying cause; disease severity tracks residual FIX activity (severe <1%, moderate 1-5%, mild >5-40% of normal)
recurrent joint bleeding leads to target joints and joint damage; 13/45 (29%) BENEGENE-2 participants had target joints at baseline

Hepatitis B surface antigen level.body:
# Hepatitis B surface antigen level

Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) level is the serum concentration of HBsAg, the key biomarker of [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). Sustained HBsAg loss (level below 0.05 IU/mL) is a component of functional cure and was the primary efficacy end point of the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md). Notably, HBsAg loss with or without seroconversion occurred only in participants who had a screening HBsAg level below 1000 IU/mL — among whom [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) plus [peginterferon alfa-2a](../molecule/peginterferon-alfa-2a.md) achieved 47% HBsAg loss and 40% seroconversion at 24 weeks after end of treatment.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Hepatitis B surface antigen level.description: The serum concentration of hepatitis B surface antigen, the key biomarker of chronic hepatitis B; sustained HBsAg loss (level <0.05 IU/mL) is a component of functional cure and the primary efficacy end point in HBV antiviral trials.

edges.note: HBsAg loss (<0.05 IU/mL) and seroconversion are the central efficacy outcomes; HBsAg loss occurred only in participants with screening HBsAg <1000 IU/mL

Hepatitis B virus.body:
# Hepatitis B virus

Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is an enveloped, partially double-stranded DNA virus of the family Hepadnaviridae that infects [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md) and causes [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). Chronic infection affects nearly 300 million people worldwide and increases the risk of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and premature death. [Xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) is a small interfering RNA that targets the conserved S region of the HBV genome to silence multiple HBV transcripts and lower hepatitis B surface antigen.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Hepatitis B virus.description: An enveloped, partially double-stranded DNA virus of the family Hepadnaviridae that infects hepatocytes and causes acute and chronic hepatitis B; chronic infection affects nearly 300 million people worldwide and increases the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

edges.note: chronic HBV infection affects nearly 300 million people worldwide and raises the risk of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and premature death

Hepatocyte.body:
# Hepatocyte

Hepatocytes are the principal parenchymal cells of the liver and the primary site of production of plasma prekallikrein (encoded by [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md)), [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md), factor XII, and high-molecular-weight kininogen, as well as [coagulation factor IX](../molecule/coagulation-factor-ix-protein.md). This central role makes them the cellular target of hepatic-directed prophylactic therapies for [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md) is taken up by hepatocytes via low-density-lipoprotein-receptor-mediated endocytosis of its lipid nanoparticle, after which CRISPR-Cas9 editing of KLKB1 occurs; preclinical data indicate the edits persist through hepatocyte turnover (~19% replaced per year in healthy human liver). For [hemophilia B](../disease/hemophilia-b.md), [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md) drives hepatocyte-specific expression of the [Factor IX R338L (Padua)](../variant/factor-ix-r338l-padua.md) transgene via a liver-specific ApoE/hAAT promoter.

## Citations
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Hepatocyte.description: The principal parenchymal cell of the liver and the primary site of production of plasma prekallikrein, C1 esterase inhibitor, factor XII, and high-molecular-weight kininogen, as well as coagulation factor IX; the cellular target of hepatic-directed therapies including NTLA-2002 for hereditary angioedema and fidanacogene elaparvovec for hemophilia B.

hepatocytes are the site of coagulation factor IX synthesis; in a monkey biodistribution study the liver had the highest fidanacogene elaparvovec vector DNA concentration (20-fold over spleen)
hepatocytes are the main source of circulating transthyretin and the site of TTR knockout by nexiguran ziclumeran

Hereditary angioedema.body:
# Hereditary angioedema

Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare, autosomal dominant genetic disorder affecting approximately 1 in 50,000 persons, characterized by recurrent, unpredictable, and potentially fatal episodes of swelling primarily affecting the gastrointestinal tract, cutaneous and submucosal tissues, and upper airway. Symptoms result from dysregulation of the contact (kallikrein-kinin) activation pathway: deficiency or dysfunction of [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md) (caused predominantly by [SERPING1](../gene/serping1-gene.md) variants) leads to unchecked activity of factor XIIa and [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md), generating excess bradykinin and increased vascular permeability. Type 1 (~85% of cases) reflects quantitative C1INH deficiency and type 2 (~15%) reflects C1INH dysfunction. Investigational hepatic-targeted and kallikrein-directed therapies, including [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), aim to provide long-term prophylaxis against [angioedema attacks](../phenotype/angioedema-attack.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)

edges.note: caused predominantly by SERPING1 variants leading to C1INH deficiency (type 1, ~85%) or dysfunction (type 2, ~15%)
recurrent painful swelling of GI tract, cutaneous and submucosal tissues; laryngeal edema can be life-threatening

Hollow-fibre infection model.body:
# Hollow-fibre infection model

The hollow-fibre infection model is an in vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic system that simulates dynamic human drug exposures against bacteria over time. It was used to define the [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) resistance-suppression PK/PD target (fAUC/MIC of 46) against a [Neisseria gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md) isolate carrying a ParC D86N mutation, confirming that total daily doses of >=4500 mg (two 3000 mg doses 8 or 12 h apart) prevented amplification of a gepotidacin-resistant subpopulation, informing the phase III dosing regimen.

## Citations

Hollow-fibre infection model.description: An in vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic system that simulates dynamic human drug exposures against bacteria; used to define the gepotidacin exposure (fAUC/MIC) needed to suppress amplification of resistant N. gonorrhoeae subpopulations.

Hydrops fetalis.body:
# Hydrops fetalis

Hydrops fetalis is the abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments. In [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md) it results from severe untreated [fetal anemia](../phenotype/fetal-anemia.md) and signals a high risk of fetal loss. No cases of fetal hydrops occurred among the 13 [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md)-treated pregnancies in the [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) study, versus hydrops in 54% of the most recent qualifying pregnancies; avoidance of hydrops fetalis is part of the [AZALEA](../study/azalea-study.md) composite primary endpoint.

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
Hydrops fetalis.description: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments; in HDFN it results from severe untreated fetal anemia and signals a high risk of fetal loss.

Hyperglycemia.body:
# Hyperglycemia

Hyperglycemia (worsened glycemic control) is elevated blood glucose reflected by increased glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). In the [ARCHES-2 trial](../study/arches-2-trial.md), a transient increase in HbA1c was observed mainly in patients with preexisting diabetes who received the highest [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) dose (mean change +0.38% vs -0.03% with placebo at week 24), with more adverse events related to glycemic control, excursions into the diabetic range, and use of additional antidiabetic therapy at 200 mg; levels returned toward baseline by trial end, and there was no change in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). Concern that this is an on-target effect is mitigated by the increased insulin sensitivity of ANGPTL3 loss-of-function homozygotes.

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
Hyperglycemia.description: Elevated blood glucose / worsened glycemic control, reflected by increased glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c); observed as a transient, dose-dependent effect of zodasiran in patients with preexisting diabetes.

Hyperphosphatemia.body:
# Hyperphosphatemia

Hyperphosphatemia is an elevated serum phosphorus concentration and the most common on-target toxicity of [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) (and FGFR inhibition generally) at the higher doses used in oncology. Because doses in [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md) are 10-100-fold lower, this toxicity was largely absent in the [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md): only a single mild grade 1 case occurred (cohort 3, 0.064 mg/kg; phosphorus 6.2 mg/dL against an upper limit of normal of 6.0), which resolved after drug interruption and did not recur when treatment resumed at 0.032 mg/kg.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)

Hypoalbuminemia.body:
# Hypoalbuminemia

Hypoalbuminemia (reduced serum [albumin](../molecule/albumin.md)) is a mild, transient, asymptomatic on-target effect of [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md), because [FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) also recycles albumin. In the phase 1 infusion-rate study albumin fell at most ~8% (30 mg/kg) to ~15% (60 mg/kg) at Day 15, remaining within the normal range; in the [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) HDFN study no grade 3 hypoalbuminemia (albumin <20 g/L) occurred, and the albumin level trended back toward baseline after the last dose.

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across infusion rates of intravenously administered nipocalimab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38362023/) (PMID:38362023)

Hypoalbuminemia.description: Reduced serum albumin concentration; a mild, transient, asymptomatic on-target effect of FcRn blockade (FcRn also recycles albumin), graded as an adverse event of special interest in nipocalimab HDFN trials.

Hypofractionated radiotherapy.body:
# Hypofractionated radiotherapy

Hypofractionated radiotherapy delivers radiation in fewer, larger fractions over a shortened course (in the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md), 40 Gy in 15 fractions of 2.66 Gy over 3 weeks), an established option for elderly patients with [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md). In STEAM group A it was combined with [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) in MGMT-unmethylated elderly patients, with a maximum tolerated zotiraciclib dose of 150 mg twice weekly.

- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)

IDH1 (gene).body:
# IDH1 (gene)

IDH1 encodes cytosolic isocitrate dehydrogenase 1. Recurrent hotspot mutations confer neomorphic activity that produces the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate and define IDH-mutant [gliomas](../disease/glioma.md). IDH status is central to glioma classification and risk: IDH-wildtype is adverse, while IDH-mutant low-grade glioma is the target of [vorasidenib](../molecule/vorasidenib.md).

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)

edges.note: IDH-wildtype status is an adverse risk factor at diagnosis; IDH-mutant low-grade gliomas are targeted by IDH inhibitors such as vorasidenib (which lowers 2-hydroxyglutarate)

INCAT disability score.body:
# INCAT disability score

The Inflammatory Neuropathy Cause and Treatment (INCAT) disability score quantifies arm and leg disability and is a standard primary outcome for defining relapse in [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md) trials. It served as the relapse-defining endpoint in subcutaneous-immunoglobulin RCTs and was among the measures that improved significantly after [autologous HSCT](../methodorprocedure/autologous-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplantation.md).

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)

INVESTMENT trial.body:
# INVESTMENT trial

The INVESTMENT (Investigating Vestibular Migraine Emgality Treatment) trial was a single-site, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial (NCT04417361) conducted at a tertiary care vestibular clinic in San Francisco from October 2020 to March 2023. It tested whether [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md), a [CGRP](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md)-targeted monoclonal antibody, is effective for [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md). To the authors' knowledge it was the first controlled trial of a CGRP-blocking medication for vestibular migraine.

Forty participants (aged 18-75 with vestibular migraine or probable VM by Barany Society criteria) were randomized 1:1 to 3 months of galcanezumab (240 mg loading then 120 mg) or placebo; 38 were included in the modified intent-to-treat analysis (galcanezumab N=17, placebo N=21). Galcanezumab outperformed placebo on the primary VM-PATHI outcome and on secondary [DHI](../biomedicalmeasure/dizziness-handicap-inventory.md) and [definite dizzy day](../biomedicalmeasure/definite-dizzy-days.md) outcomes. The study, funded by Eli Lilly as an investigator-initiated trial, was terminated early when the sponsor stopped supplying study drug.

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
INVESTMENT trial.description: Single-site, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial (NCT04417361) of galcanezumab versus placebo for vestibular migraine, conducted in San Francisco from October 2020 to March 2023; the first controlled trial of a CGRP-targeted monoclonal antibody for vestibular migraine.

Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.body:
# Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease of unknown cause. Because [CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md)-driven macrophages may contribute to inflammation and fibrosis, IPF is an investigational indication for [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) (a phase 2 placebo-controlled trial, NCT06132256, is recruiting).

## Citations

IgG4-related disease.body:
# IgG4-related disease

IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a rare, chronic, relapsing, multiorgan, fibroinflammatory, immune-mediated disorder with a reported US prevalence of 5.3 per 100,000. It is characterized by the development of mass lesions rich in CD19+ [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md) that drive inflammation and fibrosis directly through cytokines or indirectly by activating pathogenic T cells, and is associated with oligoclonal expansions of [plasmablasts](../celltype/plasmablast.md) and elevated serum IgG4. Disease flares can lead to progressive organ dysfunction. There were no approved pharmacotherapies; glucocorticoids are standard but disease control is rarely maintained on tapering. The phase 3 [MITIGATE trial](../study/mitigate-trial.md) established the efficacy of CD19-targeted B-cell depletion with [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md).

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)

Imlunestrant.body:
# Imlunestrant

Imlunestrant (LY3484356) is a next-generation, brain-penetrant, oral [selective estrogen receptor degrader](../molecularclass/selective-estrogen-receptor-degraders.md) and pure [ERα](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) antagonist designed to deliver continuous ER target inhibition, including in [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md)-mutant breast cancer. It binds ERα with high affinity, induces proteasome-mediated ERα degradation, and suppresses ER-regulated gene transcription and cell proliferation regardless of ESR1 mutation status, with significant and sustained brain exposure in preclinical models.

In the phase Ia/Ib [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md), imlunestrant at the recommended phase II dose of 400 mg once daily achieved a median PFS of 7.2 months as monotherapy in pretreated [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md), and a window-of-opportunity study ([EMBER-2](../study/ember-2-study.md)) confirmed potent ER degradation (-81%) and [Ki-67](../biomedicalmeasure/ki-67.md) reduction (-71%), establishing 400 mg as the optimal dose. The phase 3 [EMBER-3 trial](../study/ember-3-trial.md) showed imlunestrant prolonged PFS over standard endocrine therapy in patients with ESR1 mutations, and imlunestrant plus [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) significantly improved PFS over imlunestrant alone (HR 0.57). Imlunestrant is also active as monotherapy and combined with abemaciclib in [ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer](../disease/er-positive-endometrioid-endometrial-cancer.md).

Immunoglobulin G.body:
# Immunoglobulin G

Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is the most abundant circulating antibody isotype (subclasses IgG1-IgG4). Its long ~21-day serum half-life depends on recycling by the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md), which it binds at acidic endosomal pH. Pathogenic IgG auto- and alloantibodies drive antibody-mediated diseases; in [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md), transplacental transfer of maternal antierythrocyte IgG alloantibodies causes fetal hemolytic anemia. [Nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) and other [anti-FcRn antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md) lower circulating IgG (including pathogenic IgG) by blocking FcRn-mediated recycling.

## Citations

- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)

Induced myeloid leukemia cell differenti.body:
# Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1 (protein)

MCL-1 is a short-lived anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 family. Because it is short-lived, it is depleted when transcription is blocked by [CDK-9](cyclin-dependent-kinase-9-protein.md) inhibition, making it an indirect downstream target of [zotiraciclib](zotiraciclib.md). In the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md), cytoplasmic MCL-1 was detected in 99% of [glioblastomas](../disease/glioblastoma.md), and high MCL-1 levels were associated with inferior overall survival from surgery (15.2 vs 27.4 months), supporting MCL-1 as a prognostic factor and candidate therapeutic target.

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)

Inebilizumab.body:
# Inebilizumab

Inebilizumab (Uplizna; inebilizumab-cdon; MEDI-551) is a humanized, affinity-optimised, afucosylated IgG1 kappa [monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-cd19-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that binds the [B-cell surface antigen CD19](../molecule/b-lymphocyte-antigen-cd19-protein.md) and depletes CD19-expressing [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md) through antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Because CD19 is expressed earlier than CD20 and persists on [plasmablasts](../celltype/plasmablast.md) and some plasma cells, inebilizumab depletes a broader range of B-lineage cells than anti-CD20 agents. The recommended dose is two single 300 mg intravenous infusions 2 weeks apart, then 300 mg every 6 months.

Originating from Duke University and developed by Viela Bio, inebilizumab received its first global approval on 11 June 2020 in the USA for AQP4-IgG seropositive [neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder](../disease/neuromyelitis-optica-spectrum-disorder.md), based on the pivotal N-MOmentum trial (time-to-attack hazard ratio 0.227 in the seropositive subgroup). In the phase 3 [MITIGATE trial](../study/mitigate-trial.md), inebilizumab reduced the risk of flares of [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md) by 87% (hazard ratio 0.13). Characteristic adverse effects include infusion reactions, infections (urinary tract infection), and cytopenias (neutropenia, lymphopenia).

# Inebilizumab First Approval (Frampton 2020)

This AdisInsight First Approval report summarizes the development of [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) (Uplizna; inebilizumab-cdon; MEDI-551), a humanized, afucosylated anti-CD19 IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody developed by Viela Bio. Infigratinib.body:
# Infigratinib

Infigratinib (BGJ398; NVP-BGJ398) is an orally bioavailable, small-molecule [FGFR1-3 selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor](../molecularclass/fgfr-inhibitors.md). It inhibits phosphorylation of [fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3)](../molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-receptor-3-protein.md) and attenuates its downstream signaling through the STAT1 and MAPK pathways, offering a direct strategy to counteract the FGFR3 overactivity that drives [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md). Originally developed for FGFR-altered cancers (cholangiocarcinoma, urothelial carcinoma) at doses up to 200 mg/day, it is used in achondroplasia at doses 10-100-fold lower.

In the phase 2 [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md), 72 children aged 3-11 years received once-daily oral infigratinib across five ascending dose cohorts. A dose-dependent increase in [annualized height velocity](../biomedicalmeasure/annualized-height-velocity.md) was seen; at the highest dose (0.25 mg/kg/day, cohort 5), the mean change from baseline at 18 months was 2.50 cm/year (95% CI 1.22-3.79; P=0.001), with a corresponding rise in height z score (+0.54) and a decrease in the [upper-to-lower body segment ratio](../biomedicalmeasure/upper-to-lower-body-segment-ratio.md) (-0.12). The side-effect profile was generally mild with no serious adverse events, no treatment discontinuations, and only a single transient case of mild hyperphosphatemia. The 0.25 mg/kg/day dose is being advanced into a pivotal phase 3 placebo-controlled trial.

cohort 5 (0.25 mg/kg/day) at 18 months; at 6 months change from baseline AHV was dose-dependent - cohort 1 -1.82 (95% CI -4.96 to 1.32), cohort 2 1.13 (0.47-1.79), cohort 3 -0.06 (-0.93 to 0.81), cohort 4 0.94 (0.15-1.74), cohort 5 3.38 (1.67-5.10) cm/year; at month 12 cohort 5 change 2.51 (95% CI 1.02-3.99)

stats.responders: 10 of 11 (91%) showed AHV increase at 18 months; 8 of 11 (73%) increased >=25% over baseline

cohort 5; upper-to-lower body segment ratio decreased from 2.02 at baseline to 1.88 at 18 months (children with achondroplasia have a ratio ~2.0 vs ~1.0 in average stature)
