Inflammatory bowel disease.body:
# Inflammatory bowel disease

Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a group of chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract that includes [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md) and Crohn's disease. The [TL1A](../molecule/tumor-necrosis-factor-like-cytokine-1a-protein.md)-[DR3](../molecule/death-domain-receptor-3-protein.md) costimulatory cytokine system has been implicated in IBD pathogenesis, and both [TNFSF15](../gene/tnfsf15-gene.md) (encoding TL1A) and TNFRSF25 (encoding DR3) are confirmed IBD-susceptibility genes across diverse populations. TL1A blockade with [tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md) was evaluated as a new mechanism of action in the [ARTEMIS-UC trial](../study/artemis-uc-trial.md).

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)
Inflammatory bowel disease.description: A group of chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract, including ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, with confirmed genetic susceptibility involving the TL1A-DR3 (TNFSF15/TNFRSF25) costimulatory cytokine system.

Influenza-like illness.body:
# Influenza-like illness

Influenza-like illness is a constellation of flu-like symptoms. In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md), it occurred in 47% of participants receiving [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) plus [ruzotolimod](../molecule/ruzotolimod.md) and 27% of those receiving xalnesiran plus peginterferon alfa-2a. It was predominantly associated with ruzotolimod and is considered a biologic marker of on-target [TLR7](../molecule/toll-like-receptor-7-protein.md) activation; no instances were considered serious by investigators.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Influenza-like illness.description: A constellation of flu-like symptoms (fever, malaise, myalgia); with the TLR7 agonist ruzotolimod it is a biologic marker of on-target immune activation in chronic hepatitis B therapy.

Infusion-related reaction.body:
# Infusion-related reaction

An infusion-related reaction is a hypersensitivity-type reaction during or shortly after IV infusion. With [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) such reactions were uncommon: in the healthy Japanese phase 1 study one of 18 volunteers had a grade 2 infusion-related reaction (generalized erythema, facial flushing, palpitations with transient T-wave changes) that led to discontinuation after 22 mg/kg and resolved within ~1.3 h after diphenhydramine. In the UNITY HDFN study, mild infusion reactions occurred in 1% of infusions (3 of 234).

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Nipocalimab in Healthy Japanese Volunteers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39073504/) (PMID:39073504)
Infusion-related reaction.description: A hypersensitivity-type reaction occurring during or shortly after intravenous infusion (e.g. erythema, flushing, palpitations); an uncommon adverse event with IV nipocalimab.

edges.object: Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Japanese volunteers
edges.primary_source: Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Japanese volunteers

edges.note: infusion-related reactions were the most common treatment-related adverse event with nexiguran ziclumeran (5/36, 14%); one severe SAE (hypotension)

Injection site reaction.body:
# Injection site reaction

An injection site reaction is a local reaction (erythema, swelling, soreness, or bruising) at the subcutaneous injection site. In the [INVESTMENT trial](../study/investment-trial.md), two participants receiving [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) had injection site reactions of erythema and swelling, and placebo-arm participants reported injection site soreness and bruising; no serious adverse events occurred.

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
Injection site reaction.description: A local reaction at the subcutaneous injection site, such as erythema, swelling, soreness, or bruising; the most common adverse effect of subcutaneous anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies.

edges.note: two galcanezumab-arm participants experienced injection site reactions of erythema and swelling; placebo-arm participants reported injection site soreness and bruising; no serious adverse events

Interleukin-34 (protein).body:
# Interleukin-34 (protein)

Interleukin-34 (IL-34) is a second endogenous cytokine ligand of [CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md), distinct from [CSF-1](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-protein.md), that signals through the same receptor to regulate development and function of tissue macrophages. [Axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) blocks binding of both CSF-1 and IL-34 ligands; peak concentrations of IL-34 increase dose-dependently during axatilimab therapy.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
- [Axatilimab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39551906/) (PMID:39551906)
Interleukin-34 (protein).description: A second endogenous cytokine ligand of CSF-1R; binding of IL-34 to CSF-1R induces signaling regulating development and function of tissue macrophages. Its blockade by axatilimab contributes to dose-dependent increases in circulating IL-34.

edges.note: IL-34 and CSF-1 signal through CSF-1R; axatilimab blocks binding of both ligands

edges.object: Kitko 2023 — axatilimab phase I/II in cGVHD
edges.primary_source: Kitko 2023 — axatilimab phase I/II in cGVHD

Intrauterine transfusion.body:
# Intrauterine transfusion

Intrauterine transfusion (IUT) is an invasive in-utero red-cell transfusion to the fetus and the standard treatment for severe [fetal anemia](../phenotype/fetal-anemia.md) in [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md). It carries procedural complications (preterm rupture of membranes, preterm birth, fetal death; ~17% perinatal loss per procedure before 20 weeks). Delaying or avoiding IUT is the central efficacy outcome for [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md): in [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) the median gestational age at first IUT rose to 27 weeks (vs 20-22 weeks historically) and 46% of maternal-infant pairs needed no antenatal or neonatal transfusions.

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
- [Design of a Phase 3 Study of Nipocalimab in Pregnancies at Risk for Severe HDFN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39197469/) (PMID:39197469)
Intrauterine transfusion.description: An invasive in-utero red-cell transfusion to the fetus, the standard treatment for severe fetal anemia in HDFN; associated with procedural complications and fetal loss, especially before 20 weeks gestation.

edges.note: standard-of-care treatment for cordocentesis-confirmed fetal anemia; avoidance/delay of IUT is the key efficacy outcome for nipocalimab
edges.object: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn

Intravenous immunoglobulin.body:
# Intravenous immunoglobulin

Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) is a pooled human multidonor [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) blood product used in antibody-mediated diseases. One mechanism is competitive saturation of the [neonatal Fc receptor](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md): supraphysiological infused IgG saturates FcRn so endogenous (including pathogenic) IgG is catabolized rather than recycled. In [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md) IVIg (with or without plasmapheresis) has been used to delay intrauterine transfusions but with poor outcomes — only ~7% live birth without transfusion historically — motivating the higher-affinity, more selective [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md). FCGRT VNTR genotype may modulate IVIg pharmacokinetics and response.

## Citations
- [The importance of FcRn in neuro-immunotherapies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33717213/) (PMID:33717213)
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
Intravenous immunoglobulin.description: A pooled human multidonor IgG blood product used to treat antibody-mediated diseases; mechanisms include competitive FcRn saturation that accelerates catabolism of endogenous (including pathogenic) IgG, plus complement, cytokine and idiotypic effects.

edges.note: supraphysiological IVIg IgG levels saturate FcRn so endogenous IgG is degraded rather than recycled; nipocalimab FcRn affinity is more than 1000x that of IVIg
across retrospective studies only 4 of 54 IVIg-treated pregnancies (7%) had live birth without intrauterine transfusion; maternal alloantibody titer decrease only 35-43% vs 4-32 fold with nipocalimab
edges.object: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn

edges.note: first-line therapy; five RCTs demonstrated efficacy of IVIg 2 g/kg vs placebo (as early as 6 weeks, sustained to 24 and one study 48 weeks); equivalence with corticosteroids and plasma exchange in head-to-head trials; mechanisms include inhibition of macrophage-induced demyelination, neutralization of pathogenic antibodies, complement inhibition and FcRn-mediated IgG catabolism

stats.dose: 2 g/kg over 2-5 days, maintenance 1 g/kg every 3 weeks

Iron-sulfur cluster assembly.body:
# Iron-sulfur cluster assembly

Iron-sulfur cluster assembly is the mitochondrial pathway that builds iron-sulfur cofactors for numerous metabolic enzymes and depends on frataxin. Its impairment is central to the pathophysiology of [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md), the indication studied in the Luvadaxistat FRDA phase 2 trial.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Iron-sulfur cluster assembly.description: The mitochondrial pathway that builds iron-sulfur cofactors and depends on frataxin; impaired in Friedreich ataxia.

Japanese population.body:
# Japanese population

The Japanese population (volunteers born in Japan with Japanese parents and grandparents) was studied to confirm that [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) has pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics comparable to a primarily non-Asian first-in-human population. The phase 1 study in 24 healthy Japanese volunteers found dose-dependent serum IgG reductions and PK consistent with prior data, and an [FCGRT](../gene/fcgrt-gene.md) genetic analysis (Japanese vs diverse populations) identified no unique Japanese variants altering the [FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) IgG-binding site, supporting global development across diverse populations.

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Nipocalimab in Healthy Japanese Volunteers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39073504/) (PMID:39073504)
Japanese population.description: People of Japanese ancestry, studied as a primarily Asian population to confirm comparable nipocalimab pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics and high FCGRT/FcRn conservation relative to non-Asian populations.

edges.object: Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Japanese volunteers
edges.primary_source: Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Japanese volunteers

KLKB1 (gene).body:
# KLKB1 (gene)

KLKB1 is the human gene encoding [plasma prekallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md), the zymogen precursor of plasma kallikrein, and is expressed primarily in [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md). It is the therapeutic target of [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), an in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy that introduces small insertions and deletions into KLKB1 via nonhomologous end-joining repair of Cas9-induced double-strand breaks, permanently disrupting prekallikrein production and reducing total plasma kallikrein levels for the treatment of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
KLKB1 (gene).description: The human gene encoding plasma prekallikrein (the zymogen of plasma kallikrein), expressed primarily in hepatocytes; it is the target gene knocked out by the in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing therapy NTLA-2002 for hereditary angioedema.

edges.note: KLKB1 encodes plasma prekallikrein, the zymogen precursor of plasma kallikrein; primarily expressed in the liver
KLKB1 is primarily expressed in hepatocytes, the primary source of plasma prekallikrein
KLKB1 p.Cys548Tyr mutation identified in 3 F12-HAE patients from 2 families; KLKB1 abnormalities can result in overproduction or impaired regulation of plasma kallikrein

Kallikrein-kinin pathway.body:
# Kallikrein-kinin pathway

The kallikrein-kinin pathway (contact activation pathway / kinin-kallikrein system) is a plasma cascade of enzymes and peptides regulating vascular permeability, inflammation, and blood pressure. Activated factor XII (factor XIIa) converts prekallikrein to active [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md), which cleaves [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md) from high-molecular-weight kininogen; bradykinin acts on the B2 receptor to increase vascular permeability. [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md) is the key negative regulator. In [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md), loss of C1INH regulation leads to uncontrolled activation of the pathway, overproduction of bradykinin, and swelling attacks. Most investigational therapies act at different points of this pathway (factor XII, prekallikrein/kallikrein, or bradykinin B2 receptor).

## Citations
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
Kallikrein-kinin pathway.description: The plasma contact activation cascade in which factor XIIa converts prekallikrein to plasma kallikrein, which cleaves bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen; bradykinin increases vascular permeability. The pathway is normally restrained by C1 esterase inhibitor, and its dysregulation underlies hereditary angioedema.

edges.note: dysregulation (unchecked activation) of the kallikrein-kinin system causes overproduction of bradykinin and angioedema

Keam 2024 — cefepime/enmetazobactam firs.body:
# Keam 2024 — cefepime/enmetazobactam first approval

This AdisInsight First Approval report (Drugs 2024) summarizes the development, pharmacology, and pivotal trial data of cefepime/[enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) (EXBLIFEP), an intravenous fixed-dose combination of [cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) (a 4th-generation [cephalosporin](../molecularclass/cephalosporins.md)) and the extended-spectrum beta-lactamase inhibitor enmetazobactam, developed by Allecra Therapeutics and ADVANZ PHARMA for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections. It received its first approval on 22 February 2024 in the USA for adults with [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md) including pyelonephritis, supported by the phase 3 ALLIUM and phase 2 CACTUS trials.

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)

Keratopathy.body:
# Keratopathy

Keratopathy (here used broadly for corneal or retinal disorders) is an ocular adverse-event class associated with [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) at the higher doses used in oncology. Phosphorus levels and ocular events were therefore closely monitored in the [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md), but no corneal or retinal disorders were reported or identified by ophthalmic examination at any of the low doses tested in children with [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md).

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
Keratopathy.description: A corneal or retinal disorder; an ocular adverse event class associated with FGFR-inhibitor (infigratinib) use at higher oncology doses, monitored in but not observed during the low-dose achondroplasia study.

Ki-67.body:
# Ki-67

Ki-67 is a nuclear proliferation marker quantified by immunohistochemistry as the percentage of positively stained tumor cells. The change in the Ki-67 index serves as a surrogate endpoint of treatment benefit in early [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md), and a posttreatment Ki-67 <=2.7% defines complete cell-cycle arrest. In the [EMBER-2 study](../study/ember-2-study.md), ~2 weeks of [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) reduced the Ki-67 geometric mean by ~70% (71% at 400 mg, 72% at 800 mg), with complete cell-cycle arrest in 24% of evaluable tumors overall. Ki-67 was also used preclinically to demonstrate combination antiproliferative effects with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md).

## Citations
- [EMBER-2 window-of-opportunity study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39377773/) (PMID:39377773)
- [Imlunestrant preclinical profile](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652577/) (PMID:39652577)
Ki-67.description: A nuclear proliferation marker measured by immunohistochemistry; the percentage of Ki-67-positive tumor cells serves as a surrogate of treatment benefit in early breast cancer, and a posttreatment Ki-67 <=2.7% defines complete cell-cycle arrest.

edges.note: change in Ki-67 index is a surrogate endpoint of treatment benefit; complete cell-cycle arrest defined as posttreatment Ki-67 <=2.7% in tumors with baseline Ki-67 >=5%

Kitko 2023 — axatilimab phase I/II in cG.body:
# Kitko 2023 — axatilimab phase I/II in cGVHD

This phase I/II open-label, multicenter study (SNDX-6352-0503; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03604692), sponsored by Syndax Pharmaceuticals, evaluated [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) in 40 patients (17 phase I; 23 phase II) aged >=6 years with active [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md) after at least two prior systemic therapy lines. Phase I identified the optimal biologic dose (3 mg/kg every 4 weeks) and recommended phase II dose (1 mg/kg every 2 weeks). The phase II cohort met its primary endpoint with a 50% overall response rate at cycle 7 day 1, with an 82% ORR by cycle 7 day 1.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab for Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease After Failure of at Least Two Prior Systemic Therapies: Results of a Phase I/II Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36459673/) (PMID:36459673)

Klebsiella pneumoniae.body:
# Klebsiella pneumoniae

Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative bacterium and a major cause of [complicated urinary tract infection](../disease/complicated-urinary-tract-infection.md) and other healthcare-associated infections, frequently producing [extended-spectrum beta-lactamases](../molecularclass/extended-spectrum-beta-lactamases.md). It was the second most common uropathogen (9.7%) in the phase 3 ALLIUM trial. Adding [enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md) 8 ug/mL to [cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) lowered the cefepime MIC90 for ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae from greater than 64 to 1.0 ug/mL, restoring activity; some K. pneumoniae isolates carrying NDM-1, OXA-48, or KPC-3 carbapenemases remained resistant (MIC >=16 ug/mL).

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)
Klebsiella pneumoniae.description: A Gram-negative bacterium and a major cause of complicated urinary tract infection and other healthcare-associated infections, often producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases; activity against it is restored by adding enmetazobactam to cefepime.

edges.note: second most common ALLIUM uropathogen (9.7%); a frequent ESBL-producing Gram-negative pathogen in cUTI

adding enmetazobactam 8 ug/mL lowered cefepime MIC90 for ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae from >64 to 1.0 ug/mL; ALLIUM composite response 68% (cefepime/enmetazobactam) vs 56% (piperacillin/tazobactam) for K. pneumoniae

LDL cholesterol level.body:
# LDL cholesterol level

LDL cholesterol level is the plasma concentration of cholesterol carried in low-density lipoprotein particles, a principal driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. In the [ARCHES-2 trial](../study/arches-2-trial.md) for [mixed hyperlipidemia](../disease/mixed-hyperlipidemia.md), [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) lowered LDL cholesterol by -16, -14, and -20 percentage points versus placebo at week 24 across the 50, 100, and 200 mg doses; the LDL-lowering effect was attenuated at higher baseline triglyceride tertiles, and the larger non-HDL cholesterol reduction was driven principally by remnant-cholesterol lowering rather than LDL reduction.

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
LDL cholesterol level.description: The plasma concentration of cholesterol carried in low-density lipoprotein particles, a principal driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk and a secondary efficacy biomarker in lipid-lowering trials.

edges.note: LDL cholesterol was a secondary end point; mean baseline ~97 mg/dL; ANGPTL3 silencing lowered LDL by up to -20 percentage points vs placebo at week 24

Lanadelumab.body:
# Lanadelumab

Lanadelumab (Takhzyro) is a recombinant human IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody that binds and inhibits [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md). Approved in 2018 for subcutaneous long-term prophylaxis of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md) every 2 to 4 weeks, it significantly decreases attack frequency and improves quality of life. As a [plasma kallikrein inhibitor](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md), it requires regular lifelong administration; common adverse events include injection site reaction, upper respiratory infection, and headache. Some patients enrolled in the NTLA-2002 phase 2 trial had received lanadelumab as prior prophylaxis.

## Citations
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Lanadelumab.description: A recombinant human IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody that inhibits plasma kallikrein; approved in 2018 for subcutaneous long-term prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema attacks, dosed every 2 to 4 weeks.

edges.note: human IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody targeting plasma kallikrein
approved 2018 for SC long-term prophylaxis every 2-4 weeks; significantly decreases attack frequency

Lerapolturev.body:
# Lerapolturev

Lerapolturev (PVSRIPO) is a polio-rhinovirus chimera used as a viral immunotherapy. It induces persistent type-I interferon-dominant inflammation in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md), producing polyfunctional antitumor CD8+ T-cell responses. In recurrent adult glioblastoma, clinical trials reported a 16% rate of survival of at least 36 months with a manageable safety profile, and early pediatric high-grade glioma trials showed no grade 3/4 toxicity.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Lerapolturev.description: A polio-rhinovirus chimera viral immunotherapy that induces persistent type-I interferon-dominant inflammation in glioblastoma, eliciting polyfunctional antitumor CD8+ T-cell responses.

edges.note: in recurrent adult glioblastoma, clinical trials demonstrated a 16% rate of survival of at least 36 months with a manageable safety profile; in pediatric high-grade glioma no grade 3/4 toxicity in early trials

Leu 2024 — nipocalimab infusion-rate pha.body:
# Leu 2024 — nipocalimab infusion-rate phase 1 study

A phase 1, single-infusion, sequential, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, escalating dose-and-infusion-rate study at a single US site. Forty healthy adults received [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) 30 mg/kg IV over 60, 30, 15 or 7.5 min (0.5, 1, 2 or 4 mg/kg/min), 60 mg/kg over 15 min (4 mg/kg/min), or matching placebo (6 nipocalimab + 2 placebo per cohort). Nipocalimab was well tolerated at all rates, with consistent dose-dependent PK and [serum IgG](../biomedicalmeasure/serum-igg-level.md) reductions regardless of infusion rate, supporting infusion durations as short as 7.5 min for later trials.

## Citations

Limb ataxia.body:
# Limb ataxia

Limb ataxia is a loss of coordination of limb movements and is a prominent, highly penetrant neurological feature of [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md), with a sensory ataxia component linked to loss of proprioception. Along with dysarthria and impaired dexterity, it contributes to the progressive motor incapacitation that the [luvadaxistat trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md) sought, unsuccessfully, to improve.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Limb ataxia.description: Loss of coordination of limb movements; a prominent, highly penetrant neurological feature of Friedreich ataxia that includes a sensory ataxia component.

Lipase increased.body:
# Lipase increased

Increased serum lipase is a transient on-target laboratory abnormality of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), reflecting reduced macrophage-mediated enzyme clearance after CSF-1R inhibition, generally without clinical pancreatitis. It was dose-dependent in AGAVE-201 (11%, 26%, 49% across the 0.3-, 1-, and 3-mg dose groups). In the phase I/II study, a grade 3 lipase elevation without evidence of pancreatitis was one of two dose-limiting toxicities at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks.

## Citations

Lipase increased.description: An elevation in serum lipase; a transient on-target laboratory abnormality of CSF-1R inhibition by axatilimab related to reduced macrophage-mediated enzyme clearance, generally without clinical pancreatitis.

edges.note: dose-dependent - 11% (0.3-mg), 26% (1-mg), 49% (3-mg group); a grade 3 lipase elevation without pancreatitis was a dose-limiting toxicity in the phase I/II study

Lipid nanoparticle hepatic delivery.body:
# Lipid nanoparticle hepatic delivery

Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) hepatic delivery is a nonviral technology that uses lipid nanoparticles with liver tropism to encapsulate nucleic-acid payloads. In [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), the LNP encapsulates messenger RNA encoding the Cas9 endonuclease and a single guide RNA targeting [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md). The LNP is rapidly taken up by [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md) via low-density-lipoprotein-receptor-mediated endocytosis, after which Cas9 mRNA is translated and the ribonucleoprotein complex performs [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) at the KLKB1 locus. This liver-directed delivery enables highly effective hepatic gene editing with low risk of off-target effects in other tissues.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)

Live-birth rate.body:
# Live-birth rate

Live-birth rate is the proportion of pregnancies resulting in a live birth. In the phase 2 [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) study of [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) for [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md), the primary efficacy endpoint was live birth at 32 weeks gestation or later without an intrauterine transfusion, achieved in 54% of pregnancies (7/13; 95% CI 25-81) versus a 0% historical benchmark. Overall live birth occurred in 12 of 13 study pregnancies (92%).

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
Live-birth rate.description: The proportion of pregnancies resulting in live birth, used in HDFN trials (specifically live birth at >=32 weeks gestation without an intrauterine transfusion) as the primary efficacy outcome for nipocalimab.

edges.note: live birth at >=32 weeks gestation without intrauterine transfusion was the UNITY primary efficacy endpoint
edges.object: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn

Liver.body:
# Liver

The liver is the largest internal organ and the principal site of coagulation factor synthesis. It is the main target tissue for AAV-vector gene therapies including [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md).

## Citations
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Liver.description: The largest internal organ; principal site of coagulation factor synthesis and a key target tissue for AAV-based gene therapies such as fidanacogene elaparvovec.

Luvadaxistat.body:
# Luvadaxistat

Luvadaxistat (TAK-831; NBI-1065844) is a highly selective, potent oral inhibitor of [d-amino acid oxidase (DAAO)](d-amino-acid-oxidase-protein.md) (IC50 ~3.6 ng/mL for the human enzyme). By inhibiting DAAO, which catabolizes [d-serine](d-serine.md) (an NMDA-receptor co-agonist enriched in the cerebellum), it raises d-serine levels. In a preclinical FRDA mouse model it increased cerebellar d-serine and improved motor coordination.

In the phase 2 [FRDA trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md), both doses achieved target exposure and significantly raised plasma d-serine, yet luvadaxistat did not improve the primary endpoint (9-HPT-1) or any secondary endpoint versus placebo, leading to the conclusion that it is safe and well tolerated but not effective for [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md). The most common adverse events were headache and nausea.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Luvadaxistat.description: A highly selective and potent oral inhibitor of d-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) (IC50 ~3.6 ng/mL for human DAAO) that raises d-serine levels; evaluated and found ineffective for Friedreich ataxia despite favorable safety and target engagement.

edges.note: highly selective and potent DAAO inhibitor
highly selective potent inhibitor of human DAAO; PK/PD modeling showed peak DAAO target occupancy >90% at the higher dose regimen

no statistically significant difference vs placebo on primary endpoint (9-HPT-1); 75 mg BID LS mean diff -0.00054 (adjusted one-sided p=1.00); study concluded luvadaxistat is not effective for FRDA
secondary endpoint mFARS-neuro; luvadaxistat arms did not separate from placebo (also no benefit on T25FW, FARS ADLs, PGI-S, CGI-I/S, LCLA)

Luvadaxistat FRDA phase 2 trial.body:
# Luvadaxistat FRDA phase 2 trial

This phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm proof-of-concept study (NCT03214588) evaluated oral [luvadaxistat](../molecule/luvadaxistat.md) at 75 mg or 300 mg twice daily versus placebo over 12 weeks in adults with [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md). It enrolled 67 patients (randomized 2:1:2) at six US academic neurological centers from November 2017 to January 2019, with 63 (94%) completing. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline at week 12 on the inverse of the time to complete the [nine-hole peg test](../biomedicalmeasure/nine-hole-peg-test.md) (9-HPT-1). Despite achieving target [DAAO](../molecule/d-amino-acid-oxidase-protein.md) occupancy and the expected d-serine elevations, luvadaxistat did not show efficacy on the primary or secondary endpoints.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Luvadaxistat FRDA phase 2 trial.description: A phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm proof-of-concept trial evaluating oral luvadaxistat (75 mg or 300 mg twice daily) versus placebo over 12 weeks in 67 adults with genetically confirmed Friedreich ataxia, conducted at six US academic centers (2017-2019).

edges.note: 67 randomized adults (2:1:2 placebo : 75 mg BID : 300 mg BID), 63 (94%) completed; primary endpoint change from baseline at week 12 on inverse of nine-hole peg test time (9-HPT-1)

Lymphopenia.body:
# Lymphopenia

Lymphopenia (decreased lymphocyte count) was the most common adverse event of special interest with [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) in the [MITIGATE trial](../study/mitigate-trial.md), occurring in 16% (11/68) of inebilizumab recipients versus 9% (6/67) of placebo recipients. It is consistent with the drug's B-cell-depleting mechanism of action; laboratory testing in N-MOmentum likewise showed lower lymphocyte counts in inebilizumab-treated patients.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
Lymphopenia.description: A reduction in circulating lymphocyte count; the most common adverse event of special interest with inebilizumab, consistent with its B-cell-depleting mechanism of action.

MGMT (gene).body:
# MGMT (gene)

MGMT encodes O6-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase, a DNA repair enzyme that removes alkyl adducts from guanine. Methylation of the MGMT promoter silences the gene, reduces repair of alkylator-induced damage, and is a strong predictive biomarker of benefit from [temozolomide](../molecule/temozolomide.md) in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md). In the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md), MGMT methylation guided group allocation and was prognostic, with methylated tumors surviving markedly longer than unmethylated tumors.

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
MGMT (gene).description: Gene encoding the DNA repair enzyme O6-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase; methylation of its promoter silences the gene and is a strong predictive and prognostic biomarker for benefit from alkylating chemotherapy (temozolomide) in glioblastoma.

edges.note: MGMT promoter methylation silences the repair enzyme, sensitizing tumors to temozolomide; unmethylated tumors respond poorly; methylation determined centrally by methylation-specific PCR
in recurrent glioblastoma group C, median OS 11.3 months (95% CI 4.4-14.9) in MGMT-methylated vs 6.2 months (95% CI 3.1-8.3) in unmethylated; 1-year OS 42.9% methylated vs 0% unmethylated

MIDAS score.body:
# MIDAS score

The MIDAS (Migraine Disability Assessment) score quantifies headache-related disability over the prior three months. In the [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md) of [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) patients, the mean baseline MIDAS of 52.8 indicated severe disability and fell to 16.7 (difference 36.1; 95% CI 21.0-51.3; p<0.001) at 12 months, with 80% of patients achieving at least a 50% MIDAS reduction.

## Citations
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
MIDAS score.description: The Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) questionnaire score, which quantifies headache-related disability; a secondary efficacy endpoint of the Russo 2023 cohort, where high baseline values reflect severe disability.

edges.note: secondary outcome - migraine-related clinical burden assessed by MIDAS every three months for 12 months

MITIGATE trial.body:
# MITIGATE trial

MITIGATE (NCT04540497) was a phase 3, multicenter, parallel-cohort, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 80 sites in 22 countries and funded by Amgen, evaluating [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) versus placebo in adults with active [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md). A total of 135 participants underwent 1:1 randomization (68 inebilizumab, 67 placebo) to receive 300 mg intravenous infusions on days 1 and 15 and at week 26 over a 52-week treatment period, with identical glucocorticoid tapers in both groups and background immunosuppressants prohibited.

The primary endpoint was time to the first treated, adjudicated disease flare. Inebilizumab reduced flare risk by 87% (hazard ratio 0.13; 95% CI 0.06-0.28; P<0.001), with flares in only 7 of 68 (10%) inebilizumab recipients versus 40 of 67 (60%) placebo recipients. Key secondary endpoints (annualized flare rate and flare-free complete remission) all favored inebilizumab.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
MITIGATE trial.description: Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (NCT04540497) conducted at 80 sites in 22 countries evaluating inebilizumab versus placebo over a 52-week treatment period in adults with active IgG4-related disease.

edges.note: primary endpoint - time to first treated, adjudicated IgG4-related disease flare during the 52-week treatment period, assessed in a time-to-event (Cox proportional-hazards) analysis
key secondary endpoint - annualized rate of treated and adjudicated IgG4-related disease flares

primary endpoint - HR for first treated/adjudicated flare 0.13 (95% CI 0.06-0.28, P<0.001); 7/68 (10%) inebilizumab vs 40/67 (60%) placebo had a flare; 87% relative flare-risk reduction; 68 inebilizumab and 67 placebo randomized 1:1

Macrophage.body:
# Macrophage

Macrophages are phagocytic immune cells whose development and function are governed by [CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md) signaling. In [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md), CSF-1R-dependent profibrotic (M2) macrophages, derived from [nonclassical monocytes](../celltype/nonclassical-monocyte.md), drive multiorgan inflammation and fibrosis. Liver macrophages (Kupffer cells) clear serum enzymes; their depletion by [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) underlies the characteristic transient AST/CPK/lipase elevations, while macrophage depletion in skin underlies periorbital edema.

## Citations
- [Axatilimab for Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease After Failure of at Least Two Prior Systemic Therapies: Results of a Phase I/II Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36459673/) (PMID:36459673)
- [Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39292927/) (PMID:39292927)
Macrophage.description: A tissue-resident or monocyte-derived phagocytic immune cell whose development and function depend on CSF-1R signaling; profibrotic (M2) macrophages and Kupffer cells (liver macrophages) are central to cGVHD pathology and to the on-target effects of axatilimab.

edges.note: macrophages develop from the mononuclear phagocytic cell lineage including monocyte precursors and nonclassical monocytic cells under CSF-1R signaling

Maternal alloantibody titer.body:
# Maternal alloantibody titer

Maternal alloantibody titer is the serum titer of maternal anti-red-blood-cell [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) alloantibodies (e.g. anti-D, anti-K), a key biomarker of [HDFN](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md) severity. In [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md), [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) treatment decreased maternal alloantibody titers 4 to 32 times from baseline, far exceeding the 35-43% decrease reported with IVIg. Critical titers (anti-D >=32, anti-K >=4) define eligibility and risk in the nipocalimab HDFN trials.

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
- [Design of a Phase 3 Study of Nipocalimab in Pregnancies at Risk for Severe HDFN](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39197469/) (PMID:39197469)
Maternal alloantibody titer.description: The serum titer of maternal anti-red-blood-cell IgG alloantibodies (e.g. anti-D, anti-K); a key biomarker of HDFN severity and a pharmacodynamic readout of nipocalimab's inhibition of IgG recycling and transplacental transfer.

edges.note: critical alloantibody titer thresholds (anti-D >=32 in UNITY; anti-D/Rhc/RhE/RhC >=16 or Kell >=4 in AZALEA) indicate high HDFN risk

Metastatic colorectal cancer.body:
# Metastatic colorectal cancer

Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is colorectal carcinoma that has spread to distant sites. Treatment has historically been built on the fluoropyrimidine 5-fluorouracil, usually combined with oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) or irinotecan (FOLFIRI) and antibodies such as bevacizumab or cetuximab; on progression through these regimens, treatment options become limited.

[Trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102) is active in 5-fluorouracil-resistant models and is approved for refractory mCRC. In the phase 3 [RECOURSE trial](../study/recourse-trial.md) and the Japanese J003 phase 2 trial it prolonged overall survival over placebo in patients progressive on at least two prior chemotherapy regimens.

## Citations
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Metastatic colorectal cancer.description: Colorectal carcinoma that has spread beyond the colon/rectum to distant sites; in the refractory setting (progressive after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan) it is the approved indication for trifluridine/tipiracil.

Migraine.body:
# Migraine

Migraine is a common primary headache disorder, with an estimated prevalence around 12%, in which [CGRP](../molecule/calcitonin-gene-related-peptide-protein.md) signaling is a validated therapeutic target. [Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-cgrp-monoclonal-antibodies.md) such as [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md), [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md), and [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md) are established, safe preventives for episodic and chronic migraine.

Migraine and dizziness co-occur more often than expected by chance — migraine is found in up to 38% of patients with recurrent dizziness — which led to recognition of [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) as a distinct migraine subtype.

## Citations
- [A placebo controlled, randomized clinical trial of galcanezumab for vestibular migraine: The INVESTMENT study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39344988/) (PMID:39344988)
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
Migraine.description: A common primary headache disorder (prevalence ~12%) in which CGRP signaling is a validated therapeutic target; vestibular migraine is regarded as a vestibular form of migraine.

edges.note: recurrent headache is the cardinal feature; CGRP-blocking antibodies reduce monthly headache days
edges.primary_source: Russo 2023 — anti-CGRP mAbs for vestibular migraine

edges.note: migraine and dizziness co-occur more than expected by chance; migraine is found in up to 38% of patients with recurrent dizziness, motivating the recognition of vestibular migraine

Minimum inhibitory concentration.body:
# Minimum inhibitory concentration

The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is the lowest concentration of an antimicrobial that inhibits visible bacterial growth in vitro, summarised across isolate panels as MIC50 and MIC90. It is the principal measure of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) potency: MIC90 of 0.5 ug/mL against [S. aureus](../organism/staphylococcus-aureus.md) (including MRSA) and S. pneumoniae, 2-4 ug/mL against [E. coli](../organism/escherichia-coli.md), and 0.5-1 ug/mL against [N. gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md).

## Citations
- [Gepotidacin (GSK2140944) in vitro activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28483959/) (PMID:28483959)
Minimum inhibitory concentration.description: The lowest concentration of an antimicrobial that inhibits visible bacterial growth in vitro; used (with MIC50/MIC90 summary statistics) to quantify gepotidacin potency against target pathogens.

edges.note: gepotidacin MIC90 0.5 ug/mL vs S. aureus and S. pneumoniae, 2-4 ug/mL vs E. coli, 0.5-1 ug/mL vs N. gonorrhoeae

edges.primary_source: Unemo 2024 — in silico gepotidacin target mining

Mixed hyperlipidemia.body:
# Mixed hyperlipidemia

Mixed hyperlipidemia is a lipid disorder characterized by elevated plasma levels of both low-density and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. Elevated [triglyceride](../biomedicalmeasure/triglyceride-level.md) levels reflect triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (chylomicrons, VLDL, and their remnants), whose cholesterol content contributes residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk beyond LDL lowering. In the [ARCHES-2 trial](../study/arches-2-trial.md) (fasting triglycerides 150-499 mg/dL with elevated LDL or non-HDL cholesterol), [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) lowered triglycerides and atherogenic lipoproteins by silencing [ANGPTL3](../gene/angptl3-gene.md).

## Citations
- [Zodasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic Targeting ANGPTL3, for Mixed Hyperlipidemia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38809174/) (PMID:38809174)
Mixed hyperlipidemia.description: A lipid disorder characterized by elevated plasma levels of both low-density and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins; elevated remnant cholesterol contributes residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk beyond LDL cholesterol lowering.

Modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale.body:
# Modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale

The modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS) is a clinician-administered neurological rating scale for [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md), where a negative change indicates improvement. In the [luvadaxistat trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md), the mFARS-neuro total score and the FARS activities-of-daily-living component were secondary endpoints; all arms trended toward less impairment at week 12, but the luvadaxistat arms did not separate statistically from placebo.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
Modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale.description: A clinician-administered neurological rating scale for Friedreich ataxia; the mFARS-neuro total score and the FARS activities-of-daily-living component were secondary endpoints in the luvadaxistat trial.

edges.note: mFARS-neuro total score (secondary endpoint) provides a neurological functional assessment; a negative change indicates improvement; all arms trended toward less impairment but luvadaxistat did not separate from placebo (LS mean diff 2.11 at 300 mg, p=0.975)

Monthly dizziness days.body:
# Monthly dizziness days

Monthly dizziness days is the mean number of days per month with dizziness or vestibular symptoms (any internal or external [vertigo](../phenotype/vertigo.md) or [dizziness](../phenotype/dizziness.md)) recorded in a patient diary. It was the primary efficacy endpoint of the [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md), where it decreased from a baseline mean of 10.3 to 0.8 days (difference 9.5; 95% CI 3.6-15.4; p<0.001) after 12 months of anti-CGRP monoclonal antibody treatment.

## Citations
- [Anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of vestibular migraine: A prospective observational cohort study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946234/) (PMID:36946234)
Monthly dizziness days.description: The mean number of days per month with dizziness or vestibular symptoms (any internal or external vertigo or dizziness) recorded in a patient diary; the primary efficacy endpoint of the Russo 2023 cohort.

edges.note: primary outcome - reduction of mean monthly days with vertigo and/or dizziness after 12 months of anti-CGRP mAb treatment

Monthly headache days.body:
# Monthly headache days

Monthly headache days is the mean number of days per month with [headache](../phenotype/headache.md) recorded in a patient diary. As a secondary endpoint of the [Russo 2023 cohort](../study/russo-2023-anti-cgrp-mabs-for-vestibular-migraine.md), it decreased from a baseline mean of 20.9 to 7.1 days (difference 13.8; 95% CI 9.3-18.3; p<0.001) at 12 months, with 86% of patients achieving at least a 50% reduction.

Mucoactive agents.body:
# Mucoactive agents

Mucoactive agents (mucolytics) are drugs that alter the properties of airway mucus or promote its clearance - reducing mucus viscosity, modulating mucus production, and increasing mucociliary transport. Examples used in airway disease include hypertonic saline, mannitol, and [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md), the thiol-derivative mucoactive evaluated in the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md) and the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md) for [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md). They are also used in [COPD](../disease/chronic-obstructive-pulmonary-disease.md) and chronic bronchitis.

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Mucoactive agents.description: A class of agents (including mucolytics) that modify the properties of airway mucus or enhance its clearance - reducing viscosity, modulating production, and improving mucociliary transport - used in chronic hypersecretory airway diseases.

cited 2006 systematic review of 26 randomised trials found mucoactive drugs effective (though not significant) for reducing the rate of acute exacerbations and total days of disability (<20%)

Mucus density score.body:
# Mucus density score

The mucus density score is a subjective semiquantitative 3-point rating (0=fluid, 1=viscous, 2=very viscous) of sputum density, one component of the sputum-characteristic scale (with mucus purulence and mucus volume produced) used as the primary endpoint of the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md). In [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) with [chronic mucus hypersecretion](../phenotype/chronic-mucus-hypersecretion.md), mucus density at day 15 fell significantly more in the [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) plus chest physiotherapy group (-0.80, p<0.001) than with physiotherapy alone (-0.55, p=0.005).

## Citations
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)

Myc proto-oncogene protein (protein).body:
# Myc proto-oncogene protein (protein)

c-MYC is a short-lived transcription factor and proto-oncogene product frequently overexpressed in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md). It is an indirect downstream target of [zotiraciclib](zotiraciclib.md): inhibiting [CDK-9](cyclin-dependent-kinase-9-protein.md) blocks transcription and depletes c-MYC, contributing to apoptosis. In the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md), nuclear c-MYC was detected in 79% of tumors and correlated with CDK-9 and MCL-1 expression.

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)

Myelosuppression.body:
# Myelosuppression

Myelosuppression (bone-marrow suppression) is reduced bone-marrow production of blood cells, manifesting clinically as [neutropenia](../phenotype/neutropenia.md), anemia, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia. It is the major and dose-limiting toxicity of single-agent [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) and of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102), consistent across the phase 1 PK study, the early phase 1/2 TAS-102 studies (granulocytopenia as dose-limiting toxicity), and the RECOURSE phase 3 trial.

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of trifluridine and tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Myelosuppression.description: Decreased bone-marrow production of blood cells (manifesting as neutropenia, anemia, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia); the major dose-limiting toxicity of trifluridine and of trifluridine/tipiracil.

NMDA receptor.body:
# NMDA receptor

The NMDA receptor is an ionotropic glutamate receptor for which D-serine is a co-agonist. By inhibiting [DAAO](../molecule/d-amino-acid-oxidase-protein.md) and raising D-serine, [luvadaxistat](../molecule/luvadaxistat.md) is intended to enhance NMDA receptor co-agonism, the mechanism evaluated in the Luvadaxistat FRDA phase 2 trial.

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)
NMDA receptor.description: ionotropic glutamate receptor for which D-serine is a co-agonist.

NRG1 (gene).body:
# NRG1 (gene)

NRG1 is the human gene encoding [neuregulin 1](../molecule/neuregulin-1-protein.md), a growth factor that promotes [HER2/HER3 signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md). Genomic rearrangements involving NRG1 have been identified across lung, breast, pancreas, ovarian and prostate cancers and are believed to be mitogenic drivers, particularly in KRAS-wildtype pancreatic cancer and invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma. The resulting [NRG1 gene fusions](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md) retain the EGF-like domain of NRG1, which confers ligand binding and transformation via the ERBB family of receptor tyrosine kinases. Because of large introns, NRG1 fusions are best detected by RNA-based sequencing rather than DNA-based panels.

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
NRG1 (gene).description: The human gene encoding neuregulin 1, a growth factor ligand for the ERBB receptor family; oncogenic NRG1 gene fusions retaining the EGF-like domain are mitogenic drivers across several solid tumor types.

edges.note: genomic rearrangements of NRG1 are oncogenic drivers; chimeric NRG1 proteins retain the EGF-like domain conferring ligand binding and transformation

NRG1 fusion-positive cancer.body:
# NRG1 fusion-positive cancer

NRG1 fusion-positive (NRG1+) cancer is a molecularly defined subset of solid tumors driven by oncogenic [NRG1 gene fusions](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md), which produce chimeric ligands that constitutively activate [HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md). The fusions occur largely in the absence of other canonical driver mutations. NRG1 fusions are rare (<1% of solid tumors; 0.3-1.7% of lung cancer, 0.5-1.8% of pancreatic cancer) but enriched in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma of the lung (up to ~30%) and KRAS-wildtype PDAC (up to ~18%). Subtypes include [NRG1-fusion NSCLC](../disease/nrg1-fusion-non-small-cell-lung-cancer.md) and [NRG1-fusion PDAC](../disease/nrg1-fusion-pancreatic-ductal-adenocarcinoma.md). Patients have limited therapeutic options; [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) is being developed for this indication in the [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md).

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)

NRG1 gene fusion.body:
# NRG1 gene fusion

An NRG1 gene fusion is an oncogenic, in-frame rearrangement joining an upstream partner gene to [NRG1](../gene/nrg1-gene.md), retaining the EGF-like domain. The chimeric protein acts as a constitutive ligand for [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md), driving [HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md) and tumorigenesis. Reported partners include CD74, SLC3A2, ATP1B1, VAMP2, CLU, APP, SDC4, TNC and many others. NRG1 fusions are rare (<1% of solid tumors) but enriched in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma of the lung (up to ~30%) and KRAS-wildtype PDAC (up to ~18%), and define [NRG1 fusion-positive cancer](../disease/nrg1-fusion-positive-cancer.md). Because of large NRG1 introns, RNA-based sequencing is the superior detection method. The fusion confers oncogene addiction and sensitivity to [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md).

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
NRG1 gene fusion.description: An oncogenic in-frame gene fusion joining an upstream partner gene to NRG1, retaining the EGF-like domain of NRG1; the chimeric protein acts as a constitutive ligand for HER3, driving HER2-HER3 signaling and tumorigenesis.

NRG1-fusion non-small cell lung cancer.body:
# NRG1-fusion non-small cell lung cancer

NRG1-fusion NSCLC is non-small-cell lung cancer driven by an [NRG1 gene fusion](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md), a subtype of [NRG1 fusion-positive cancer](../disease/nrg1-fusion-positive-cancer.md). NRG1 fusions occur in roughly 0.3-1.7% of lung cancers and up to ~30% of invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, typically mutually exclusive with EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, RET and NTRK alterations. These tumors have poor prognostic features and respond poorly to standard chemoimmunotherapy and afatinib. In the preclinical study, a patient with CD74-NRG1 NSCLC (six prior lines, including afatinib) achieved a RECIST partial response (-33%, deepening to -41%) on [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md), including intracranial response. NSCLC is the largest planned cohort (up to 100 patients) in the [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md).

## Citations

NRG1-fusion pancreatic ductal adenocarci.body:
# NRG1-fusion pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

NRG1-fusion PDAC is pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma driven by an [NRG1 gene fusion](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md), a subtype of [NRG1 fusion-positive cancer](../disease/nrg1-fusion-positive-cancer.md). NRG1 fusions are specifically enriched in KRAS-wildtype PDAC (up to ~18%), a setting with no approved therapy targeting the driver lesion and poor responses to conventional chemotherapy. Because of large NRG1 introns, RNA-based sequencing is recommended for KRAS-wildtype PDAC. In the preclinical study, two patients with ATP1B1-NRG1 PDAC treated with [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) (750 mg IV q2w) experienced tumor shrinkage (one partial response -44% deepening to -82%; one stable disease -22% to -25%), CA 19-9 normalization, and prolonged disease control (~14 and 11 months). PDAC is a planned cohort (up to 50 patients) in the [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md).

NT-proBNP.body:
# NT-proBNP

NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) is a circulating biomarker of myocardial wall stress used as a prognostic and disease-progression marker in [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). In the [nexiguran ziclumeran phase 1 trial](../study/nexiguran-ziclumeran-phase-1-attr-cm-trial.md), the geometric mean fold change in NT-proBNP from baseline to month 12 was 1.02 (95% CI 0.88-1.17), consistent with disease stability; baseline median NT-proBNP was 2052 ng/L.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Nexiguran Ziclumeran for ATTR Cardiomyopathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555828/) (PMID:39555828)
NT-proBNP.description: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, a circulating biomarker of myocardial wall stress used as a prognostic and disease-progression marker in heart failure and transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.

edges.note: NT-proBNP is a prognostic and disease-progression marker in ATTR-CM; progression defined as increase >700 ng/L and >30% from baseline

NTLA-2002.body:
# NTLA-2002

NTLA-2002 (Intellia Therapeutics) is an investigational in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy for [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). It is delivered by [lipid nanoparticle hepatic delivery](../methodorprocedure/lipid-nanoparticle-hepatic-delivery.md) with liver tropism, encapsulating mRNA encoding the Cas9 endonuclease and a single guide RNA targeting [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md). After uptake by [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md), Cas9 makes double-strand breaks at the KLKB1 locus; nonhomologous end-joining repair introduces indels that permanently disrupt prekallikrein production, lowering total [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) and rebalancing bradykinin production. The goal is lifelong control of [angioedema attacks](../phenotype/angioedema-attack.md) after a single intravenous dose.

In the [phase 1](../study/ntla-2002-phase-1-trial.md) dose-escalation portion, single doses of 25, 50, or 75 mg produced dose-dependent reductions in total plasma kallikrein (-67% to -95%) and a mean -95% reduction in monthly attacks with no serious adverse events. In the [phase 2](../study/ntla-2002-phase-2-trial.md) randomized portion, 25 mg and 50 mg reduced the monthly attack rate by -75% and -77% versus placebo and lowered plasma kallikrein by -55% and -86%, supporting advancement to a phase 3 trial.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)

NTLA-2002 phase 1 trial.body:
# NTLA-2002 phase 1 trial

This is the phase 1 dose-escalation portion of an ongoing, multicenter, open-label, single-group phase 1-2 trial (NCT05120830) of [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), an in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy targeting [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md), in 10 adults with type 1 or type 2 [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). Patients received a single intravenous dose of 25 mg (n=3), 50 mg (n=4), or 75 mg (n=3). No dose-limiting toxic effects or serious adverse events occurred; the most common adverse events were infusion-related reactions (70%) and fatigue (60%). A dose-dependent reduction in total plasma kallikrein protein level (-67% to -95%) and a mean -95% reduction in monthly angioedema attacks were observed.

## Citations

NTLA-2002 phase 2 trial.body:
# NTLA-2002 phase 2 trial

This is the phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled portion of the phase 1-2 trial (NCT05120830) of [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md) in 27 adults with type 1 or type 2 [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). Patients were randomized 2:2:1 to a single intravenous dose of NTLA-2002 25 mg (n=10), 50 mg (n=11), or placebo (n=6), with prior long-term prophylaxis washed out. The estimated mean monthly attack rate from week 1 through week 16 was 0.70 (25 mg), 0.65 (50 mg), and 2.82 (placebo), a difference of -75% and -77% versus placebo. Total plasma kallikrein protein levels fell -55% (25 mg) and -86% (50 mg) from baseline to week 16. Adverse events were grade 1-2 in NTLA-2002 recipients; no serious adverse events occurred in treated patients.

## Citations

Nausea.body:
# Nausea

Nausea is a common, predominantly grade 1-2 treatment-emergent adverse event of [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md). It occurred in 39.2% of patients receiving imlunestrant monotherapy at the recommended phase II dose in the [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md), 17.1% in the imlunestrant arm of [EMBER-3](../study/ember-3-trial.md), and was more frequent with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) combinations.

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
Nausea.description: A gastrointestinal symptom (the urge to vomit); one of the most common, mostly low-grade, treatment-emergent adverse events with imlunestrant in the EMBER program.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae.body:
# Neisseria gonorrhoeae

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the Gram-negative diplococcus that causes [uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea](../disease/uncomplicated-urogenital-gonorrhoea.md). It has developed or acquired resistance to all antimicrobials used for gonorrhoea treatment and is classed as an urgent threat (CDC) and high priority (WHO). [Gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) is highly active against it (MIC range 0.032-4 mg/L, MIC90 1 mg/L); the [GyrA gene](../gene/gyra-gene.md) and [ParC gene](../gene/parc-gene.md) carry the quinolone resistance-determining region substitutions relevant to gepotidacin resistance.

Neonatal Fc receptor (protein).body:
# Neonatal Fc receptor (protein)

The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) is a widely expressed MHC class I-like receptor — an alpha subunit encoded by [FCGRT](../gene/fcgrt-gene.md) complexed with beta-2-microglobulin — that binds [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) and [albumin](../molecule/albumin.md) at acidic endosomal pH and recycles them to the cell surface, protecting them from lysosomal degradation and giving IgG its long ~21-day half-life. FcRn is also the sole placental transporter of maternal IgG to the fetus. It is the target of [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) and other [anti-FcRn monoclonal antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md), whose blockade accelerates IgG catabolism and lowers circulating IgG and pathogenic auto/alloantibodies.

Neuregulin-1 (protein).body:
# Neuregulin-1 (protein)

Neuregulin 1 (NRG1) is a growth factor ligand encoded by [NRG1](../gene/nrg1-gene.md). Under healthy conditions it aids growth and development of epithelial, glial and muscle cells by promoting [HER2/HER3 signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md). NRG1 binds primarily to [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md) (and HER4), driving heterodimerization with [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md), EGFR and HER4 and activation of downstream PI3K-AKT signaling. The EGF-like domain of NRG1 is retained in oncogenic [NRG1 fusion proteins](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md), which act as constitutive ligands; [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) blocks this NRG1-HER3 interaction.

Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.body:
# Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder

Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare, autoimmune, demyelinating disease of the central nervous system now recognized as distinct from multiple sclerosis. It is typically characterized by incomplete recovery from recurrent attacks of optic neuritis and/or transverse myelitis, resulting in accumulating impairment such as blindness and paraplegia. Approximately 75-90% of patients carry pathogenic IgG autoantibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG), the most abundant water channel in the CNS. [B cells](../celltype/b-cell.md) play a prominent role in NMOSD immunopathogenesis, providing the rationale for treatment with [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md), which received its first US approval for AQP4-IgG seropositive NMOSD in June 2020.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.description: A rare, autoimmune, demyelinating disease of the CNS, distinct from multiple sclerosis, characterized by recurrent attacks of optic neuritis and/or transverse myelitis with incomplete recovery and accumulating impairment; most patients are seropositive for AQP4-IgG.

edges.note: B cells play a prominent role in the immunopathogenesis of NMOSD; rationale for CD19-targeted B-cell depletion

Neutropenia.body:
# Neutropenia

Neutropenia is a hematologic adverse event observed predominantly with [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) plus [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) combination therapy, reflecting the [CDK4/6 inhibitor](../molecularclass/cdk4-6-inhibitors.md) component. It occurred in 42.9% of patients (14.3% grade >=3) in the imlunestrant + abemaciclib arm of the [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md), and was the most frequent grade >=3 adverse event (19.7%) in the imlunestrant-abemaciclib group of [EMBER-3](../study/ember-3-trial.md), while being uncommon with imlunestrant monotherapy.

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)
- [EMBER-3 phase 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)

Nexiguran ziclumeran.body:
# Nexiguran ziclumeran

Nexiguran ziclumeran (nex-z, also known as NTLA-2001; Intellia Therapeutics and Regeneron) is an investigational, one-time, in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy for [transthyretin amyloidosis](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). It is delivered by [lipid nanoparticle hepatic delivery](../methodorprocedure/lipid-nanoparticle-hepatic-delivery.md) with liver tropism and carries two components: a single-guide RNA targeting [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md) and the human-codon-optimized mRNA of Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9. After uptake by [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md), Cas9 introduces double-strand breaks at the TTR locus; nonhomologous end-joining repair creates indels that permanently knock out TTR, the main source of circulating [transthyretin](../molecule/transthyretin-protein.md).

In the [phase 1 trial](../study/nexiguran-ziclumeran-phase-1-attr-cm-trial.md) of 36 patients with ATTR cardiomyopathy, a single dose reduced [serum TTR](../biomedicalmeasure/serum-transthyretin-level.md) by a mean of -90% at month 12, with reductions sustained to 24 months. Treatment-related adverse events were limited to transient infusion-related reactions (14%) and AST elevations (6%).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Nexiguran Ziclumeran for ATTR Cardiomyopathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555828/) (PMID:39555828)

Nexiguran ziclumeran phase 1 ATTR-CM tri.body:
# Nexiguran ziclumeran phase 1 ATTR-CM trial

This is an ongoing, single-arm, open-label, two-part phase 1 trial (NCT04601051) evaluating a single intravenous infusion of [nexiguran ziclumeran](../molecule/nexiguran-ziclumeran.md) (nex-z, also known as NTLA-2001), an in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy targeting [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md), in 36 patients with [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). In the dose-finding part 1, patients received 0.7 mg/kg (N=9) or 1 mg/kg (N=3); in the part 2 expansion, patients received a fixed 55 mg dose (N=24). A single dose produced deep, rapid, and durable reductions in [serum TTR](../biomedicalmeasure/serum-transthyretin-level.md) (mean -90% at month 12) and was associated with transient infusion-related reactions. The clinical effect of nex-z is being further evaluated in the phase 3 MAGNITUDE trial (NCT06128629).

## Citations

Nine-hole peg test.body:
# Nine-hole peg test

The nine-hole peg test (9-HPT) is a quantitative, performance-based timed measure of upper-extremity function and manual dexterity. Its inverse, 9-HPT-1 (1/seconds), was the primary efficacy endpoint of the [luvadaxistat FRDA trial](../study/luvadaxistat-frda-phase-2-trial.md), where a larger value indicates better function. Neither luvadaxistat dose differed significantly from placebo in change from baseline at week 12. The lack of difference between first and second assessments at each visit indicated good intra-day stability and low fatigue sensitivity in [Friedreich ataxia](../disease/friedreich-ataxia.md).

## Citations
- [Results of a randomized double-blind study evaluating luvadaxistat in adults with Friedreich ataxia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34018342/) (PMID:34018342)

Nipocalimab.body:
# Nipocalimab

Nipocalimab (M281) is a high-affinity, fully human, aglycosylated, effectorless [IgG1 monoclonal antibody](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md) that selectively binds and blocks the IgG-binding site on the [neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md). By blocking FcRn-mediated IgG recycling it accelerates catabolism of circulating IgG, lowering total IgG and pathogenic auto/alloantibodies while sparing IgG production and other humoral and cellular immune functions. Its Fab binds FcRn with picomolar affinity at both endosomal (pH 6.0) and extracellular (pH 7.6) pH.

Across phase 1 studies in healthy volunteers, single IV doses of 30-60 mg/kg produced dose-dependent reductions in [serum IgG](../biomedicalmeasure/serum-igg-level.md) of roughly 64% (30 mg/kg) to 79-80% (60 mg/kg), independent of infusion rate. It is in development for multiple IgG auto- and alloantibody-mediated diseases including [generalized myasthenia gravis](../disease/generalized-myasthenia-gravis.md) and [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md), the latter studied in the phase 2 [UNITY](../study/unity-study.md) and phase 3 [AZALEA](../study/azalea-study.md) trials.

Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Jap.body:
# Nipocalimab phase 1 study in healthy Japanese volunteers

A phase 1, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-dose escalation study (WCCT Global, Cypress, CA) in 24 healthy Japanese volunteers, who received single IV [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) 10, 30 or 60 mg/kg or placebo (6 nipocalimab + 2 placebo per cohort). Nipocalimab was generally safe and well tolerated, with dose-dependent [serum IgG](../biomedicalmeasure/serum-igg-level.md) reductions and PK comparable to the primarily non-Asian first-in-human study. A complementary analysis of [FCGRT](../gene/fcgrt-gene.md) genetic variation found no unique Japanese variants altering the [FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) IgG-binding site, supporting global development across the [Japanese population](../population/japanese-population.md) and other diverse populations.

## Citations
- [Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Nipocalimab, a Neonatal Fc Receptor Blocker, in Healthy Japanese Volunteers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39073504/) (PMID:39073504)

Nitrofurantoin.body:
# Nitrofurantoin

Nitrofurantoin is an oral antibacterial recommended in both US and European guidelines as a first-line empirical therapy for [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md), with relatively low community resistance rates. It served as the active comparator (100 mg twice daily for 5 days, slow-release Macrobid formulation) for [gepotidacin](molecule/gepotidacin.md) in the phase 3 [EAGLE-2](../study/eagle-2-trial.md) and [EAGLE-3](../study/eagle-3-trial.md) non-inferiority trials.

Nonclassical monocyte.body:
# Nonclassical monocyte

Nonclassical monocytes (nonclassical CD14+/CD16++ monocytic cells, NCMCs) are a peripheral-blood monocyte subset whose differentiation depends on [CSF-1](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-protein.md)/[CSF-1R](../molecule/colony-stimulating-factor-1-receptor-protein.md) signaling. [Axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md) preferentially eliminates nonclassical (not classical or intermediate) monocytes, and NCMC levels serve as a pharmacodynamic surrogate of efficacy in the population PK/PD model. In patients with cGVHD, typical baseline NCMC levels were estimated at 16 cells/uL, lower than in healthy participants (29.7 cells/uL) or patients with cancer (54.2 cells/uL).

# ONC201

ONC201 (dordaviprone) is an oral imipridone anticancer agent and dopamine receptor D2 antagonist that targets the mitochondrial protease ClpP, causing mitochondrial dysfunction and a p53-independent integrated stress response with antitumor TRAIL expression. It has shown early clinical success in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) and recurrent H3K27M-mutant diffuse midline [glioma](../disease/glioma.md), and is being combined with the BBB-penetrant PI3K/Akt inhibitor [paxalisib](paxalisib.md) for DIPG.
