Objective response rate.body:
# Objective response rate

Objective response rate (ORR) is the proportion of patients with measurable disease achieving a best overall response of complete or partial response (RECIST v1.1). In the EMBER program it was a key secondary endpoint: [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) monotherapy ORR was 11.8% at the RP2D in advanced [ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer](../disease/er-positive-her2-negative-breast-cancer.md) and 10.3% in [ER-positive endometrioid endometrial cancer](../disease/er-positive-endometrioid-endometrial-cancer.md), rising with [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) combinations (e.g., 61.8% for imlunestrant + abemaciclib + AI).

## Citations

Odintsov 2022 — zenocutuzumab preclinica.body:
# Odintsov 2022 — zenocutuzumab preclinical NRG1 fusions

This preclinical study characterizes [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) (Zeno; MCLA-128), a HER2xHER3 bispecific IgG1 antibody, as therapy for tumors driven by [NRG1 gene fusions](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md). Zeno inhibited growth of NRG1 fusion-positive lung, breast, pancreatic and ovarian cancer cell lines at low or subnanomolar concentrations (e.g., IC50 0.04 nmol/L in MDA-MB-175-VII), with NRG1-fusion HBEC cells ~40,000-fold more sensitive than parental controls, while sparing isogenic control cells. Mechanistically Zeno suppressed phosphorylation of [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md), [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md), EGFR and HER4 and downstream [HER2-HER3 / PI3K-AKT signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md), inducing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis, and enhanced antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.

In PDX models Zeno (25 mg/kg weekly) caused significant tumor regression. In three patients with chemotherapy-resistant NRG1 fusion-positive metastatic cancer (two ATP1B1-NRG1 PDAC, one CD74-NRG1 NSCLC) treated with Zeno 750 mg IV every 2 weeks on single-patient protocols, all experienced clinical benefit, including RECIST partial responses of -44% to -82% and prolonged disease control. These results led to the global phase I/II [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md).

# Open Targets

Open Targets is an open-access knowledgebase that provides target-disease association scores aggregated from diverse evidence types (genetic and drug associations, text mining, animal-model data). # Overall response rate

Overall response rate (ORR) is the proportion of patients achieving a complete or partial response per the 2014 NIH consensus criteria for [chronic graft-versus-host disease](../disease/chronic-graft-versus-host-disease.md). Overall survival.body:
# Overall survival

Overall survival (OS) is the time from a defined baseline until death from any cause and is a core efficacy and prognostic endpoint in [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md). In the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md), median OS with single-agent [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) in recurrent disease was 7.1 months overall, but differed markedly by MGMT status (11.3 vs 6.2 months). The glioma review reports OS as a primary endpoint across multiple targeted-therapy trials in glioma.

# PARC (gene)

PARC (parC) is the bacterial gene encoding the [ParC protein](../gene/parc-protein.md), the C subunit of [topoisomerase IV](../biologicalfunction/topoisomerase-iv.md). PROPEL 2 trial.body:
# PROPEL 2 trial

PROPEL 2 (NCT04265651) is a prospective, multicenter, multinational, open-label, phase 2 dose-finding study of once-daily oral [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md) in children aged 3-11 years with [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md), funded by BridgeBio Pharma. It comprises a dose-escalation phase with an extended-treatment period (five ascending weight-based dose cohorts: 0.016, 0.032, 0.064, 0.128, and 0.25 mg/kg/day), a dose-expansion phase to confirm the selected dose, and a pharmacokinetic substudy. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of adverse events leading to dose decrease or discontinuation, and the primary efficacy outcome is the change from baseline in [annualized height velocity](../biomedicalmeasure/annualized-height-velocity.md).

A total of 72 children were enrolled across the five cohorts. A dose-dependent increase in annualized height velocity was observed; at the highest dose (cohort 5, 0.25 mg/kg/day) the mean change from baseline at 18 months was 2.50 cm/year (95% CI 1.22-3.79; P=0.001), accompanied by an increase in height z score (+0.54) and a decrease in the [upper-to-lower body segment ratio](../biomedicalmeasure/upper-to-lower-body-segment-ratio.md) (-0.12). It is the first study to target the genetic driver of FGFR3 overactivity in children with achondroplasia, and the 0.25 mg/kg/day dose is being carried into a phase 3 placebo-controlled trial (NCT06164951).

## Citations
- [Oral Infigratinib Therapy in Children with Achondroplasia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555818/) (PMID:39555818)
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)

PROPEL study.body:
# PROPEL study

PROPEL (NCT04035811) is a prospective, noninterventional natural-history study sponsored by QED Therapeutics that characterizes the natural history of [achondroplasia](../disease/achondroplasia.md) in children. Eligible children are aged 2.5-10 years with a diagnosis of achondroplasia, and are observed for a minimum of 6 months and a maximum of 2 years, with the study enrolling up to 200 children. Its primary endpoint is to establish baseline [annualized height velocity](../biomedicalmeasure/annualized-height-velocity.md) (AHV).

By establishing each child's baseline AHV, PROPEL allows each participant to act as their own control in the subsequent interventional [PROPEL 2 trial](../study/propel-2-trial.md) of oral [infigratinib](../molecule/infigratinib.md). Children who complete at least 6 months in PROPEL are eligible for PROPEL 2.

## Citations
- [Infigratinib in children with achondroplasia: the PROPEL and PROPEL 2 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35342457/) (PMID:35342457)

ParC (protein).body:
# ParC (protein)

ParC is the C subunit of bacterial [topoisomerase IV](../biologicalfunction/topoisomerase-iv.md), a type II topoisomerase. It is encoded by the [PARC gene](../gene/parc-gene.md) and is one of the two molecular targets of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md). Residue D86 is located in the gepotidacin binding site; the ParC D86N substitution is a prevalent stepping-stone mutation predisposing to gepotidacin resistance.

ParC D86N.body:
# ParC D86N

ParC D86N is an amino acid substitution at residue D86 of the [ParC](../molecule/parc-protein.md) subunit of [Neisseria gonorrhoeae](../organism/neisseria-gonorrhoeae.md) topoisomerase IV, located in the [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) binding site. Selected by historical fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin) use, it is a prevalent stepping-stone mutation: it does not by itself substantially raise the gepotidacin MIC but reduces dual-targeting to single-targeting, predisposing to high-level resistance when a GyrA A92T mutation is also acquired. It was present in all three phase 2 urogenital microbiological failures and in 10.6% of 33,213 global gonococcal genomes.

## Citations
- [Microbiological Analysis from a Phase 2 Randomized Study in Adults Evaluating Single Oral Doses of Gepotidacin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30249694/) (PMID:30249694)

Paxalisib.body:
# Paxalisib

Paxalisib (GDC-0084) is an oral, blood-brain-barrier-penetrant PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway inhibitor studied in diffuse midline [glioma](../disease/glioma.md). It is combined with [ONC201](onc201.md) for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, where the combination has produced symptom resolution and tumor regression in preclinical and preliminary clinical work; a phase 2 study reported tolerability consistent with other PI3K inhibitors.

Peginterferon alfa-2a.body:
# Peginterferon alfa-2a

Peginterferon alfa-2a (pegylated interferon alfa-2a) is a pegylated recombinant interferon with immunomodulatory and antiviral activity, used as a finite-duration immunomodulatory therapy for [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md), peginterferon alfa-2a 180 ug subcutaneously weekly was combined with [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) 200 mg (group 4), producing the highest [HBsAg](../biomedicalmeasure/hepatitis-b-surface-antigen-level.md) loss (23%) and seroconversion (20%) of any group at 24 weeks after end of treatment, but also the most grade 3 or 4 adverse events (50%), including cytopenias such as decreased platelet (57%) and neutrophil (40%) counts.

## Citations

Penicillin-binding protein.body:
# Penicillin-binding protein

Penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) are bacterial transpeptidase enzymes that catalyze cross-linking during peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis. They are the targets of beta-lactam antibacterials: [cefepime](../molecule/cefepime.md) penetrates the cell wall of most Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and binds PBP targets, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis with bactericidal effect. Modification of PBPs by target alteration is one of the resistance mechanisms to cefepime/[enmetazobactam](../molecule/enmetazobactam.md), alongside production of uninhibited beta-lactamases, efflux-pump overexpression, and outer-membrane porin mutations.

## Citations
- [Cefepime/Enmetazobactam: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38761353/) (PMID:38761353)

edges.note: cefepime binds PBPs to inhibit peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis; modification of PBPs by target alteration is one resistance mechanism to cefepime/enmetazobactam

Periorbital edema.body:
# Periorbital edema

Periorbital edema is swelling around the eyes and a characteristic class effect of CSF-1R targeting, attributed to [macrophage](../celltype/macrophage.md) depletion with release of matrix-degrading proteases and proteoglycan deposition. It is a dose-dependent on-target adverse effect of [axatilimab](../molecule/axatilimab.md), occurring in 3%, 23%, and 29% of the 0.3-, 1-, and 3-mg AGAVE-201 dose groups respectively, with no events above grade 1 in the 0.3-mg group. In the phase I/II study it was more common at 3 mg/kg regardless of dosing interval.

Peters 2015 — TAS-102 review.body:
# Peters 2015 — TAS-102 review

This narrative review by Godefridus J. Peters (Therapeutic Advances in Medical Oncology, 2015;7(6):340-356) summarises the therapeutic potential of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102) in gastrointestinal malignancies. It describes the cytotoxic mechanism of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) (thymidylate synthase inhibition and incorporation into DNA), the role of [tipiracil](../molecule/tipiracil.md) in raising trifluridine bioavailability by inhibiting [thymidine phosphorylase](../molecule/thymidine-phosphorylase-protein.md), activity in 5-fluorouracil-resistant models, and combination studies.

The review covers the clinical development of TAS-102 culminating in two placebo-controlled randomized trials in fluoropyrimidine-refractory [metastatic colorectal cancer](../disease/metastatic-colorectal-cancer.md): the Japanese J003 phase 2 study and the worldwide phase 3 [RECOURSE trial](../study/recourse-trial.md), both showing an overall-survival benefit for TAS-102 over placebo.

## Citations

Pharos/TCRD.body:
# Pharos/TCRD

Pharos is the web interface to the Target Central Resource Database (TCRD), which categorizes targets into four tiers of increasing druggability evidence: Tdark (unknown druggability), Tbio (weak evidence), Tchem (drugs with sufficient activity), and Tclin (already targets of approved drugs). At the time of writing it categorized 20,412 targets. In [StarGazer](../methodorprocedure/stargazer.md), Pharos druggability data are acquired in real time via API; the number of distinct druggability levels per target (excluding Tdark) is normalized into one of the five [drug target prioritization](../concept/drug-target-prioritization.md) features.

PheWAS catalog.body:
# PheWAS catalog

The PheWAS catalog is a phenome-wide association study catalog of odds ratios between SNPs and phenotypes derived from electronic medical records (the 2013 version: 3144 SNPs versus 1358 phenotypes from 13,835 individuals of European ancestry). In [StarGazer](../methodorprocedure/stargazer.md), its data are loaded locally and, aggregated with embedded GWAS associations, define the curated list of 1844 phenotypic traits used for [drug target prioritization](../concept/drug-target-prioritization.md); risk alleles (odds ratio >=1) and protective alleles (odds ratio <1) are processed into a normalized feature score.

Piranga trial.body:
# Piranga trial

The Piranga trial (NCT04225715) is a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, controlled, adaptive, open-label platform trial for [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). It evaluated 48 weeks of treatment with [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) 100 mg (group 1), xalnesiran 200 mg (group 2), xalnesiran 200 mg plus [ruzotolimod](../molecule/ruzotolimod.md) 150 mg (group 3), xalnesiran 200 mg plus [peginterferon alfa-2a](../molecule/peginterferon-alfa-2a.md) 180 ug (group 4), or nucleoside/nucleotide analogue (NA) therapy alone (group 5) in 159 participants who had virologic suppression on NA therapy. The primary efficacy end point was [HBsAg](../biomedicalmeasure/hepatitis-b-surface-antigen-level.md) loss (HBsAg <0.05 IU/mL) at 24 weeks after the 48-week treatment period. HBsAg loss occurred in 7%, 3%, 12%, 23%, and 0% of groups 1-5 respectively, demonstrating that adding an immunomodulator (especially peginterferon alfa-2a) was essential for HBsAg loss.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)

Placenta.body:
# Placenta

The placenta is the transient fetomaternal organ that mediates maternal-fetal exchange, including FcRn-dependent transplacental transfer of maternal IgG. Blocking this transfer is the rationale for [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) in [hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn](../disease/hemolytic-disease-of-the-fetus-and-newborn.md), as evaluated in the UNITY study.

## Citations
- [Nipocalimab in Early-Onset Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115062/) (PMID:39115062)
Placenta.description: The transient fetomaternal organ mediating maternal-fetal exchange, including FcRn-dependent transplacental transfer of IgG relevant to nipocalimab therapy in hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

Plasma exchange.body:
# Plasma exchange

Plasma exchange (plasmapheresis) is a therapeutic apheresis procedure that separates and removes plasma to filter out high-molecular-weight pathogenic agents such as antibodies and antigen-antibody complexes. It is a first-line, RCT-proven treatment for [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md): two RCTs (52 participants total) demonstrated short-term improvement versus sham exchange, though benefit often wanes within ~8 weeks, so concurrent therapy (e.g. corticosteroids) is sometimes used. Peripheral-line plasma exchange can enable safer outpatient procedures.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Plasma exchange.description: A therapeutic apheresis procedure that separates and removes plasma from blood to filter out high-molecular-weight pathogenic agents (antibodies and antigen-antibody complexes); a first-line, RCT-proven treatment for CIDP.

edges.note: two RCTs (1986 parallel-group, 1996 cross-over; 52 participants total) showed improved short-term outcome vs sham plasma exchange using the Neuropathy Impairment Score, with re-deterioration in the majority within ~8 weeks in the second; >80% of plasma-exchange responders required no additional therapy in the authors' practice

Plasma kallikrein (protein).body:
# Plasma kallikrein (protein)

Plasma kallikrein is a serine protease of the contact ([kallikrein-kinin](../biologicalpathway/kallikrein-kinin-pathway.md)) activation pathway. It is produced in the liver as the zymogen prekallikrein (encoded by [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md)) and is activated by factor XIIa; the active enzyme cleaves [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md) from high-molecular-weight kininogen, increasing vascular permeability and driving [angioedema attacks](../phenotype/angioedema-attack.md). Normally regulated by [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md), plasma kallikrein is a clinically validated therapeutic target in [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md): it is inhibited by [Plasma kallikrein inhibitors](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md) and its total level is reduced by RNA-silencing and gene-editing approaches such as [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
Plasma kallikrein (protein).description: A serine protease of the contact (kallikrein-kinin) activation pathway, produced in the liver as the zymogen prekallikrein (encoded by KLKB1) and activated by factor XIIa; it cleaves bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen and is a clinically validated therapeutic target for hereditary angioedema.

edges.note: plasma kallikrein is a central protease of the contact activation (kallikrein-kinin) pathway
plasma kallikrein is directly responsible for cleavage of bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen
unchecked plasma kallikrein activity drives excess bradykinin production and angioedema attacks; clinically validated therapeutic target for treatment and prevention of attacks

Plasma kallikrein inhibitors.body:
# Plasma kallikrein inhibitors

Plasma kallikrein inhibitors are a class of agents that reduce [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) activity or total level in the [kallikrein-kinin pathway](../biologicalpathway/kallikrein-kinin-pathway.md), thereby decreasing [bradykinin](../molecule/bradykinin-protein.md) production and preventing or treating bradykinin-mediated swelling in [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). The class spans several modalities: monoclonal antibodies ([lanadelumab](../molecule/lanadelumab.md), STAR-0215), small molecules ([berotralstat](../molecule/berotralstat.md), [sebetralstat](../molecule/sebetralstat.md), ATN-249, KVD-824), the recombinant protein [ecallantide](../molecule/ecallantide.md), the prekallikrein-lowering antisense oligonucleotide [donidalorsen](../molecule/donidalorsen.md), and the gene-editing therapy [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), which lowers total plasma kallikrein by knocking out KLKB1.

## Citations
- [Kallikrein inhibitors for angioedema: the progress of preclinical and early phase studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38366937/) (PMID:38366937)
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
Plasma kallikrein inhibitors.description: A class of therapeutic agents that reduce plasma kallikrein activity in the kallikrein-kinin pathway to prevent or treat bradykinin-mediated angioedema, comprising monoclonal antibodies, small-molecule inhibitors, antisense oligonucleotides, and gene-editing therapies used in hereditary angioedema.

edges.note: class reduces plasma kallikrein activity or level, decreasing bradykinin production
approved (lanadelumab, berotralstat, ecallantide) and investigational kallikrein-directed agents for prophylaxis or on-demand treatment of HAE

Plasma trifluridine exposure.body:
# Plasma trifluridine exposure

Plasma trifluridine exposure is the systemic pharmacokinetic exposure to [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md), quantified by the area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC0-last and AUC0-inf) and the maximum observed concentration (Cmax). Trifluridine AUC0-last and Cmax after the single morning dose were the primary endpoints of the phase 1 [Belani 2017](../study/belani-2017-trifluridine-tipiracil-pk-study.md) study.

Coadministration of [tipiracil](../molecule/tipiracil.md) (as [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md)) raised trifluridine AUC0-last ~37-fold (6618 vs 176 ng*h/mL) and Cmax ~22-fold (2155 vs 96 ng/mL) versus trifluridine alone, while plasma concentrations of trifluridine alone were also much more variable (Cmax CV 92% vs 44%).

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of trifluridine and tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)
Plasma trifluridine exposure.description: The systemic pharmacokinetic exposure to trifluridine in plasma, quantified by area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-last/AUC0-inf) and maximum observed concentration (Cmax); the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint of the phase 1 trifluridine/tipiracil study.

edges.note: trifluridine AUC0-last and Cmax (single morning dose) were the primary endpoints comparing trifluridine/tipiracil with trifluridine alone, determined by noncompartmental methods

Plasmablast.body:
# Plasmablast

Plasmablasts are late-stage, antibody-secreting B-lineage cells that retain [CD19](../molecule/b-lymphocyte-antigen-cd19-protein.md) expression while having lost CD20, making them targetable by CD19-directed (but not CD20-directed) depletion. IgG4-related disease is associated with striking oligoclonal expansions of circulating plasmablasts. [Inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) rapidly depletes peripheral CD20- plasmablasts and plasma cells, an advantage over anti-CD20 strategies.

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
Plasmablast.description: A late-stage, antibody-secreting B-lineage cell that retains CD19 expression while losing CD20; expands oligoclonally in IgG4-related disease and is depleted by inebilizumab.

edges.note: plasmablasts are a late B-lineage differentiation stage that retain CD19 (targetable by inebilizumab) while losing CD20

Platelet count decreased.body:
# Platelet count decreased

Decreased platelet count (thrombocytopenia) is a cytopenic adverse effect of interferon-based therapy. In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md), it occurred in 57% of participants receiving [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) plus [peginterferon alfa-2a](../molecule/peginterferon-alfa-2a.md) (group 4), the highest of any group, alongside decreased neutrophil count (40%); cytopenias and elevated liver-enzyme levels were most frequent in the peginterferon alfa-2a group.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Platelet count decreased.description: A reduction in the circulating platelet count; a known cytopenic adverse effect of interferon-based therapy.

Powell 2022 — gepotidacin juvenile rat a.body:
# Powell 2022 — gepotidacin juvenile rat arthropathy

This nonclinical study (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2022) assessed oral [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) toxicity and toxicokinetics in juvenile Long Evans rats from postnatal day 4 to 32/35, with macroscopic and microscopic skeletal examinations of the femoral head and stifle joint to detect fluoroquinolone-like [arthropathy](../phenotype/arthropathy.md). No arthropathy was observed at the highest tolerated dose, supporting potential pediatric use.

## Citations
- [Novel Bacterial Topoisomerase Inhibitor Gepotidacin Demonstrates Absence of Fluoroquinolone-Like Arthropathy in Juvenile Rats](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36255258/) (PMID:36255258)
Powell 2022 — gepotidacin juvenile rat a.description: Nonclinical juvenile rat toxicity and toxicokinetics study assessing whether gepotidacin causes fluoroquinolone-like arthropathy on articular surfaces of the femoral head and stifle joint.

Progression-free survival.body:
# Progression-free survival

Progression-free survival (PFS) is the time from enrollment or randomization to documented disease progression (per RECIST v1.1) or death from any cause. It was the principal efficacy endpoint across the EMBER program: a secondary endpoint in the phase 1 [EMBER trial](../study/ember-trial.md) and [endometrial cohort](../study/ember-trial-endometrial-cohort.md), and the primary endpoint for all three between-group comparisons of the phase 3 [EMBER-3 trial](../study/ember-3-trial.md). [Imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md) prolonged PFS over standard endocrine therapy in [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md)-mutant patients, and imlunestrant + [abemaciclib](../molecule/abemaciclib.md) improved PFS over imlunestrant alone.

## Citations
- [EMBER-3 phase 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660834/) (PMID:39660834)
Progression-free survival.description: The time from enrollment or randomization until documented disease progression or death from any cause; the primary efficacy endpoint of the EMBER program trials, estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method.

edges.note: primary endpoint per RECIST v1.1; assessed by investigator and blinded independent central review

Proton therapy.body:
# Proton therapy

Proton therapy delivers external-beam radiation using protons, whose Bragg-peak dose deposition reduces exit dose to surrounding normal brain. The [glioma treatment review](../publication/glioma-treatment-review-2024.md) highlights its growing role in pediatric low-grade [glioma](../disease/glioma.md): a prospective study of 174 children reported 5-year progression-free survival of 84% and overall survival of 92%, with potential improvements in quality of life and cost-effectiveness compared with older photon techniques.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Proton therapy.description: A form of external-beam radiotherapy using protons to deposit dose with a sharp Bragg peak, reducing exit dose to normal tissue; increasingly used in pediatric low-grade glioma to reduce late toxicity.

edges.note: prospective study of 174 pediatric low-grade glioma patients receiving proton therapy reported 5-year PFS 84% and OS 92% (median follow-up 4.4 years); reduces radiation exit dose and may improve quality of life

Pulmonary exacerbation rate.body:
# Pulmonary exacerbation rate

The pulmonary (acute respiratory) exacerbation rate is the number of acute exacerbations per unit time. It is the primary endpoint of the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), measured over 12 months in [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md) and analysed by negative binomial regression; the trial is powered to detect a 40% reduction (controls 3/year vs intervention 1.8/year) with [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) versus placebo. Reducing exacerbations is also cited as a benefit of mucoactive drugs in the [Crisafulli 2007 pilot study](../study/crisafulli-2007-erdosteine-in-bronchiectasis.md).

## Citations
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
- [Effectiveness of erdosteine in elderly patients with bronchiectasis and hypersecretion (Crisafulli)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18035199/) (PMID:18035199)
Pulmonary exacerbation rate.description: The rate (number per unit time, eg per year) of acute respiratory exacerbations - episodes of new or worsening respiratory symptoms requiring treatment change - in chronic lung disease such as bronchiectasis and COPD.

edges.note: BETTER trial primary endpoint - acute respiratory exacerbation rate by 12 months, analysed by negative binomial regression

QT prolongation.body:
# QT prolongation

QT prolongation is a concentration-dependent cardiac adverse effect of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md). A thorough QT study found a slope of 1.45 ms/ug/mL between gepotidacin plasma concentration and change in QTcF; plasma concentrations are kept below 14 ug/mL (predicted to correspond to a ~20 ms QT increase) to limit clinically relevant prolongation, which guided dose selection. No patient in the EAGLE trials had a post-baseline QTcF >500 ms or change from baseline >60 ms.

## Citations
- [Dose selection for a phase III study evaluating gepotidacin (GSK2140944) in the treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36411033/) (PMID:36411033)
QT prolongation.description: A concentration-dependent prolongation of the cardiac QT interval observed with gepotidacin; plasma concentrations are kept below 14 ug/mL to limit clinically relevant QTc prolongation.

edges.object: Scangarella-Oman 2022 — gonorrhoea phase III dose selection
edges.primary_source: Scangarella-Oman 2022 — gonorrhoea phase III dose selection

Quality of life.body:
# Quality of life

Quality of life (QoL) is a key patient-reported secondary outcome of the [BETTER trial](../study/better-trial.md), assessed at 12 months in people with [bronchiectasis](../disease/bronchiectasis.md). Adults complete the 37-item bronchiectasis QoL tool (B-QoL, with a respiratory subdomain) and children the validated Parent-proxy Cough QoL-8 (PC-QoL). The minimal clinically important difference is 0.9 (SD 1.8) for PC-QoL and 7-10 (SD 17, domain-dependent) for B-QoL. The secondary hypothesis is that regular [erdosteine](../molecule/erdosteine.md) improves QoL versus placebo.

## Citations
- [Erdosteine in children and adults with bronchiectasis (BETTER trial)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38719503/) (PMID:38719503)
Quality of life.description: A patient-reported outcome capturing health-related quality of life; in the BETTER trial assessed with the bronchiectasis QoL tool (B-QoL) for adults and the Parent-proxy Cough QoL-8 (PC-QoL) for children.

edges.note: key secondary outcome at 12 months - B-QoL (37-item, adults) and PC-QoL (children); MCID 0.9 (SD 1.8) for PC-QoL and 7-10 (SD 17) domain-dependent for B-QoL

RECOURSE trial.body:
# RECOURSE trial

RECOURSE was a worldwide (Japan, USA, Europe, Australia), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial that evaluated [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102, 70 mg/m2/day) versus placebo in 800 patients (2:1 randomization, 534 vs 266) with [metastatic colorectal cancer](../disease/metastatic-colorectal-cancer.md) refractory to or progressive on standard systemic therapy (fluoropyrimidines, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, bevacizumab). As summarised in the [Peters 2015 review](../publication/peters-2015-tas-102-review.md), TAS-102 improved median [overall survival](../biomedicalmeasure/overall-survival.md) (7.1 vs 5.3 months; HR 0.68; p<0.001) and [progression-free survival](../biomedicalmeasure/progression-free-survival.md) (2.0 vs 1.7 months; HR 0.48; p<0.001), with a disease control rate of 44% versus 16%.

The RECOURSE results led to regulatory approval of trifluridine/tipiracil for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. The main toxicity was hematologic (grade 3 neutropenia in 38% of the TAS-102 group), without fluoropyrimidine-typical toxicities such as hand-foot syndrome.

## Citations
- [Randomized trial of TAS-102 for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25970050/) (PMID:25970050)
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
RECOURSE trial.description: Worldwide (Japan, USA, Europe, Australia), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial of trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102, 70 mg/m2/day) versus placebo in 800 patients (2:1 randomization, 534 vs 266) with metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to standard chemotherapy, as described in the Peters 2015 review.

edges.note: patients progressive on systemic anticancer treatment (fluoropyrimidines, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, bevacizumab); at least two prior regimens, majority four
primary endpoint

Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2.body:
# Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 (protein)

Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 (HER2, encoded by ERBB2) is a member of the ERBB family of receptor tyrosine kinases. In NRG1-driven cancers it acts as the catalytically active dimerization partner for the pseudokinase [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md): [NRG1](../molecule/neuregulin-1-protein.md)-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimers phosphorylate HER3 and propagate [PI3K-AKT signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md), and HER2-HER3 dimers may be the most oncogenic ERBB heterodimers. [Zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) docks onto the more abundant HER2 with one Fab arm as the first step of its Dock & Block mechanism.

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2.description: A member of the ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase family encoded by ERBB2; it serves as a dimerization partner for HER3 in NRG1-driven signaling and is one of the two targets of the bispecific antibody zenocutuzumab.

edges.note: HER2-HER3 dimers may represent the most oncogenic heterodimers of the ERBB family; HER2 phosphorylates HER3 to propagate signaling
NRG1-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimerization; in cells expressing only HER2 and HER3, NRG1 induces phosphorylation of both

edges.object: The phase I/II eNRGy trial — zenocutuzumab in NRG1 fusion cancers
edges.primary_source: The phase I/II eNRGy trial — zenocutuzumab in NRG1 fusion cancers

Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-3.body:
# Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-3 (protein)

Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-3 (HER3, encoded by ERBB3) is the predominant receptor for [neuregulin 1](../molecule/neuregulin-1-protein.md) and oncogenic NRG1 fusion ligands. HER3 is a pseudokinase with little intrinsic enzymatic activity and is a dependent heterodimerization partner: on NRG1 binding it dimerizes with [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md), EGFR or HER4, becomes phosphorylated, and forms docking sites that activate [PI3K-AKT signaling](../biologicalpathway/her2-her3-pi3k-akt-signaling.md). [Zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) positions its HER3 Fab arm to block NRG1 binding to HER3 and prevent the conformational change required for HER2-HER3 heterodimerization ("block").

## Citations
- [Zenocutuzumab, a HER2xHER3 Bispecific Antibody, Is Effective Therapy for Tumors Driven by NRG1 Gene Rearrangements](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35135829/) (PMID:35135829)
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-3.description: A pseudokinase member of the ERBB receptor family encoded by ERBB3 and the predominant receptor for NRG1; on NRG1 binding it heterodimerizes with HER2 (and EGFR/HER4) to activate PI3K-AKT signaling, and it is the second target of zenocutuzumab's Dock & Block mechanism.

edges.note: HER3 is the predominant receptor for NRG1 and oncogenic NRG1 fusion ligands
HER3 is a pseudokinase that, when phosphorylated by partner ERBB receptors, forms docking sites for SH2-domain proteins and activates the PI3K pathway
NRG1-induced HER3 heterodimerization with HER2

Riedl 2024 — hepatic targeting in HAE.body:
# Riedl 2024 — hepatic targeting in HAE

This clinical commentary review (J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract 2024;12:911-8) summarizes hepatic-focused investigational prophylactic therapies for [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md) that have advanced into human trials. The liver is the primary site of production of [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md), prekallikrein, high-molecular-weight kininogen, and factor XII, making it a central therapeutic target. Reviewed agents include the GalNAc3-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide [donidalorsen](../molecule/donidalorsen.md), the GalNAc3-conjugated siRNA ADX-324, the AAV5 gene therapy BMN 331 (expressing wild-type human C1INH from SERPING1), and the in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md), which targets [KLKB1](../gene/klkb1-gene.md).

## Citations
- [Clinical Progress in Hepatic Targeting for Novel Prophylactic Therapies in Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142864/) (PMID:38142864)
Riedl 2024 — hepatic targeting in HAE.description: Clinical commentary review of hepatic-focused investigational prophylactic therapies for hereditary angioedema that have advanced into human trials, covering GalNAc-conjugated antisense (donidalorsen) and siRNA (ADX-324), AAV5 gene therapy (BMN 331), and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing (NTLA-2002).

Rituximab.body:
# Rituximab

Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that depletes B cells and the pathogenic autoantibodies they produce. In [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md) it is used off-label, especially in refractory disease, supported by numerous case series (e.g. ~70% responder rate within a median of 2 months in 13 Italian cases), at doses of 2 g total over 2 weeks or 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks. A randomized controlled trial is ongoing to determine whether rituximab can allow suspension of IVIg without clinical worsening.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Rituximab.description: An anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that depletes B cells; used off-label in refractory CIDP based on case series and currently the subject of a randomized controlled trial.

edges.note: case series evidence (e.g. 13 Italian cases) reported ~70% responder rate within a median of 2 months lasting up to 1 year, particularly in refractoriness; an ongoing Italian RCT (EudraCT 2017-005034-36) aims to assess whether rituximab allows IVIg suspension without worsening

stats.dose: 2 g total over 2 weeks or 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks

Rozanolixizumab.body:
# Rozanolixizumab

Rozanolixizumab is a high-affinity humanized anti-[FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) IgG4 monoclonal antibody in the [FcRn-blocker class](../molecularclass/anti-fcrn-monoclonal-antibodies.md). Unlike efgartigimod, its [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md) RCT (completed March 2021, results unpublished) appeared negative for the primary outcome (change in I-RODS at week 13), with lack of efficacy in 5/17 treated versus 4/17 placebo subjects and no between-group difference in I-RODS logit score.

## Citations
- [Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Outlooks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38435981/) (PMID:38435981)
Rozanolixizumab.description: A high-affinity humanized anti-FcRn IgG4 monoclonal antibody; in a CIDP RCT it appeared negative for the primary outcome (I-RODS change at week 13).

edges.note: high-affinity human anti-FcRn IgG4 monoclonal antibody
high-affinity anti-FcRn antibody blocking IgG recycling
CIDP RCT (ended March 2021, results unpublished) appeared negative for primary outcome; lack of efficacy in 5/17 treated vs 4/17 placebo and no inter-group difference in I-RODS logit change

Russo 2023 — anti-CGRP mAbs for vestibul.body:
# Russo 2023 — anti-CGRP mAbs for vestibular migraine

This prospective observational cohort study (Russo et al., Cephalalgia 2023) enrolled 50 chronic migraine patients meeting criteria for [vestibular migraine](../disease/vestibular-migraine.md) at the Headache Center of University Federico II of Naples, treated between November 2020 and June 2021 with [erenumab](../molecule/erenumab.md) (140 mg), [fremanezumab](../molecule/fremanezumab.md) (225 mg), or [galcanezumab](../molecule/galcanezumab.md) (240 mg loading then 120 mg). It was the first prospective study aimed specifically at demonstrating efficacy of [anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies](../molecularclass/anti-cgrp-monoclonal-antibodies.md) in vestibular migraine.

Response was excellent: 45 (90%) patients had at least a 50% reduction in monthly dizziness/vestibular symptom days, 43 (86%) at least a 50% reduction in headache frequency, and 40 (80%) at least a 50% MIDAS reduction at 12 months; 39 (78%) had a concomitant reduction in all three. Mean monthly dizziness days fell from 10.3 to 0.8 (difference 9.5; 95% CI 3.6-15.4; p<0.001) by 12 months. No significant efficacy difference was found among the three antibodies.

## Citations

Ruzotolimod.body:
# Ruzotolimod

Ruzotolimod (RO7020531) is an investigational oral toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) agonist that is selectively activated in the liver, evaluated as an immunomodulator to restore the dysregulated antiviral immune response in [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md), ruzotolimod 150 mg orally every other day was combined with [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) 200 mg (group 3), achieving HBsAg loss in 12% of participants at 24 weeks after end of treatment. Influenza-like illness (47%) and pyrexia, biologic markers of on-target [TLR7](../molecule/toll-like-receptor-7-protein.md) activation, were the characteristic adverse effects.

SERPING1 (gene).body:
# SERPING1 (gene)

SERPING1 is the human gene encoding [C1 esterase inhibitor](../molecule/c1-esterase-inhibitor-protein.md) (C1INH), produced primarily by the liver. Pathogenic SERPING1 variants are the predominant cause of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md): type 1 (~85% of cases) arises from variants producing a truncated or misfolded C1INH that cannot be secreted (quantitative deficiency), while type 2 (~15%) arises from variants yielding dysfunctional C1INH. The AAV5 gene therapy BMN 331 (AAV5 hSERPING1) and ex vivo gene therapy OTL-105 aim to restore functional C1INH by delivering or correcting SERPING1.

STRING database.body:
# STRING database

STRING is a database of known and predicted protein-protein interactions (functional associations, including experimentally confirmed, predicted, and text-mined interactions). Version 11.5 contained over 20 billion interactions across 14,094 organisms, of which StarGazer uses human and orthologous genes. In [StarGazer](../methodorprocedure/stargazer.md), STRING data are acquired in real time via API; the node degree (number of proteins directly connected to a target node), normalized to the highest node degree in the network, contributes one of the five [drug target prioritization](../concept/drug-target-prioritization.md) features, and STRING also performs gene-ontology enrichment analysis.

## Citations

# Scangarella-Oman 2018 — phase 2 gonorrhoea microbiological analysis

This article (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2018) reports the microbiological correlates of treatment success from a phase 2 randomized, open-label, dose-ranging single-oral-dose study of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) for [uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea](../disease/uncomplicated-urogenital-gonorrhoea.md). It includes susceptibility testing, QRDR genotyping of GyrA and ParC, frequency-of-resistance, and fAUC/MIC efficacy assessments for 69 microbiologically evaluable participants.

This narrative review (Sex Transm Infect 2022) summarises how in vitro hollow-fibre infection model PK/PD data, phase II clinical data, and population PK modelling/simulation were combined to select the [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) dosing regimen (two 3000 mg oral doses 10-12 h apart) for the phase III [uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhoea](../disease/uncomplicated-urogenital-gonorrhoea.md) study, balancing efficacy, resistance suppression, and QT-prolongation safety limits.

Sebetralstat.body:
# Sebetralstat

Sebetralstat (KVD900; KalVista Pharmaceuticals) is an investigational oral small-molecule inhibitor of [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) developed for on-demand treatment of [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md) attacks. It is rapidly absorbed (measurable plasma levels 10-20 minutes after oral dosing, peak within 1 hour) and strongly inhibits plasma kallikrein activity and downstream factor XIIa generation during kallikrein-kinin system activation. In a phase 2 crossover trial of 68 patients, a single 600 mg dose significantly extended the time to use of conventional attack treatment within 12 hours versus placebo (P=0.0010). As a [plasma kallikrein inhibitor](../molecularclass/plasma-kallikrein-inhibitors.md), it was well tolerated with mostly mild adverse events.

## Citations

Selective estrogen receptor degraders.body:
# Selective estrogen receptor degraders

Selective estrogen receptor degraders (SERDs) are endocrine therapies that antagonize [estrogen receptor alpha](../molecule/estrogen-receptor-alpha-protein.md) transcriptional activity and promote its degradation, achieving more complete inhibition of estrogen signaling than aromatase inhibitors or selective ER modulators. The class includes [fulvestrant](../molecule/fulvestrant.md), [elacestrant](../molecule/elacestrant.md), and the next-generation, brain-penetrant oral SERD [imlunestrant](../molecule/imlunestrant.md). Next-generation oral SERDs were developed to overcome fulvestrant's intramuscular administration and limited efficacy in [ESR1](../gene/esr1-gene.md)-mutant disease.

## Citations
- [Phase Ia/Ib EMBER Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39241211/) (PMID:39241211)

Serum IgG level.body:
# Serum IgG level

Serum IgG level is the concentration of total [immunoglobulin G](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) in serum and the primary pharmacodynamic readout of [FcRn](../molecule/neonatal-fc-receptor-protein.md) blockade. Across the nipocalimab studies, single IV doses lowered serum IgG by ~49% (10 mg/kg), ~64-69% (30 mg/kg) and ~76-80% (60 mg/kg), with maternal IgG falling ~85% in the UNITY pregnancy study; the percent reduction tracks the therapeutic and on-target effect of [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md).

# Serum transthyretin level

Serum transthyretin level is the serum concentration of [transthyretin](../molecule/transthyretin-protein.md) protein, the primary pharmacodynamic measure of TTR-lowering therapies in [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). Sjögren's disease.body:
# Sjögren's disease

Sjögren's disease is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease with lymphocytic infiltration of the exocrine glands. It is named among the autoantibody-mediated diseases (with myasthenia gravis, warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia and rheumatoid arthritis) whose pathogenesis involves [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) and for which [nipocalimab](../molecule/nipocalimab.md) and FcRn blockade are under evaluation.

Small interfering RNA therapeutics.body:
# Small interfering RNA therapeutics

Small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics are double-stranded RNA molecules that degrade a target messenger RNA through RNA interference. They offer high specificity, potent activity, reversibility, and durable gene silencing with infrequent dosing, and are frequently conjugated to N-acetyl-D-galactosamine (GalNAc) for selective hepatic uptake. [Xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) (targeting the hepatitis B virus genome) and [zodasiran](../molecule/zodasiran.md) (targeting [ANGPTL3](../gene/angptl3-gene.md)) are members of this class.

# Staphylococcus aureus

Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive coccus and WHO high-priority pathogen that can survive intracellularly within host phagocytes, contributing to persistent and recurrent skin and respiratory infections. [Gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) is bactericidal against it (including MRSA and fluoroquinolone-resistant strains) with MIC90 0.5 ug/mL, and reduces the intracellular bacterial burden in cultured phagocytic cells irrespective of resistance phenotype.

StarGazer.body:
# StarGazer

StarGazer is a Python-based Streamlit hybrid intelligence dashboard (AstraZeneca) for [drug target prioritization](../concept/drug-target-prioritization.md) and digital [drug repositioning](../concept/drug-repositioning.md). It integrates three data types — disease-target association, target druggability, and protein-protein interaction — from four open-access databases: the [PheWAS catalog](../dataset/phewas-catalog.md), [Open Targets](../dataset/open-targets.md), [Pharos/TCRD](../dataset/pharos-tcrd.md), and the [STRING database](../dataset/string-database.md). Five features (GWAS/PheWAS odds ratios, Open Targets association, Pharos druggability, STRING node degree, and presence in both PheWAS and GWAS) are normalized and summed into an overall StarGazer score (maximum 1) that ranks genes by drug repositioning potential for any of 1844 phenotypic traits. A use case applied it to insomnia, returning 106 associated genes ranked by score.

## Citations
- [StarGazer: A Hybrid Intelligence Platform for Drug Target Prioritization and Digital Drug Repositioning Using Streamlit](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35711912/) (PMID:35711912)
StarGazer.description: A Python-based Streamlit hybrid intelligence dashboard (AstraZeneca) that integrates disease-target association, target druggability, and protein-protein interaction data from four open-access databases into a single normalized scoring system to prioritize drug targets and identify drug repositioning candidates across 1844 phenotypic traits.

Subcutaneous immunoglobulin.body:
# Subcutaneous immunoglobulin

Subcutaneous immunoglobulin (SCIg) is pooled human [IgG](../molecule/immunoglobulin-g.md) given subcutaneously, increasingly used as convenient home/self-administered maintenance therapy in IVIg-responsive [CIDP](../disease/chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-polyradiculoneuropathy.md). A large international RCT (172 subjects) showed 0.2 g/kg weekly SCIg prevents relapse versus placebo (no added benefit at 0.4 g/kg), and ADVANCE-CIDP 1 (132 subjects) showed hyaluronidase-facilitated SCIg 10% gave a >20% relapse-rate reduction versus placebo while permitting infusions as infrequent as 4-weekly.

## Citations

Surgical resection of glioma.body:
# Surgical resection of glioma

Surgical resection is the primary cytoreductive treatment for [glioma](../disease/glioma.md), aiming to maximize the extent of resection (ideally gross total resection) while preserving neurological function and quality of life. The [glioma treatment review](../publication/glioma-treatment-review-2024.md) emphasizes that extent of resection strongly influences progression-free and overall survival, with gross total resection improving outcomes especially in younger patients; supratotal/subtotal resection and laser interstitial thermal therapy are being explored to balance benefit against morbidity.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Surgical resection of glioma.description: Cytoreductive neurosurgery for glioma aiming to maximize extent of resection (ideally gross total resection) while preserving neurological function and quality of life; extent of resection is a strong determinant of survival.

edges.note: achieving gross total resection significantly improves survival in low- and high-grade glioma, particularly in younger patients; extent of resection is measured by FLAIR signal removed (LGG) or enhancing/necrotic tissue removed (HGG)
subtotal/supratotal resection strategies and laser interstitial thermal therapy explored to balance survival benefit against neurological morbidity

TNFSF15 (gene).body:
# TNFSF15 (gene)

TNFSF15 is the human gene encoding [TL1A](../molecule/tumor-necrosis-factor-like-cytokine-1a-protein.md) (tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A). Both TNFSF15 and TNFRSF25 (encoding the TL1A receptor DR3) have been confirmed as [inflammatory bowel disease](../disease/inflammatory-bowel-disease.md)-susceptibility genes across diverse populations. In the [ARTEMIS-UC trial](../study/artemis-uc-trial.md), a genetic-based diagnostic test was designed to identify [ulcerative colitis](../disease/ulcerative-colitis.md) patients more likely to respond to the anti-TL1A antibody [tulisokibart](../molecule/tulisokibart.md), based on a propensity to overexpress TL1A.

## Citations
- [Phase 2 Trial of Anti-TL1A Monoclonal Antibody Tulisokibart for Ulcerative Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321363/) (PMID:39321363)
TNFSF15 (gene).description: The human gene encoding TL1A (tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A); a confirmed inflammatory bowel disease-susceptibility gene across diverse populations and the gene whose product is targeted by the anti-TL1A antibody tulisokibart.

edges.note: TNFSF15 encodes TL1A
TNFSF15 (encoding TL1A) confirmed as an inflammatory bowel disease-susceptibility gene across diverse populations, including Crohn's disease susceptibility SNPs

TTR (gene).body:
# TTR (gene)

TTR is the human gene encoding [transthyretin](../molecule/transthyretin-protein.md) (prealbumin), a transport protein for thyroid hormone and retinol (vitamin A), produced mainly by [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md). Misfolded transthyretin deposits as amyloid fibrils in [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md); both wild-type TTR and pathogenic TTR variants (such as [p.Val142Ile](../variant/ttr-v142i.md)) can drive the disease. TTR is the therapeutic target of [nexiguran ziclumeran](../molecule/nexiguran-ziclumeran.md), an in vivo [CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing](../methodorprocedure/crispr-cas9-gene-editing.md) therapy that permanently knocks out the gene in hepatocytes.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Nexiguran Ziclumeran for ATTR Cardiomyopathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555828/) (PMID:39555828)
TTR (gene).description: The human gene encoding transthyretin (prealbumin), a serum and cerebrospinal fluid transport protein for thyroid hormone and retinol-binding protein; it is produced mainly by hepatocytes and is the target gene knocked out by the in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy nexiguran ziclumeran for transthyretin amyloidosis.

edges.note: TTR encodes transthyretin (prealbumin), the protein deposited as amyloid fibrils in ATTR amyloidosis
hepatocytes are the main source of circulating TTR protein
pathogenic TTR variants (e.g. p.Val142Ile) cause hereditary variant ATTR-CM; wild-type TTR underlies wild-type ATTR-CM

TTR V142I.body:
# TTR V142I

TTR V142I (p.Val142Ile, historically V122I) is a pathogenic missense substitution in the [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md) gene and the most common hereditary variant causing variant [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). In the [nexiguran ziclumeran phase 1 trial](../study/nexiguran-ziclumeran-phase-1-attr-cm-trial.md), 7 of 36 patients (19%) carried p.Val142Ile, two of whom were homozygous; it was the most frequent of five different pathogenic TTR variants represented among the 31% of patients with variant ATTR-CM.

## Citations

TTR V142I.description: A pathogenic missense substitution in the transthyretin gene (valine to isoleucine), the most common hereditary variant causing variant transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, particularly among people of African ancestry.

TYMP (gene).body:
# TYMP (gene)

TYMP is the human gene encoding [thymidine phosphorylase](../molecule/thymidine-phosphorylase-protein.md) (TP / platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor, PDECGF). The encoded enzyme degrades thymidine and the nucleoside analog [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md), and its inhibition by [tipiracil](../molecule/tipiracil.md) underlies the [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102) combination. TP/PDECGF is frequently overexpressed in colorectal and gastric tumors, where it promotes angiogenesis.

## Citations
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
TYMP (gene).description: The human gene encoding thymidine phosphorylase (also known as platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor), the enzyme that degrades thymidine and trifluridine and is the target of tipiracil.

TYMS (gene).body:
# TYMS (gene)

TYMS is the human gene encoding [thymidylate synthase](../molecule/thymidylate-synthase-protein.md) (TS), the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo thymidine monophosphate synthesis and a central target of fluoropyrimidine and antifolate chemotherapy. The active monophosphate metabolite of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) inhibits the encoded enzyme as a secondary mechanism of action of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md).

## Citations
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
TYMS (gene).description: The human gene encoding thymidylate synthase, the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo dTMP synthesis and a central target of fluoropyrimidine and antifolate chemotherapy.

Temozolomide.body:
# Temozolomide

Temozolomide (TMZ) is an oral alkylating (DNA-methylating) chemotherapeutic that forms the backbone of standard-of-care treatment for newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype [glioblastoma](../disease/glioblastoma.md): maximal safe surgery, radiotherapy with concomitant temozolomide (200 mg/m2, days 1-5 of 28-day cycles), and six adjuvant maintenance cycles. Its efficacy depends strongly on [MGMT](../gene/mgmt-gene.md) promoter methylation, and unmethylated tumors respond poorly, motivating temozolomide-omission strategies in elderly patients. In the [STEAM trial](../study/eortc-1608-steam-trial.md) it served as the combination partner for [zotiraciclib](../molecule/zotiraciclib.md) in group B.

## Citations
- [Zotiraciclib (TG02) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in the elderly or for recurrent glioblastoma: The EORTC 1608 STEAM trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38159337/) (PMID:38159337)
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Temozolomide.description: An oral alkylating (methylating) chemotherapeutic agent that is the backbone of standard-of-care chemoradiotherapy for newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype glioblastoma; its activity is strongly dependent on MGMT promoter methylation status.

edges.note: standard of care for newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype glioblastoma is surgery then radiotherapy with concomitant temozolomide plus six maintenance cycles; poor activity in MGMT promoter-unmethylated tumors; standard regimen 200 mg/m2 days 1-5 of 28-day cycles
conventional chemotherapy backbone in high-grade glioma, used with radiotherapy and surgical resection
temozolomide benefit depends on MGMT promoter methylation; MGMT-unmethylated tumors derive little benefit, motivating temozolomide-omission trials

The phase I/II eNRGy trial — zenocutuzum.body:
# The phase I/II eNRGy trial — zenocutuzumab in NRG1 fusion cancers

This article describes the rationale and design of the phase II component of the open-label phase I/II [eNRGy trial](../study/enrgy-trial.md) (NCT02912949), which evaluates [zenocutuzumab](../molecule/zenocutuzumab.md) in patients with [NRG1 fusion-positive cancer](../disease/nrg1-fusion-positive-cancer.md). It reviews the biology of [NRG1 gene fusions](../variant/nrg1-gene-fusion.md) as oncogenic drivers (rare, <1% of solid tumors; enriched in IMA of the lung and KRAS-wildtype PDAC), the Dock & Block mechanism of zenocutuzumab against [HER2](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-2-protein.md) and [HER3](../molecule/receptor-tyrosine-protein-kinase-erbb-3-protein.md), and the trial's eligibility criteria, procedures, and endpoints.

The paper presents no efficacy results; it specifies the primary endpoint ([objective response rate](../biomedicalmeasure/objective-response-rate.md)), key secondary endpoint ([duration of response](../biomedicalmeasure/duration-of-response.md)), and planned sample sizes (up to 100 NSCLC, 50 PDAC, 100 basket; maximum 250 overall).

## Citations
- [The phase I/II eNRGy trial: Zenocutuzumab in patients with cancers harboring NRG1 gene fusions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38348690/) (PMID:38348690)
The phase I/II eNRGy trial — zenocutuzum.description: A trial design and rationale article describing the phase II component of the open-label phase I/II eNRGy trial (NCT02912949) of zenocutuzumab in patients with NRG1 fusion-positive NSCLC, PDAC and other solid tumors.

Therapeutic response rate.body:
# Therapeutic response rate

The therapeutic response rate (therapeutic success) is a composite efficacy endpoint, recommended by FDA and EMA guidance, combining per-participant clinical success (total symptom score of 0, i.e. complete symptom resolution) and microbiological success (reduction of qualifying uropathogens from >=10^5 CFU/mL at baseline to <10^3 CFU/mL) without other systemic antibiotic use, assessed at test-of-cure. It was the primary endpoint of the [EAGLE-2](../study/eagle-2-trial.md) and [EAGLE-3](../study/eagle-3-trial.md) trials of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md) for [uncomplicated urinary tract infection](../disease/uncomplicated-urinary-tract-infection.md). For gonorrhoea, the analogous microbiological success measure is culture-confirmed eradication of N. gonorrhoeae at test-of-cure.

## Citations
- [Design of Two Phase III, Randomized, Multicenter Studies Comparing Gepotidacin with Nitrofurantoin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36271314/) (PMID:36271314)
Therapeutic response rate.description: A composite efficacy endpoint combining per-participant clinical success (complete symptom resolution) and microbiological success (reduction of qualifying uropathogens to <10^3 CFU/mL) at test-of-cure; the primary endpoint of the EAGLE uUTI trials.

Thrombocytopenia.body:
# Thrombocytopenia

Thrombocytopenia is an abnormally low platelet count. In the [glioma treatment review](../publication/glioma-treatment-review-2024.md) it is reported, along with photosensitivity, as one of the most frequent (reversible) adverse events of [depatuxizumab mafodotin](../molecule/depatuxizumab-mafodotin.md) in glioblastoma.

## Citations
- [Focus on current and emerging treatment options for glioma: A comprehensive review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689623/) (PMID:38689623)
Thrombocytopenia.description: An abnormally low platelet count; reported as a reversible adverse event of the EGFR antibody-drug conjugate depatuxizumab mafodotin in glioblastoma.

Thymidine monophosphate.body:
# Thymidine monophosphate

Thymidine monophosphate (dTMP, thymidylate) is the deoxyribonucleotide produced by [thymidylate synthase](../molecule/thymidylate-synthase-protein.md)-catalyzed reductive methylation of dUMP, and is an essential precursor for DNA synthesis. Inhibition of thymidylate synthase by the active monophosphate metabolite of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) depletes intracellular dTMP/dTTP and leads to dUMP accumulation, contributing to the cytotoxicity of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md).

## Citations
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Thymidine monophosphate.description: The deoxyribonucleotide thymidine monophosphate (dTMP), the product of thymidylate synthase-catalyzed reductive methylation of dUMP and an essential precursor for DNA synthesis.

Thymidine phosphorylase (protein).body:
# Thymidine phosphorylase (protein)

Thymidine phosphorylase (TP), encoded by [TYMP](../gene/tymp-gene.md) and also known as platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PDECGF), is a pyrimidine nucleoside phosphorylase found in the gastrointestinal tract, liver, and tumor tissue. It catalyzes the phosphorolysis of thymidine and of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md), degrading the latter to the inactive metabolite FTY and thereby causing trifluridine's poor oral bioavailability.

It is the molecular target of [tipiracil](../molecule/tipiracil.md), whose inhibition of TP allows clinical use of trifluridine. TP/PDECGF is an angiogenic enzyme overexpressed in colorectal and gastric tumors and is associated with poor prognosis; its breakdown product 2-deoxy-D-ribose promotes tumor angiogenesis, an effect also inhibited by tipiracil.

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of trifluridine and tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Thymidine phosphorylase (protein).description: A pyrimidine nucleoside phosphorylase, also known as platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PDECGF), that catalyzes the phosphorolysis of thymidine and trifluridine; it degrades trifluridine and drives tumor angiogenesis, and is the molecular target of tipiracil.

edges.note: phosphorolyzes (degrades) trifluridine to the inactive metabolite FTY (5-trifluoromethyluracil), in the gastrointestinal tract, liver, and tumor tissue, causing trifluridine's poor oral bioavailability
high PDECGF/TP expression is overexpressed in colorectal tumor tissue and is a prognostic factor for poor survival; promotes angiogenesis via the breakdown product deoxyribose-1-phosphate

Thymidylate synthase (protein).body:
# Thymidylate synthase (protein)

Thymidylate synthase (TS), encoded by [TYMS](../gene/tyms-gene.md), is a rate-limiting enzyme of pyrimidine de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis that catalyzes the reductive methylation of dUMP to thymidine monophosphate (dTMP), playing a central role in DNA synthesis. It is a classical chemotherapeutic target.

The trifluridine monophosphate (TFT-MP) metabolite of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md) binds covalently to the TS active site (Tyr146) and is a potent reversible inhibitor (Ki 0.38 nM); this is a secondary mechanism of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md), whose major mechanism is incorporation of trifluridine into DNA. TS inhibition depletes dTTP and causes dUMP accumulation.

## Citations
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Thymidylate synthase (protein).description: A rate-limiting enzyme of pyrimidine de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis that catalyzes the reductive methylation of dUMP to dTMP; a central chemotherapeutic target inhibited by the trifluridine monophosphate metabolite of TAS-102.

edges.note: catalyzes the reductive methylation of dUMP to thymidine monophosphate (dTMP) using 5,10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate as cofactor; rate-limiting in pyrimidine de novo synthesis and DNA synthesis

Time to disease flare.body:
# Time to disease flare

Time to disease flare (or time to attack) is a time-to-event endpoint measuring the interval from treatment start to the first treated, adjudicated flare, analyzed by Cox proportional-hazards methods. It was the primary endpoint of both the [MITIGATE trial](../study/mitigate-trial.md) in [IgG4-related disease](../disease/igg4-related-disease.md) (hazard ratio 0.13 for [inebilizumab](../molecule/inebilizumab.md) vs placebo) and the N-MOmentum trial in [neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder](../disease/neuromyelitis-optica-spectrum-disorder.md) (hazard ratio 0.272 in the overall ITT population).

## Citations
- [Inebilizumab for Treatment of IgG4-Related Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541094/) (PMID:39541094)
- [Inebilizumab: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32729016/) (PMID:32729016)
Time to disease flare.description: A time-to-event measure of the interval from treatment start to the first treated, adjudicated disease flare (or attack), analyzed by Cox proportional-hazards methods as the primary endpoint in inebilizumab trials.

Tipiracil.body:
# Tipiracil

Tipiracil (tipiracil hydrochloride, TPI) is a potent, specific 6-methylene-bridged uracil-derived small-molecule inhibitor of [thymidine phosphorylase](../molecule/thymidine-phosphorylase-protein.md) (IC50 35 nM, Ki 17 nM for recombinant human enzyme) and a poor inhibitor of uridine phosphorylase. It is the non-cytotoxic component of [trifluridine/tipiracil](../molecule/trifluridine-tipiracil.md) (TAS-102).

By inhibiting thymidine phosphorylase, tipiracil blocks the rapid first-pass degradation of [trifluridine](../molecule/trifluridine.md), dramatically increasing trifluridine oral exposure — approximately 37-fold for AUC and 22-fold for Cmax in patients with advanced solid tumours, as shown in the phase 1 PK study. Tipiracil also has anti-angiogenic and anti-metastatic activity because thymidine phosphorylase (also known as platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor, PDECGF) drives tumor angiogenesis.

## Citations
- [A phase 1 study of the pharmacokinetics of trifluridine and tipiracil (components of TAS-102) vs trifluridine alone](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28111727/) (PMID:28111727)
- [Therapeutic potential of TAS-102 in the treatment of gastrointestinal malignancies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26557901/) (PMID:26557901)
Tipiracil.description: A potent, specific small-molecule inhibitor of thymidine phosphorylase (a 6-methylene-bridged uracil derivative); the non-cytotoxic component of trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) that blocks degradation of trifluridine to raise its bioavailability.

edges.note: thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor component of the trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) combination, present at a 1:0.5 molar ratio to trifluridine
most potent human thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor identified; IC50 35 nM, Ki 17 nM (recombinant human TP); poor inhibitor of uridine phosphorylase (IC50 >100 uM)
inhibition of thymidine phosphorylase prevents first-pass degradation of trifluridine, increasing trifluridine AUC ~37-fold and Cmax ~22-fold versus trifluridine alone
trifluridine AUC0-last 6618 vs 176 ng*h/mL (ratio of geometric means ~37.55) with trifluridine/tipiracil vs trifluridine alone; AUC0-inf 27-fold higher
trifluridine Cmax 2155 vs 96 ng/mL (geometric means) with trifluridine/tipiracil vs trifluridine alone; ~22-fold increase

Toll-like receptor 7 protein.body:
# Toll-like receptor 7 protein

Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an endosomal pattern-recognition receptor that senses single-stranded RNA and activates innate antiviral immune responses. It is the molecular target of [ruzotolimod](../molecule/ruzotolimod.md), an oral TLR7 agonist selectively activated in the liver and used as an immunomodulator combined with [xalnesiran](../molecule/xalnesiran.md) in [chronic hepatitis B](../disease/chronic-hepatitis-b.md). In the [Piranga trial](../study/piranga-trial.md), influenza-like illness and pyrexia in the ruzotolimod group were noted as biologic markers of on-target TLR7 pharmacodynamic effect.

## Citations
- [Xalnesiran with or without an Immunomodulator in Chronic Hepatitis B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39774313/) (PMID:39774313)
Toll-like receptor 7 protein.description: An endosomal pattern-recognition receptor that senses single-stranded RNA and activates innate antiviral immune responses; the molecular target of the immunomodulator ruzotolimod in chronic hepatitis B.

edges.note: TLR7 agonism (ruzotolimod) aims to restore antiviral immune responses; influenza-like illness and pyrexia are biologic markers of TLR7 activation

Topoisomerase IV.body:
# Topoisomerase IV

Topoisomerase IV is a bacterial type IIA topoisomerase, a heterotetramer of two [ParC](../molecule/parc-protein.md) and two ParE subunits, that decatenates replicated DNA. It is one of the two enzymatic targets of [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md); well-balanced dual inhibition of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV means a single target-site mutation does not substantially reduce gepotidacin susceptibility.

## Citations
- [Gepotidacin (GSK2140944) in vitro activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28483959/) (PMID:28483959)
Topoisomerase IV.description: A bacterial type IIA topoisomerase (heterotetramer of two ParC and two ParE subunits) that decatenates DNA during replication; one of the two enzymatic targets of gepotidacin.

Total plasma kallikrein protein level.body:
# Total plasma kallikrein protein level

The total plasma kallikrein protein level measures the concentration of [plasma kallikrein](../molecule/plasma-kallikrein-protein.md) protein (active kallikrein plus its zymogen precursor prekallikrein). It serves as the pharmacodynamic biomarker of target engagement for KLKB1-directed therapies in [hereditary angioedema](../disease/hereditary-angioedema.md). A prespecified minimum 60% reduction from baseline was the criterion for selecting the [NTLA-2002](../molecule/ntla-2002.md) doses to advance to phase 2; all phase 1 dose levels met this threshold, with reductions of -67% (25 mg), -84% (50 mg), and -95% (75 mg) from baseline through the latest assessment.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing of KLKB1 for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38294975/) (PMID:38294975)
- [CRISPR-Based Therapy for Hereditary Angioedema](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39445704/) (PMID:39445704)

Transaminase increased.body:
# Transaminase increased

Increased transaminases (elevated alanine and/or aspartate aminotransferase) is the most common adverse effect of [fidanacogene elaparvovec](../molecule/fidanacogene-elaparvovec.md). In [BENEGENE-2](../study/benegene-2-trial.md) it occurred in 24 of 45 participants (53%) and was generally mild and asymptomatic; in pooled phase 3 plus phase 1/2a data (n=60) increased transaminases occurred in 47%. It is presumed to indicate a cellular immune response to AAV capsid and is managed with glucocorticoids (62% of BENEGENE-2 participants received glucocorticoids for elevated aminotransferases and/or decreasing [factor IX activity](../biomedicalmeasure/factor-ix-activity.md)).

## Citations
- [Gene Therapy with Fidanacogene Elaparvovec in Adults with Hemophilia B](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39321362/) (PMID:39321362)
- [Fidanacogene Elaparvovec: First Approval](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38472707/) (PMID:38472707)
Transaminase increased.description: Elevation of liver aminotransferase enzymes (alanine aminotransferase and/or aspartate aminotransferase) above normal, the most common adverse effect of fidanacogene elaparvovec, presumed to reflect a cellular immune response to AAV capsid and managed with glucocorticoids.

Transthyretin (protein).body:
# Transthyretin (protein)

Transthyretin (TTR, prealbumin) is a tetrameric serum protein encoded by [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md) and produced mainly by [hepatocytes](../celltype/hepatocyte.md); it transports thyroid hormone and retinol (vitamin A). When the tetramer dissociates and the protein misfolds, it deposits as amyloid fibrils in the myocardium, causing [transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy](../disease/transthyretin-amyloid-cardiomyopathy.md). Therapeutic strategies either stabilize the TTR tetramer or reduce TTR synthesis; [nexiguran ziclumeran](../molecule/nexiguran-ziclumeran.md) lowers circulating transthyretin by gene-editing knockout of TTR.

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Nexiguran Ziclumeran for ATTR Cardiomyopathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555828/) (PMID:39555828)
Transthyretin (protein).description: A tetrameric serum transport protein for thyroid hormone and retinol-binding protein, produced mainly by hepatocytes; when misfolded it deposits as amyloid fibrils in the myocardium, causing transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.

edges.note: deposition of misfolded transthyretin as amyloid fibrils within the myocardium causes ATTR-CM; either tetramer stabilization or reduction of TTR synthesis is therapeutic

Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.body:
# Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy

Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, often fatal infiltrative cardiomyopathy caused by deposition of misfolded [transthyretin](../molecule/transthyretin-protein.md) as amyloid fibrils within the myocardium. It is characterized by progressive decline in cardiac structure and function, deteriorating functional capacity, symptomatic heart failure, frequent hospitalization, and death. The disease arises from wild-type transthyretin (ATTRwt) or from pathogenic [TTR](../gene/ttr-gene.md) variants (ATTRv, e.g. [p.Val142Ile](../variant/ttr-v142i.md)). [Nexiguran ziclumeran](../molecule/nexiguran-ziclumeran.md) was evaluated for this indication in an open-label [phase 1 trial](../study/nexiguran-ziclumeran-phase-1-attr-cm-trial.md).

## Citations
- [CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing with Nexiguran Ziclumeran for ATTR Cardiomyopathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39555828/) (PMID:39555828)
Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.description: A progressive, often fatal infiltrative cardiomyopathy caused by deposition of misfolded transthyretin as amyloid fibrils within the myocardium, presenting as symptomatic heart failure with progressive decline in cardiac structure and function; it arises from wild-type (ATTRwt) or pathogenic variant (ATTRv) transthyretin.

edges.note: cardiac failure was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event (13/36, 36%); reflects underlying progressive heart failure of ATTR-CM

Triazaacenaphthylene antibiotics.body:
# Triazaacenaphthylene antibiotics

The triazaacenaphthylene antibiotics are a novel structural class of antibacterial agents whose first-in-class member is [gepotidacin](../molecule/gepotidacin.md). They are a type of [bacterial topoisomerase inhibitor](bacterial-topoisomerase-inhibitors.md) that inhibits bacterial DNA replication by a unique mechanism, structurally distinct from fluoroquinolones, conferring activity against fluoroquinolone-resistant pathogens.

## Citations
